heading: Radiotherapy in the setting of breast reconstruction: types, techniques, and timing [Ho Lancet Onc '17]
heading_path: Surgery > Radiotherapy in the setting of breast reconstruction: types, techniques, and timing [Ho Lancet Onc '17]
full_text: Timing - Immediate vs delayed: In patients with initial skin involvement, all reconstruction should be delayed until after RT. Immediate: In the past, immediate reconstruction was relatively contraindicated due to potential impact on heart/lung dose (implant-based) and to avoid irradiating flaps (autologous - necrosis). Now, practitioners should be aware that acute reconstruction complications may interrupt PMRT. In 2019, direct to implant (DTI) or delayed autologous (avoiding irradiation of flaps) appear to have the [lowest rates] of complications. There is suggestion of any use of tissue expanders having a higher rate of complications due to a second procedure required, regardless of PMRT use. Consider VMAT for immediate implants if heart dose high (e.g. IM coverage) [Dumane Rad Onc '18]: May be useful in pts with implant constructions receiving RNI with DIBH. Consider reconstruction if prior radiation to the breast. Delayed: Reconstruction offered 6-12 mo after RT. Modern series demonstrate more complications with delayed reconstruction. Timing of autologous after PMRT: One study demonstrated less complications with > 12 mo delay [Baumann PRCS '11], while another suggests no difference if ± 6 mo after PMRT [Momoh '12]. Delayed-immediate with tissue expander placement and partial inflation initially. In 2019, DTI (immediate) or delayed autologous appear to have the [lowest rates] of complications. Tissue expanders are typically partially inflated initially, then over-inflated 2w after RT. Timing of Implant exchange after RT: One study suggests ≥ 6 mo delay adequate: Implant failures for exchange ± 6 mo of 8→ 22% [Peled PRSJ '12]. This strategy avoids RT to an autologous flap. Estimated rate of implant failure is no different if implant placed before or after RT [Santosa '16]. Permanent implant after RT may be best, as capsulotomy may be performed at time of exchange. Implants vs. autologous: Implant reconstruction for skinnier or athletic women who don't wish for tissue transfer. In 2019, DTI (immediate) or delayed autologous appear to have the [lowest rates] of complications. Autologous reconstruction should be performed after RT (Per NCCN). TRAM irradiation with ~30% requiring new flap due to necrosis [Tran PRCS '01] DIEP irradiation with more fat necrosis, fibrosis, and flap contracture [Rogers PRCS '02] Fat necrosis for muscle sparing TRAM vs. DIEP of 9→ 23% [Garvey PRCS '14] Autologous conclusions: Avoid direct irradiation of the flap as opposed to modifying flap design; delay reconstruction 3-6 mo after RT is complete. Newer data suggests overall complication rates of ~26% regardless of timing relative to PMRT [Billig PRS '17] including DIEP reconstruction [Taghizadeh JPRAS '15]. Most recently, Cleveland clinic data has also suggested no difference in reconstruction failure with delayed vs. immediate autologous reconstruction. RoR Reconstruction complications See the [Toxicity] section and impact of PMRT on reconstruction complications. The use of a [Boost] in PMRT does not appear to affect local control, even in the higher risk groups of LVSI. Clinical Pearl: Surgical Margins Lumpectomy Margins for IDC/DCIS: Current Recommendations, Their Implications & Impact [Schnitt, Moran, Giuliano JCO '20] DCIS: SM < 1mm does not mandate re-excision. 2 mm is standard for BCT. 3 mm for omission of RT. 1 cm previously. IDC: No tumor on Ink! ASTRO-SSO Margin Consensus for stage I-II invasive breast cancer [Moran IJROBP '14]: No tumor on ink! See the [Treatment Planning] section for more. SM+ with LR RR 2.4 not nullified by boost, systemic therapy, or favorable biology [Houssami ASO '14]. At 6.5y of MFU, IBTR was only 5.3% for stage I-II breast cancer. Wider margins do not significantly improve LC. Time to stop the routine practice of margins more widely clear than tumor on ink. Still, consider re-excision for multiple risk factors (i.e. young age, mult SM close, EIC) [Jagsi IJROBP '14]. Does not apply to: pure DCIS, NAC, APBI.

heading: Margins
full_text: See the Surgical Margins Summary Box above and [Omission of RT] in the DCIS section for more. Lumpectomy Margins for IDC/DCIS: Current Recommendations, Their Implications & Impact [Schnitt, Moran, Giuliano JCO '20] ASCO-SSO-ASTRO Guideline: DCIS Margins for BCS with WBRT August 15, 2016 Use of a 2 mm margin is standard for DCIS treated with WBRT and is associated with low rates of IBTR with the potential to decrease re-excision rates, improve cosmetic outcomes, and decrease health care costs. Surgical margins < 2 mm does not mandate re-excision. If pure DCIS with < 2 mm SM, consider post-excision MMA for residual calcifications, extent of DCIS in proximity to margin, location of margin, cosmetic impact of re-excision, life expectancy. Notable exception: no re-excision if < 1 mm at fibroglandular border of breast (skin/chest wall). ASCO Guideline: Invasive Breast Cancer Margins for BCS with WBRT in Stage I and II April 7, 2014 Emphasis placed on the use of post-lumpectomy mammograms for cases with microcalcifications. There is no evidence that wider margins in younger women leads to less IBTR. Tumor on ink is associated with at ≥ 2x increased IBTR, not nullified by boost, systemic tx or favorable biology. The Diminishing Impact of Margin Definitions and Width on LR following BCT for early IBC [Shah ASO '20]. What about focal positive margins after BCS? Most would recommend re-excision, which may diminish the 10y relapse rate down to baseline. An analysis of 1,752 pts w 193 SM+ demonstrated 5y LR substantially greater for < 40y, around the same for > 40y. What about focal positive margins for T1-2N0 after MRM? British Columbia retro of 2,570 women w 94 SM+. About half (41) rec'd PMRT. Trend towards improvement in pts ≤ 50, T2, G3, and LVSI. In patients without these features, there was no LR w/o PMRT. LR RF for BCT: SM+, molecular subtype (Her2 or basal), young age (less strong). Note: EIC is not important as long as negative margins are obtained. LR decreased during BCT by boost, chemo, or endocrine.

heading: Subtypes / Pathology
full_text: Pathology Noninvasive: DCIS (85%), LCIS (15%), Paget's (0.5-5%). DCIS ~20-25% of all breast malignancies. 5x more common than LCIS. LCIS and DCIS may be hard to tell from ADH or invasive carcinomas with early invasion - Review path! Unlike DCIS, IDC increases risk of having IDC in contra breast by 10-15%. Invasive: Ductal (65-80%), Lobular (10-15%), Mucinous (2%), Tubular (1-2%), Medullary (5%). Papillary, inflammatory, secretory, adenoid cystic, glandular (adenoid), cystic (cylindromatous), metaplastic. Rare favorable: tubular, medullary (colloid, not atypical), mucinous, papillary. Bad = micropapillary. Ductal forms nests, Lobular tends to form in a single file pattern. Mucinous is less prone to metastases. Tubular is almost always ER(+)HER2(-). If tubular is ER(-) and/or HER2(+), review path! Medullary carcinoma (atypical, not colloid): G3, LVSI, pushing tumor border, syncytial growth pattern. Previously though lower potential for mets. Interobserver variance present, do not withhold adjuvant systemic therapy - Review path! Subtypes Luminal A: HER2 negative. Luminal B: Can be HER2 negative with Ki-67 > 15%. Lymph node involvement for luminal A / B of 11→ 51% [Inic CNIO '14]. Triple negative (~10%): Still candidates for BCT and wider margins not necessary. HER2 positive (~15%) StatPearls: Mucinous Breast Cancer Last update: 11/18/2019. StatPearls: Tubular Breast Carcinoma Last update: 9/26/2019. StatPearls: Medullary Breast Carcinoma Last update: 11/26/2019. StatPearls: Phyllodes Tumor of the Breast (Cystosarcoma) Last update:  12/27/19 StatPearls: Male Breast Cancer Last update: 11/15/2019.ASCO Guideline: Management of Male Breast Cancer Last update: 2/14/2020. Scarff-Bloom-Richardson system (Elston-Ellis modification): Grade: Glandular/tubular differentiation, nuclear pleomorphism, mitotic count. Each scored 1-3. Grade 1: 3-5. Grade 2: 6-7. Grade 3: 8-9. Lowery [BCRT '12]: Meta. 12k patients.Difference in LRR between subtypes is not as pronounced in the TM setting! Luminal subtypes with LRR RR ~0.35 vs. HER2/neu or TN after BCT Luminal subtypes with ~0.65 RR vs. HER2/neu or TN after MRM. Difference in LRR not as pronounced in the TM setting! Male breast cancer [Giordano NEJM '18]: More likely ER+, BRCA2. See StatPearls and ASCO Guidelines above. Treatment: MRM→ Chemo/RT if indicated→ Tamox x5y. Don't use anastrozole due to incomplete estradiol suppression from feedback loops. Phyllodes tumors aka cystosarcoma phyllodes [Chaney Cancer '00, Barrio ASO '07]. See the StatPearls above. Surgical margins and adjuvant therapy in Phyllodes of the breast [Neron ASO '20] Rapidly growing fibroadenoma. Rare. Contain stromal and epithelial elements. Benign, borderline, and malignant subtypes (no uniform agreement). Stromal overgrowth, size ≥ 7 cm, proliferation > 10/10 HPF, infiltrative borders and necrosis may predict distant metastasis. Rare tumors with leaf-like, lobulated appearance on microscopic sections. Margins most important (1 cm), although some now say 3 mm [Neron]. Axillary eval not necessary in cN0. No role for hormones even if ER/PR+. RT is a 2B recommendation. Recommend RT for > 2 cm removed with lumpectomy and >10 cm removed with mastectomy [1]. Axillary breast cancer 1% have axillary metastasis with no breast primary. MRI can identify primary breast lesions in 70% of patients. One strategy: ALND→ chemo→ RT. Reimage before RT to see if calcs develop at primary site. May do ALND + WBRT. Paget’s Disease: Crusting/eczematous change of nipple or areolar complex. Associated with IDC ~90% of the time if there is a palpable mass. MRI can be useful after a full thickness punch biopsy of nipple. ~50% of women will have a palpable mass. 15% do not have associated abnormalities in imaging. 25% with associated DCIS. >80% HER2+. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram.

heading: HR+
full_text: Use endocrine therapy if ER+ AND tumor > 0.5 cm (consider for tumors ≤ 0.5 cm). Supplementation with 1200 mg calcium and 800 IU Vit D. ER and PR should be considered positive if at least 1% positive tumor nuclei [ASCO Guidelines '20]. As of 2020, there is a new category of "Low Positive" for 1-10% positivity. ER positive breast cancer can have extremely late recurrences, even 20 years out! RoR When stopping tamoxifen at 5y for T1N0 disease, there is still at least a 10% chance of DM at 20 years! This suggests that certain patients should be selected for extended therapy (e.g. greater than 5y of hormone therapy) [Pan NEJM '17]. 5 years of tamoxifen has the most significant reduction in BCM not only during years 0-4, but also years 5-9 and 10-14 (i.e., after discontinuation). Relative risk of recurrence is not significant after 10 years, however. Tamoxifen is effective regardless of whether or not chemotherapy has been given. Overall mortality was little affected, despite small absolute increases in thromboembolic or uterine cancer mortality (both in women older than 55y of age) [EBCTCG]. For early stage, ER+ node negative disease, 9y DM is only 5% for women < 50 years with Oncotype recurrence score 11-25 if clinical low risk. Clinical low risk: G1 ≤ 3 cm, G2 ≤ 2 cm, G3 ≤ 1 cm (all add up to 4). These patients may not require extended hormone therapy, for example, but should be offered given young age if able to tolerate [Sparano NEJM '19]. Luminal A disease carries a low but persistent risk of DM greater than 15y after treatment, while Luminal B appears to have a much higher early risk of distant failure that confers a very short-term benefit to tamoxifen treated patients [Yu JAMA Onc '19]. SERMs may be used for breast cancer prophylaxis in high risk populations (e.g., 5y projected risk of breast cancer ≥ 1.66% or women with LCIS) [2019 USPSTF Recommendation]. Deliver adjuvant endocrine treatment if node positive, including an AI, for up to 10 years. Node negative patients should consider extended therapy for up to 10 years, but should not be routinely offered extended therapy (e.g. greater than 5 years). Extended therapy carries ongoing risks and side effects which should be weighed against potential absolute benefit of extended therapy greater than 5 years [ASCO Guideline]. For metastatic disease, sequential hormones are preferred unless in cases of immediately life-threatening disease. Ovarian suppression or ablation should be considered in premenopausal women. Postmenopausal women favor AIs over endocrine therapy, with or without CDK 4/6 inhibitors (e.g. palbociclib). Fulvestrant should be administered as second line therapy, and may be given with palbociclib. Mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitor everolimus may be administered with exemestane whose disease progresses while receiving non-steroidal AIs. For patients with TPBC, HER2 along with AI can be effective for those who are not chemo candidates [ASCO Guideline]. Clinicopathological characteristics and BCSS for single HR+ breast cancer [Li JAMA Netw Open '20]: SEER.TBLQS: The more hormone receptor-positivity the better, meaning those with ER(+)PR(-) and especially ER(-)/PR(+) breast cancers may be deserving of their own more aggressive treatment algorithms. 823,399 pts. 1990-2015. MFU 6y. ER/PR(+) in 67%, ER(+)/PR(-) in 12%, ER(-)/PR(+) in 2%, ER/PR(-) in 19%. MVA demonstrated HR(+) discordance with lower BCSS than HR(+). BCSS HR for isolated ER(+) / PR(+) of 1.4→ 1.6. Isolated PR(+) does worse. MonarchE (2017-2019) [Johnston JCO '20, '22]: Endo ± adjuvant abemaciclib x2y (CDK4/6i). TBL QS: Two years of adjuvant abemaciclib improves disease-free survival by 3.5% among women with node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. 5,637 patients. High-risk ER+, HER2-. N2 or N1 and one of T3, G3, or Ki-67 ≥ 20%. Primary endpoint iDFS. MFU 42 mo. Patients must have received surgery, RT (as indicated), and/or adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Over 95% of patients received RT and chemotherapy, while just over 2/3 received AI as endo therapy. 2y iDFS 89→ 92%. 4y iDFS 79→ 86%. 5y OM ~6%. PALLAS (2015-2018) [Mayer Lanc Onc '21, Gnant JCO '21]: Endocrine therapy ± Palbociclib. At interim analysis, addition of 2y of palbociclib to adjuvant endocrine therapy did not improve iDFS. 5,761 pts. Stage II-III HR+, HER2- BC. MFU 31 mo. 3y iDFS ~88%. 4y iDFS ~84% G3-4 neutropenia of 0.3→ 61%, leucopenia 2→ 30%, fatigue 0.3→ 2.0%. Serious AE 8→ 12%. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram. ASCO Guideline: Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 Testing in Breast Cancer May 30, 2018 Roughly speaking, if HER2 is 2+ on IHC, copy number > 6 signals/nucleus is positive regardless if HER2/CEP17 is ± 2.0. IHC 2+ is IBC with weak to moderate complete membrane staining in > 10% of tumor cells [Wolff JCO '13]. If initially negative, a new HER2 test may be ordered on the excision specimen. Dual-probe (control probe) ISH assay: Concomitant IHC review required for dual-probe ISH groups 2-4. ISH group 2: HER2/CEP17 ≥ 2.0, average HER2 copy number < 4.0 signals/cell. Evidence is limited in efficacy of HER2 therapy in this group. If the IHC is not 3+, then it is recommended HER2 be considered negative due to the low HER2 copy number. ISH group 3: HER2/CEP17 < 2.0, average HER2 copy number > 6.0 signals/cell. ISH group 4: HER2/CEP17 < 2.0, average HER2 copy number ≥ 4 and < 6.0 signals/cell. For all groups if IHC 2+, have a second pathologist review who is blinded to the ISH results. If second pathology review equivocal, ISH group 2 and 4 are negative, while ISH group 3 is positive (due to high copy number > 6) ASCO Guideline: Systemic Tx for Pts w Advanced HER2+ Breast Cancer May 31, 2022 RoR ASCO Guideline Update: Systemic Tx for Advanced HER2+ Breast Cancer [Giordano JCO '22]. ASCO Guideline: Recommendations on Dz Mgmt for Pts w Advanced HER2+ BrCa and Brain Mets May 31, 2022 RoR Click on RoR for bullet point summaries of these articles. Then, click on RoR to return to this section. ASCO Guidelines Update: Management of Advanced HER2+ BrCa and Brain Mets [Ramakrishna JCO '22].

heading: HER2-neu
full_text: See the HER2/neu Summary Box above. Commonly false positive or false negative. Equivocal result: Reflex FISH testing on same specimen or repeat tests if new specimen available. Generally speaking, if IHC 2+, then HER2+ if HER2/CEP17 ≥ 2.0 or copy number > 6 signals/nucleus. 3% of women treated with trastuzumab can develop cardiotoxicity. This risk increases if the patient also received doxorubicin. AC + trastuzumab has 27% frequency of significant cardiac dysfunction. Lifetime dose of adriamycin = 450 mg. With neoadjuvant chemo, total pCR 50% [TRYPHAENA] (compared to ~30% for ER+/HER2-). For residual disease after NAC, give T-DM1 adjuvantly as opposed to trastuzumab for DFS benefit [KATHERINE]. HER2(+) is considered a weak prognostic indicator in DCIS [NSABP B-43]. With adjuvant chemo, there may be no benefit in adding Pertuzumab to Trastuzumab for node negative disease QS [APHINITY Piccart JCO '21].

heading: HER2 low expression
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > HER2-neu > HER2 low expression
full_text: Evolving data as of 2022. TBL QS: "HER2-low expression is positively associated with ER expression and likewise is associated with better prognosis than HER2-0 tumors" [Tarantino JAMA Onc '22]. [DESTINY-Breast 04] defined Low expression of HER2 defined as a score of 1+ on IHC or 2+ with negative FISH. Patients with HER2 IHC 1+ or 2+ and ISH-negative metastatic breast cancer who have received at least one prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, and if receptor-positive are refractory to endocrine therapy, should be offered treatment with trastuzumab deruxtecan [ASCO Rapid Recommendation Update Moy JCO '22] As of September of 2022, there is no evidence to support HER2 directed therapy in non-metastatic HER2 low expression patients. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram.

heading: Topoisomerase I inhibitors
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > HER2-neu > Topoisomerase I inhibitors
full_text: For metastatic disease, see the [Topoisomerase I inhibitors] section in the [metastatic breast cancer] section. There may not be a benefit in the addition of a boost in patients who receive trastuzumab (controversial). RoR Types of Anti-HER2 therapy Trastuzumab targets subdomain IV of HER2. Don't give concurrently with Adriamycin but can be given with RT. Add pertuzumab with pCR ~50-60%! Pertuzumab targets HER2 to inhibit dimerization. Pertuzumab significantly improves PFS compared to trastuzumab + docetaxel alone. Lapatinib interrupts HER2/neu and EGFR pathways. Lapatinib + capecitabine demonstrates around 30% CNS ORR for heavily pretreated [NALA trial]. Pyrotinib is an irreversible pan-ErbB inhibitor. It appears to nearly double PFS (OS still maturing) compared to lapatinib in combination with capecitabine for patients with HER2+ metastatic breast cancer at the cost of nearly quadrupled G3+ diarrhea QS [PHOEBE Xu ASCO ‘20, Lanc Onc '21] Neratinib is an irreversible pan-HER2 and erbB1/4 inhibitor. Neratinib + capecitabine demonstrated 50% of pts with CNS ORR in the treatment naive setting, although not durable [TBCRC 022]. The [NALA trial] demonstrated ~30% CNS ORR for heavily pretreated. Tucatinib targets HER2. It [improves PFS and OS] in pts with brain mets who have progressed on HP and T-DM1. T-DM1 is a drug conjugate (trastuzumab + microtubule inhib agent DM1, a derivative of maytansine). Now preferred for residual disease after NAC [KATHERINE]. There is no apparent benefit for use in NAC as compared to carboplatin. Common Regimens AC→ TH ± pertuzumab. AC: Adriamycin 60 + cyclo 600 q2/3w x4c→ Paclitaxel 175 q3w x4c or 80 q1w x12c. Trastuzumab 4 mg/kg loading→ 2 mg/kg q1w concurrent with paclitaxel→ trast mono (6 mg/kg q3w) x1y. Cardiac monitoring at baseline and 3, 6, 9 mo. TCH ± pertuzumab. Taxotere 75, Carbo AUC 6, H 8→ 6, Pertuzumab 840→ 420 q3w up to 18c (6c given neoadjuvantly). TCHP (carboplatin) is the most common contemporary NAC for HER2+ breast cancer [KRISTINE]. Analysis of NSABP B-31 and N9831 [Perez JCO '11, '14]: AC→ T ± Herceptin.See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. Around 1% OS benefit per year when adding herceptin to adjuvant paclitaxel after AC chemotherapy. 4045 pts with HER2(+) operable breast cancer. MFU 8y. NSABP B-31: AC→ T q3w ± Herceptin→ Herceptin x1y. NCCTG N9831: AC→ T q1w vs. AC→ T→ H vs. AC→ T+H→ H. N+ or N- , ≥ T1b if ER-, ≥ T1c if ER+. 10y OS 75→ 84% (HR 0.63). 10y DFS 62→ 74% (HR 0.60). NAC in HER2+ There appears to be no benefit with the addition of T-DM1 to herceptin/perjeta for HER2+ breast cancer. Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg loading→ 6 mg/kg q3w x10c, then given for a year total after surgery and RT (if indicated).

heading: NAC in HER2+
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > HER2-neu > NAC in HER2+
full_text: See more in the [neoadjuvant chemotherapy] section. NeoSphere [Gianni Lanc Onc '16]: Phase II. TP vs. HP vs. TH vs. THP. Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab and docetaxel only had 23% total pCR. 417 pts. 2007-2009. Locally advanced, inflammatory or early stage breast cancer treated with NAC. Trastuzumab (H): 8 loading, 6 mg/kg q2w Docetaxel (T): 75 q3w, increasing to 100 from cycle 2 if tolerated Pertuzumab (P): 840 loading, then 420 q2w. All patients received FEC after surgery and trastuzumab 6 mg/kg q3w x1 year. 5y PFS 73→ 73→ 81→ 86%. 5y PFS for ± pCR of 76→ 85%. NOAH [Gianni Lancet '10, '14]: Neo chemo ± trastuzumab. Give trastuzumab preop if ≥ T2, N+, HER2+ early stage breast cancer. 235 pts with LABC or IBC. Chemo: AT→ T q3w x4c with CMF d1,8 q4w x3c. Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg loading→ 6 mg/kg q3w x10c, then given for a year total. 3y EFS 56→ 71%. 5y EFS 43→ 58%. Breast pCR 22→ 43%, total pCR 19→ 38%. CALGB 40601 [Carey JCO '16, Fernandez-Martinez JCO '20]: TL vs. TH vs. THL. pCR with dual HER2 targeted therapy was not significantly higher than single HER2 targeting. 305 pts with stage II-III HER2 positive breast cancer. Total pCR ~27→ 44→ 52%. Post-treatment residual disease was largely luminal A (69%). pCR correlated with RFS in the 2020 publication. TRYPHAENA [Schneeweiss Ann Onc '13, EJC '18]: H/P: FEC+H/P x3c→ THP x3c, FEC x3c→ THP x3c, TCH/P x6c. Phase II. 256 pts. Operable, HER2+ LABC or IBC 1:1:1 as above. T = Docetaxel. Only 3% reported left ventricular cardiac dysfunction. pCR in breast 57-66%. Total pCR 43→ 52%. Pooled TRYPHAENA and NeoSphere [Saifi RTO '23]: Her-2 directed therapy→ MRM ± PMRT. HER2+ BC patients who achieve ypN0 after primary systemic therapy have excellent LRC which supports de-escalation of PMRT. 312 cN+ patients. ypN0 (55%), ypN+ (45%). 5y LRRFS in ypN0 of ~97%. 5y LRRFS in ypN+ of ~82→ 89% (p=0.17). 5y LRRFS in ypN1 of ~85→ 89% (p=0.60). 5y LRRFS in ypN2 of 75→ 92% (p=0.019). On MVA, clinical nodal disease at diagnosis and ypN0 were significantly associated with LRR. KRISTINE [Hurvitz JCO '19]: TCH-P vs. T-DM1 + Pertuzumab.TBLQS: Womp womp, chemo-free neoadjuvant T-DM1 + pertuzumab has a lower response rate and higher risk of pre-op progression than standard TCHP. 444 pts. HER2+ stage II-III. MFU 37 mo. Chemo: Docetaxel, Carboplatin, Trastuzumab + Pertuzumab q3w x6c neoadjuvantly, up to 12c adjuvant. This is the most common contemporary neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimen for HER2+ breast cancer.. pCR 56→ 44%. G3+ 68→ 32%, AEs leading to treatment discontinuation 18→ 4%. There were more progression rates prior to surgery with T-DM1+P. Neo-PATH (2019-2020) [Ahn JAMA Onc '22]: Phase II. Pertuzumab, Atezolizumab, Docetaxel and trastuzumab. 67 women with stage II-III HER2+ breast cancer (primary tumor size > 2 cm or pathologically confirmed LN+ cancer without distant metastases). HR+ in 48%. pCR in 61%. pCR for HR- / HR+ of 77→ 44%. pCR for PD-L1 ± of 53→ 100%. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram. TRAIN-2 QS [van der Voort ASCO ‘20, JAMA Onc '21]: {(FEC x3c→ CarboT x6c) vs. CarboT x9c} + HP. Carboplatin and Paclitaxel appear to be very promising for HER2 positive breast cancer. There appears to be no benefit in anthracycline-based chemotherapy for HER2 positive breast cancer in the setting of TCHP. 438 patients. Stage II-III HER2 positive breast cancer. MFU 4y. FEC-PC: 5-FU 500, epirubicin 90, CPM 500 x3c→ Paclitaxel 80, Carbo AUC 6 d1,8 x6c. Both groups received trastuzumab (6 mg/kg; loading dose 8) and pertuzumab (420; loading 840) q3w. 3y EFS ~93%. 3y OS ~98%. LVEF decline ≥ 10% of 8→ 3%. Adjuvant Chemo for HER+ breast cancer Give adjuvant T-DM1 if residual disease after NAC. Compare to [CREATE-X] for HER2(-) or TNBC. Giving 6 vs. 12 months of adjuvant trastuzumab depends on who you ask (see conflicting trials below). For now, 1 year is considered "standard" by many med oncs.

heading: Adjuvant Systemic Therapy for HER2(+) breast cancer
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > HER2-neu > Adjuvant Systemic Therapy for HER2(+) breast cancer
full_text: Give adjuvant T-DM1 instead of Trastuzumab if there is residual disease after NAC for 10% 3y DFS benefit [KATHERINE]. Compare to [CREATE-X] for HER2(-) disease, which provides 5-10% 5y OS advantage (10% for TNBC). HERA BIG [Cameron Lancet '17, Bachir IJROBP '22]: Observation vs. trastuzumab x1y vs. 2y.Two years of trastuzumab appears to offer no additional benefit. TBL QS: Radiation does not appear to affect cardiac function or the risk cardiovascular events in women receiving trastuzumab. Breast RT does not affect LVEF whether right or left sided QS [Bachir IJROBP '22]. Even T1-2N1 HER2(+) receiving targeted therapy [appears to benefit] from PMRT. 5,102 pts. Advanced breast cancer. 2001-2005. MFU 11y. Trastuzumab 8 loading, then 6 q3w x1-2y. 10y DFS 63→ 69→ 69%. Secondary cardiac endpoints 1→ 4→ 7%. ATEMPT [Bellon IJROBP '22]: Adjuvant T-DM1 vs. Paclitaxel and Trastuzumab. The ATEMPT trial evaluated whether adjuvant T-DM1 alone had less toxicity than paclitaxel and trastuzumab for women with stage 1, node-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer. It didn’t, but this secondary analysis explored whether T-DM1 concurrent with adjuvant RT increased toxicity compared to RT concurrent with trastuzumab. TBL QS: Toxicity with concurrent T-DM1 appears comparable to that of trastuzumab. Stage I, node negative HER2-positive breast cancer. G2+ skin toxicity 34→ 23%. Pneumonitis ˜1%. Skin toxicity for conventional / hypofractionation of 45→ 18%. PERSEPHONE [Earl Lancet '19]: Non-inferiority. Trastuzumab 12 vs. 6 mo.TBLQS: Among women with fairly early and mostly ER(+) HER2(+) breast cancer receiving mostly anthracycline-based chemo, 6 was non-inferior to 12 month of adjuvant trastuzumab. 4,099 pts. HER2+ early breast cancer with clear indication for chemo. 30% N1. 70% ER+. MFU 5y. Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg loading→ 6 mg/kg q3w x10c, then given for a six mo - 1 year total. Roughly 90% of chemo regimens included an anthracycline, with heterogeneous outcomes for taxanes. TCH ± P (docetaxel, carboplatin, herceptin) is a more common contemporary regimen. 4y DFS ~90%. Serious AE 24→ 19%, stopping early due to cardiotoxicity 8→ 3%. PHARE [Pivot Lancet '19]: Non-inferiority. Adjuvant Trastuzumab 12 vs. 6 mo.This trial had a different approach to non-inferiority margins, and RT did not appear in the heterogeneity analysis.TBLQS: Among women with fairly early, and mostly ER(+) HER2(+) breast cancer receiving anthracycline-based chemo, 6 months of adjuvant trastuzumab was not non-inferior to 12 months. 3400 pts. HER2+ early breast cancer. 30% N1. 60% ER+. MFU 7.5y. HR for DFS 1.08 (compared to 1.07 in PERSEPHONE), but non-inferiority was not met. ShortHER [Conte JCO '23]: Phase III noninferiority. Trastuzumab x9w vs. 1 year. 1,254 patients with node positive HER2+ breast cancer, or node negative with at least one additional risk factor: > 2 cm primary, G3, LVSI, Ki-67 > 20%, age <35y, or HR- (ER and PR < 10%). MFU 9y. 10y DFS ~77%. 10y OS ~88%. Numerically, differences for patients at low or intermediate risk (N0/N1-3) is negligible, while N4+ patients have a clear benefit with 1y trastuzumab. Late Relapses in HER2+ receiving adjuvant Trastuzumab [Chumsri JCO '19]: AC→ T ± Herceptin.For HR+, HER2- patients, there is a suggestion of > 50% of recurrences occurring after 5 years [Pan NEJM '17]. In contrast, HR- breast cancer has a higher risk of recurrence in the first few years, which declines after 5 years. The benefit of adjuvant trastuzumab persists for a long time. A distinct pattern of recurrence was observed between HR+ and HR- HER2+ disease but with a similar degree of benefit from adjuvant trastuzumab. Risk of recurrence in years 5-10 in HR+ HER2+ breast cancer is low, particularly in patients with N0 or N1 disease. 3,177 pts from NSABP B-31 and N9831. Median 50y. 30% N2, 15% N3. MFU 8y. RFS for HR+ breast cancer of 0.65 during the first 5 years. 5y RFS for HR+ breast cancer of 11→ 17%. There was no significant difference in RFS based on HR status during years 5-10. Recurrence at 5-10y for N0 / N1 of 3.2→ 6.4%. Trastuzumab improved benefit in both HR+ and HR- breast cancers. Median time to recurrence or death 2.5 years. There was a low risk of recurrence in years 5-10 among patients with HR+ HER2+ breast cancer. 5-10y PFS for HR+ HER2+ with N0 / N1 of 3.2→ 6.4%. Previous reports suggest 11→ 19%. Intrinsic subtypes and outcomes Intrinsic subtypes: HER2 enriched (77%), Lum B (10%), Lum A (8%), Basal-like (5%). 10y RFS for basal / HER2 enriched / Lum B / Lum A of 64→ 69→ 73→ 77%. 10y RFS for basal / HER2 enriched / Lum B / Lum A receiving trastuzumab of 74→ 77→ 82→ 90%. 10y RFS for N0 HER2 enriched of 89%. APT Study [Tolaney NEJM '15, JCO '19]: Paclitaxel + Trastuzumab x12w→ 9 mo maintenance Trastuzumab. Treatment with adjuvant paclitaxel and trastuzumab was associated with decreased risk of early recurrence by 2%. 406 pts. HER2+ ≤ 3 cm. N0 or Nmic. MFU 7y. Very few RT details available. Chemo: Paclitaxel 80 q1w x12c. Trastuzumab 4 loading→ 2 q1w. Maintenance could be 6 q3w. 3y DFS 99%. 7y DFS 93%. Among 12 relapses, 2 were due to distant metastasis. G3+ neuropathy at least one episode in 3.2% (n=13). Symptomatic CHF 0.5% (n=2), both of whom had normalization of LV EF after discontinuation of trastuzumab. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram. Neoadjuvant PARPi vs. Neoadjuvant carboplatin for TNBC PARP inhibitors are a good treatment for BRCA mutant breast cancers, so how do they do with TNBC at large? PARPi requires BRCA mutation for synergistic effect. Without faulty DS-DNA repair such as in the setting of a BRCA mutation, then PARPi is not effective in and of itself. Recall: 20% of TNBC have BRCA mutations. Carboplatin appears to nearly double pCR [BrighTNess]. For now, Carboplatin is used as opposed to PARPi for NAC in TNBC. Perhaps there may be a benefit of PARPi in the BRCA subset. These trials need to be repeated now that we know BRCA mutations are required for PARPi to be effective.

heading: Triple Negative Breast Cancer
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > Triple Negative Breast Cancer
full_text: See the Neoadjuvant PARPi vs. Neoadjuvant Carboplatin Summary Box above. Multi-D Management of TNBC with Extensive Regional Nodal Involvement [Smith, Goetz and Boughey JCO '20]. Accounts for around 12% of breast cancers in the USA. TNBC appears to have roughly the same rate of [brain mets] as HER2(+) HR(-) breast cancer. With neoadjuvant chemo, total pCR is 60% when adding carboplatin [BrighTNess] (compared to ~30% for other histologies). For residual disease after NAC, give capecitabine for OS benefit [CREATE-X]. If no NAC, add Capecitabine to Docetaxel, Cyclophosphamide and epirubicin for 5% DFS5 benefit [CBCSG010 Li JCO '20] Adjuvant capecitabine appears to be important, improving 5y DFS by 10% [SYSUCC-001 Wang ASCO ‘20, JAMA '20] TBL QS: Without the biologic stress test of neoadjuvant chemo, all-comers who receive upfront surgery for triple-negative breast cancer may benefit from the addition of maintenance capecitabine. ASCO Rapid Recommendation Update: Use of ICI in High-Risk, Node negative TNBC [Korde JCO '22] See ASCO neoadjuvant therapy guidelines from 2021. RoR Results from [KEYNOTE 522] demonstrate an EFS benefit and potential OS benefit with the addition of Pembro to chemotherapy. Patients with cT1cN1-2 or T2-4N0 (stage II or III) TNBC are recommended to receive Pembro (200 mg once q3w or 400 mg once q6w) in combination with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab after surgery. Adjuvant pembrolizumab may be given either concurrent with or after completion of RT. Given that irAEs associated with pembrolizumab therapy can be severe and permanent, careful screening for and management of common toxicities are required. Please see the [ASCO guideline for management of irAEs] for more details.

heading: PARPi, Carboplatin and Immunotherapy
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > Triple Negative Breast Cancer > PARPi, Carboplatin and Immunotherapy
full_text: See the Neoadjuvant PARPi vs. Neoadjuvant Carboplatin Summary Box above. I-SPY 2 [Rugo NEJM '16]: Phase II. Veliparib (PARPi) with carboplatin.Remember, back in 2016, the carbo/veliparib combo was one of the big winners of the ISPY2 trial by almost doubling pathologic complete response (pCR) rate from 26% to 51%. See [BrighTNess] trial below. 72 patients. Stage II-III breast cancer, ≥ 2.5 cm. HER2 status, HR and 70 gene assay performed. Veliparib and carboplatin should be considered for HER2- tumors. TNBC with pCR of 51%. I-SPY 2 (2015-2016) [Nanda JAMA Onc '20]: Phase II. T→ AC ± Pembro. TBL QS: Even after investigational therapies like ICI, a pCR portends excellent overall prognosis for all types of breast cancer. 250 pts. Stage II-III BrCa. Primary endpoint pCR. Secondary endpoint RCB, EFS, DFS. MFU 3y. For HR(+)/HER2(-), pCR 13→ 30% For TNBC, pCR 22→ 60%. 3y EFS 93% for patients who achieved pCR. I-SPY 2 Residual Cancer Burden (RCB) [Symmans JAMA Onc '21]: T→ AC ± ten investigational agents.TBL QS: “Residual cancer burden as a continuous response measure exhibits favorable attributes for neoadjuvant trials in breast cancer, providing additional information beyond pathologic complete response rate and pretreatment disease characteristics.” See patient level data suggesting RCB is prognostic across all subgroups. RoR 938 women with breast tumors > 2.5 cm with high risk receptor status (i.e., ER < 5% or HER2+) and/or high-risk genomic scores (via Mammaprint) were randomly assigned to NAC with paclitaxel or one of ten investigational agents x12 weeks then cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin x12 weeks followed by surgery. EFS was significantly worse with each increase in RCB at time of surgery [Online calculator]. This was the case across every subtype, even ER+/HER2- where there was a HR 1.75 for recurrence or death with each increase in RCB class (this subtype was less likely to achieve complete (class 0) or near complete (class I) responses. Figures 1 and 2 provide really nice visuals at a glance for the outcomes presented here. ISPY-2 Clipping the Positive LN [Switalla ASO '24]: Clip placement in the positive LN before NAC is increasingly common. There is significant association between clip placement and omission of ALND, even among patients with pN+ disease. Retrospective analysis of cN+ ISPY-2 patients undergoing axillary surgery after NAC. Among 801 cN+ patients, 20% (n=161) had pre-NAC clip placement in the positive node. The proportion of patients who were cN+ with clipped node increased from 2.4→ 36.2% between 2011-2021. Multivariable logistic regression showed nodal clipping was independently associated with higher odds of SLN-only surgery (OR 4.3, 95CI 2.8-6.8), which was also true among patients with residual pN+ disease. Completion ALND did not differ based on clip retrieval success. No significant differences in EFS were observed in those with or without clip placement, both with or without successful clip retrieval (HR 0.85, 95CI 0.4-1.7; HR 1.8 95CI 0.5-6.0). BrighTNess trial [Loibl Lanc Onc '18]: 3 arm. T→ AC vs. CarboT→ AC vs. CarboT + Veliparib (PARPi)→ AC.Note: Only 15% of patients on this trial were BRCA mutants. Note: The addition of carboplatin to TNBC chemo has not yet demonstrated an OS benefit. This is being evaluated in [NRG-BR003] and ACRIN E1131. TBLQS: Adding carboplatin to neoadjuvant T→ AC chemotherapy for TNBC nearly doubles the pCR rate, while the PARPi veliparib doesn’t seem to provide any additional benefit. Recall: Utilize Xeloda for TNBC patients who do not achieve a pCR for a 5y OS benefit of 10% [CREATE-X]. 634 pts. Stage II-III TNBC, Only 15% had germline BRCA mutations. Total pCR 31→ 58→ 53%. No subset seemed to benefit from the addition of veliparib. Carboplatin with more febrile neutropenia. MDACC [Litton JCO ‘19]: Phase II. Neoadjuvant talazoparib (PARPi) alone.In appropriately selected pts (read: BRCA-mutants), PARPi is very promising in the [neoadjuvant] or [metastatic] setting. TBLQS: The PARP-inhibitor talazoparib confers a >50% pathologic complete response rate when given as monotherapy in women with early-stage, BRCA-mutated breast cancer. See [EMBRACA] trial for metastatic BRCA-mutated cancers, which demonstrated a doubling in ORR. 20 patients. Stage I-III (at least 1 cm) germline BRCA mutated breast cancer, mostly TNBC. pCR > 50%. KEYNOTE-522 [Schmid NEJM ‘20, '22]: Phase III. CarboT ± Pembro→ AC or EC→ surgery → ± Pembro.pCR is increased when adding Pembro to TC/AC chemotherapy. Node positive TNBC appears to benefit the most. TBLQS: Adding Pembro to neoadjuvant chemo for TNBC dramatically improves pCR rate. TBL QS: The addition of Pembro to neoadjuvant systemic therapy and continuation as adjuvant therapy for localized TNBC significantly improves event-free survival. 1174 pts. Stage II-III TNBC. > 80% were PD-L1 positive. MFU 3.25y. Pembro was given for up to 9 cycles after surgery. Capecitabine was not allowed. pCR 51→ 65%. 1.5y EFS ~85→ 91%. 3y EFS 77→ 85%. Equal benefit for those with or without PD-L1+ disease or lack of pCR. G3+ 73→ 78%. Any grade endocrine disorders (thyroid disorder, adrenal insufficiency, thyroiditis, and hypophysitis) 9→ 27%. GeparNUEVO [Loibl ASCO '21🐦]: Durvalumab added to NACT in early TNBC. Significantly improved iDFS, DDFS, and OS. MFU 44 mo. Benefit regardless of PDL-1. (* 3y iDFS 77→ 86%. 3y DDFS 78→ 92%. 3y OS 84→ 95%.23 3y iDFS in pCR arm for ± Durva of ~86→ 96%. KEYNOTE 119 (2015-2017) [Winer Lanc Onc '21]: Phase III. 2nd or 3rd line Single-agent chemo vs. Pembro. TBL QS: Pembrolizumab did not improve survival compared to standard chemotherapy in patients with TNBC who progress after one to two lines of therapy—even among those with CPS ≥ 1 or ≥ 10. 622 mTNBC pts with progression on 1-2 prior systemic therapies. MFU 2.5y. Chemo: Single agent Capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine. Pembro 200 mg q3w x35 cycles. MS for CPS 10+ of ~12→ 13 mo (p=0.057). MS for CPS 1+ of ~10 mo. MS for all-comers of ~10 mo. BROCADE3 (2014-2018) [Diéras Lanc Onc '20]: Carboplatin and Paclitaxel ± Veliparib (PARPi). 513 patients. HER2 negative advanced breast ca with germline BRCA1/2mt. Up to two prior lines of chemo for mets. MFU 3y. MPFS 13→ 15 mo. NRG-BR003 [NCT02488967]: Adjuvant ddAC→ T ± Carboplatin. See NCTN Trial Portfolios by Disease Site: [Breast] and [Future Directions] section. Node positive or high-risk node negative TNBC. NSABP B-59/GBG 96-GeparDouze [NCT03281954]: CarboP→ AC/EC ± Atezolizumab→ Atez Maintenance x1y. TNBC with palpable breast mass ≥ 2.0 cm. Carbo AUC 5 q3w x4c, Paclitaxel 80 q1w x12c→ Doxo 60 or Epi 90/Cyclophosphamide 600 q2-3w x4c. Nearly 80% accrual as of January 2021. Metastatic TNBC: PARPi has a doubling of ORR in the metastatic setting if BRCA mutant TNBC [OlympiAD]. Metastatic TNBC: Atezolizumab added to nab-paclitaxel appears to have an OS benefit if PD-L1 is positive [IMpassion130]. Metastatic TNBC: Chemotherapy + Pembrolizumab has a MS benefit for patients with CPS ≥ 10 [KEYNOTE 355]. Metastatic TNBC: AKT (PI3K) inhibitors added to paclitaxel have a PFS benefit especially if with AKT or PI3K activating mutations and/or PTEN deletions [PAKT trial]. Diagnosis of Inflammatory Breast Cancer The diagnosis of inflammatory breast cancer (T4d) is a clinical diagnosis requiring erythema/peau d'orange changes occupying at least 1/3 of breast which has developed over a period of less than six months. Differential diagnosis includes mastitis and locally advanced breast cancer (LABC - e.g., T4b if edema is present).

heading: Inflammatory breast cancer
full_text: See the Diagnosis of Inflammatory Breast Cancer Summary Box above. Don't perform SLNB for IBC, as the FNR approaches 25% due to alteration of subdermal lymphatics QS [Sosa JAMA '22]. 1-4% of breast cancer cases in the US. No RCTs available. 70% present with regional disease, 30% with DM. Around 1/5 will have contralateral ALN disease as the only site of M1 disease around half the time. Usually ER-, HER2+ Inflammatory vs. LABC: Neglected primary tumors cause secondary lymphatic congestion, erythema, edema, warmth, and asymmetric enlargement. Bulky axillary LAD impedes normal lymphatic flow from the breast. Inflammatory breast cancer has rapid onset <6 months. LABC: >6 mo interval between first sx and presentation for medical tx, no ulceration or skin nodules. Dermal lymphatic invasion (e.g. presence of tumor emboli in dermis) is typical, but full thickness skin biopsy is not required as it is not sufficient in and of itself for diagnosis of inflammatory breast cancer (inflammatory breast cancer is a clinical diagnosis). If skin punch is negative, do incisional biopsy. Add photograph to document. Treatment paradigm: NAC→ MRM→ PMRT (CW, RNI). Upfront surgery CI due to skin involvement: high LF, wound issues. 80% respond to chemo. If there is no response to chemo, consider switching chemo (carboplatin, vinorelbine, capecitabine), or pre-op RT (50 Gy) followed by boost to 60 Gy+. NEVER do BCS for IBC. SLNB is not a reliable method of assessing ALNs in women with IBC. MDACC [Liao IJROBP '00, Bristol '08, Stecklein PRO '19]: Retro. Qday to 60 Gy vs. BID to 60-66 Gy for risk factors.Risk factors: Less than PR to NAC, close SM (< 2 mm), and < 45y. Caveat: Late G3+ for 66 Gy BID may be > 20%. Partial response is defined as < 50% reduction in the clinical skin changes and bidirectional tumor measurements using clinical and radiographic means. 1977-1993 (References above): 115 pts with nonmetastatic IBC. MFU nearly 6y.After 1977, max CW dose 60 Gy. 45-50 Gy PMRT/RNI with boost up to 60 Gy in BID or conventional. After 1981, most got 45/1.5 BID with 15/1.5 BID boost (60 Gy total). After 1985, most got 51 Gy/1.5 BID with 15/1.5 BID boost (66 Gy total). 5y LRC for 60 / 66 Gy BID 58→ 84%. 10y LRC for 60 / 66 Gy BID 58→ 77%. For patients with < PR / PR / CR to NAC: 5y LRC 51→ 86→ 95%. 5y OS 12→ 51→ 73%. 5y DMFS 0→ 42→ 70%. G3-4 late toxicity for 60 / 66 Gy BID of ~15→ 29% (p=0.08). Lymphedema for 60 / 66 Gy BID of 2.5→ 9%. Fibrosis for 60 / 66 Gy BID of 4→ 6%. Brachial plexopathy for 60 / 66 Gy BID of 0→ 2%. Prognostic factors: Less than PR to NAC, SM close (< 2 mm), < 45y, ± 4 nodes, use of taxane. 2007-2015 (References above): 103 pts with nonmetastatic IBC. MFU 3.5y. After 2006, only patients < 45y, less than PR to NAC, and close/positive SM received 66 Gy BID. After 2006, others (mainly pCR, or minimal residual dz) received median 50/25 with median 10/5 boost (60 Gy total). Carboplatin was added to AC→ T for TNBC. Boost covers surgical bed including mastectomy flaps, drain sites, and scar. 5y LRR-free survival for 60 Gy qday / 66 Gy BID of ~100→ 95%. No difference in crude rates of toxicity. Mayo (2000-2010) [Brown IJROBP '14]: Retro. NAC→ MRM→ Once daily RT. 52 pts with nonmetastatic IBC. Aggressive bolus. MFU 5y. Roughly 50/25 with 10 Gy boost (66%). Consider 16 Gy boost for age < 45, < PR, or SM+. Boost to mastectomy scar + 2-5 cm to block edge. Bolus (0.5-1.5 cm) every day continued regardless of skin reaction. 5y LRC 81%. 5y DFS 56%. 5y OS 64%. LRR is associated with a worse OS. ECE was associated with worse LCR, DFS, and OS. pCR is associated with a trend towards improved LRC. Age > 50yo was associated with better DFS. Acute G3 toxicity in 46%. No late G3 toxicities, with two G4 (~4%) toxicities.

heading: Treatment of Inflammatory breast cancer
heading_path: Subtypes / Pathology > Inflammatory breast cancer > Treatment of Inflammatory breast cancer
full_text: ARRO: [Inflammatory breast cancer]. If < PR to chemo, may switch to alternate chemo or consider preop RT if patient is still considered for surgery. MDACC: 3-5 mm bolus. Boost covers surgical bed including mastectomy flaps, drain sites, and scar. Qday for pCR or minimal residual disease. BID for < 45y, SM close/positive/unknown, and < PR to NAC. 1.5 BID to 51 Gy. Boost to 60 or 66 Gy (initial skin involvement and tumor). Bolus for qday: qod for the first two weeks, then prn to achieve brisk erythema. Bolus for BID: every fraction x5d, qof x5d, then prn to achieve brisk erythema. Boost any residual to 66 Gy. Mayo: 0.5-1.5 cm bolus. Boost covers scar + 2-5 cm to block edge. Bolus every day continued regardless of skin reaction. Standard PMRT: Cover CW, undissected axilla, SCN, IMN.

heading: DCIS and LCIS
full_text: Breast cancer is the most frequently dx cancer globally: 250k invasives (80%) and 60k non-invasives (20%) in the U.S. Noninvasive (20%): DCIS (85%), LCIS (15%), Paget's (0.5-5%). Increasing incidence may be due to early detection/MMA screening. LCIS is usually incidentally detected. DCIS ~20-25% of all breast malignancies. DCIS is 5x more common than LCIS. LCIS and DCIS may be difficult to tell from ADH or invasive carcinomas with early invasion (Review path!). LCIS vs. DCIS Risk of progression to IDC at 10y for LCIS / DCIS of ~10→ 40%. LCIS is generally non-surgical unless pleomorphic or if there is concern for DCIS (calcs) on imaging. If LCIS alone, observe but if high-risk can do b/l ppx mastectomy, or easier, tamoxifen. Residual microcalcs on MMA suggest DCIS. Take these patients to surgery. Treat Pleomorphic LCIS as DCIS (i.e., at least with BCS). No data for RT. > 4 foci of LCIS increases risk therefore ≤ 4 terminal ductal lobular units from single core may be observed [1]. This is in NCCN 2020. Breast cancer death: ~3% for DCIS. SEER [Narod JAMA Onc '15]: DCIS 20y BCSM 3.3%. 10y OM BCS 0.9%, BCT 0.8%, TM 1.3%. Invasive IBTR 4.9→ 2.5%. MVA: Age < 35y and black with higher BCSM. Should Everyone with DCIS Receive Adjuvant RT? [Warren and Bellon JCO '21].

heading: ADH
full_text: Development and prospective validation predicting low risk for ADH upstaging to malignancy [Lustig ASO '20]: Patients with ADH on core needle biopsy can be stratified into a low oncological cohort with a 2% risk of being upstaged to carcinoma. These patients may be counseled and potentially offered observation as an alternative to surgery. Surgical excision of ADH is recommended due to undersampling of potential malignancy. Upstaging rate was 25%. Five variables were associated with upstaging: Lesion > 5 mm on U/S or MMA, One or more "high-risk" lesion(s) on core needle biopsy, pathological suspicion for cancer and incomplete removal of calcifications on core needle biopsy. [NSABP P-1] included women with h/o LCIS or ADH (most < 3 cm) or 5y breast cancer risk of ≥ 1.66%. Even though there was a 50% RRR in invasive disease for LCIS or ADH during the 5y while on tamoxifen, less than half of women take SERMs to decrease their risk of developing invasive breast cancer. Recommend Chemoendocrine prevention with ADH!

heading: LCIS
full_text: LCIS is a benign entity and is removed from TNM staging, 8th ed. LCIS differs from DCIS as it has no e-cadherin (CDH-1, upstream). Incidentally detected b/c MMA occult and non-palpable. Pleomorphic (PLCIS) is more likely to be detected radiographically. Her2+.Think: PLCIS is like G3 DCIS. Comedonecrosis and microcalcs (radiopaque). PLCIS: Like LCIS, but enlarged ±  irregular nuclei. Also high Ki-67, HR-, HER2+. PLCIS does not have unique recs, due at least in part by lack of historical histo info. Recommendations: Treat P-LCIS like DCIS (at least with BCS). No data for RT. Small studies: Pleomorphic and necrotic LCIS have similar risk for invasive carcinoma as DCIS! 7% of LCIS progresses to IDC in 10y if not treated (~1%/yr), but only 20-25% lifetime risk [Chuba JCO '05]. Compared to 30-40% of DCIS progressing to IDC at 10y (3-4%/yr) if left untreated. LCIS is multicentric in 90% of TM specimens, and is found in the contralateral breast ~33-50% of the time. Only 25-50% of subsequent cancers are ILC. LCIS is more likely to develop into IDC than ILC. Higher risk for DCIS in contra breast, but overall risk for ipsilateral is equal to risk for contralateral. Controversy: Surgical excision after core? This question is in context of no MMA structural abnormalities or residual MMA calcifications (i.e. residual DCIS). Some small retro studies say no. Other studies show 17-27% of pts are upgraded to invasive cancer or DCIS. NSABP [Fisher Cancer '04]: 180 pts LCIS treated with BCS alone. 12y IBTR 14%, 12y CBTR 8%, Around 33% of IBTR were invasive (~5% of the entire cohort). Given these results, pts are not treated with RT after lumpectomy. Tamoxifen in LCIS and ADH See the [Hormone Therapy] section and the Summary Box below. [NSABP P-1] included women with h/o LCIS or ADH (most < 3 cm) or 5y breast cancer risk of ≥ 1.66%. Even though there was a 50% RRR in invasive disease for LCIS or ADH during the 5y while on tamoxifen, less than half of women take SERMs to decrease their risk of developing invasive breast cancer. Risks of tamoxifen: No increased risk of endometrial cancer for premenopausal women. There appears to be a slightly greater risk of PE and cataracts, but not DVT or stroke. There are less osteoporotic fractures with tamoxifen, especially in postmenopausal women.

heading: DCIS
full_text: See the [What is Low Risk DCIS?] Summary Box above the Omission of RT for Low Risk DCIS section. Around 60k cases per year. Mammographic detection is most common. 15-30% progress to IDC in 10y (3-4%/yr) if not treated, ~ 10x higher risk for IDC! [Ryser JNCI '19] Compared to ~7% of LCIS progressing to IDC at 10y (~1%/yr). Mortality risk ≅ 10% of recurrence risk after BCS. Up to 50% may progress to invasive disease over a 30 year period [Collins Cancer '05, Sanders Cancer '05] Incidental IDC at surgery in 10-20% of bx-proven DCIS, higher if G3, ≥ T2 or palpable [Brennan Radiology '11]. Prediction model for underlying IDC with DCIS [Meurs BJC '18, Nomogram]: Biopsy→ Excision. There is a 21% risk of underlying IDC with DCIS. 2,892 DCIS biopsies with 589 invasive cancers. MVA of underlying DCIS: G3 DCIS (OR 1.43), palpable tumor (OR 2.22), BI-RADS 5 (OR 2.36). ADH: ~10-30% will have underlying DCIS at the time of excision. IDC with EIC (extensive intraductal component) if > 25% of IDC is DCIS. IDC with DCIS is associated with a lower oncotype than IDC without DCIS [Zeng BJC '20]. If margins < 1mm, ~30% will have residual dz at excision, higher residual percentage if low grade. See [Omission of RT] in the DCIS section for more. Most growth for low-grade is discontinuous, vs high grade which has continuous growth (paradoxical). Theory to have 1 cm margins in any surgery. Goal for omission of RT: SM ≥ 3mm. Goal for RT: SM ≥ 2 mm, though smaller margins do not mandate re-excision. True multicentricity is rare in the modern era. 80% of the time gaps are < 5 mm. 10% poorly diff have gaps, while 30% well diff has gaps (paradoxical). G1-2 DCIS is more likely to be multifocal/centric, more likely to have gaps, and almost always ER positive. G3 DCIS tends to be continuous and is less likely to be ER positive. Pathology subtypes: "C2PMS". Comedo (worst), Cribriform (third worst), Papillary, Micropapillary, Solid (poor). MMA: Microcalcs are most common (84-98% of cases). Clumped pattern more likely G3 then heterogeneous pattern. Small focal masses are associated with ER+ DCIS. >11 mm and linear vs grouped are more likely to have invasive component.Recall: higher grade DCIS is more likely to be continuous (less likely to be grouped / have gaps). NSABP B-43 (2008-2014) [Flowchart, NCT00769379, Cobleigh JCO ‘21]: BCT ± Trastuzumab IV w1, w4. See [Future Directions] for more. Primary completion date June 2020. HER2/neu is considered a weak prognostic indicator in DCIS. TBL QS: The addition of concurrent trastuzumab to whole breast radiation does not significantly reduce the risk of breast tumor recurrence among patients with HER2+ DCIS. 2014 patients. G3 83%. Postmenopausal 74%. Hormonal therapy 57%. MFU 6.5y. Annual IBTR of ~1→ 0.8% (p=0.26). MRI 98% Sn for high-grade DCIS, MMA ~50%. Can r/o APBI (20% r/o). MRI does not increase the likelihood of negative margins or decrease conversion to mastectomy. Risk of axillary involvement approaches 0% for pure DCIS in modern studies. If pure DCIS, consider SLNB if G3 and >3-4 cm as the risk of nodal involvement appears to increase with size [1]. Risk of axillary recurrence regardless of use of Tamoxifen is 0.1% [Wapnir JNCI '11]. Sample nodes in the context of TM due to permanent alteration of lymphatics. DCIS with microinvasion ≤ 1 mm. If present, consider SLNB as positive 3-10% of the time. Percentage of nodal involvement: No SLN for pure DCIS; but 3-5%+ due to occult invasive disease Recall: up to 25% of bx-proven DCIS can return with an invasive component at the time of surgery. RoR

heading: DCIS with Microinvasion
heading_path: DCIS and LCIS > DCIS > DCIS with Microinvasion
full_text: Many studies say ≤ 2 mm. However, AJCC T1mic ≤ 1 mm. DCIS with microinvasion ≤ 1 mm. If present, consider SLNB as positive 3-10% of the time. Typically, in studies, DCIS with microinvasion are included with early-stage IDC therefore information is limited. Modern single institution studies don't indicate a worse outcome for DCIS with microinvasion vs. G3 DCIS. May be related to pathologic features of underlying DCIS, not conferring worse prognosis. Recurrence rate for TM / BCS / BCT of ~2-4→ ~30-45→ ~7-15%. EBCTCG: Overview of the RCTs for RT in DCIS [Correa JNCI '10] BCS ± RT. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. IBTR cut in half with RT (compared to [2/3 RRR] for IDC). Around half of recurrences are invasive. There is no difference in BCM or OM. However, no therapy has demonstrated an OS benefit for DCIS given the [low risk of death] to begin with. The benefit for BCT is more pronounced in women ≥ 50y. There is no increased mortality with RT or increased heart events. 3,729 patients from B17, EORTC 10853, UK ANZ DCIS and SweDCIS. All trials: LRR halved with RT. ~50% of recurrences are invasive. All trials: 50 Gy in 25 fractions without boost. 10y IBTR 28→ 13%. 10y invasive IBTR 15→ 7%. In both groups, 48% of the recurrences were invasive. All IBTR HR 0.49, ipsi DCIS recurrence HR 0.61. 10y IBTR for women < 50 of 29→ 19%. 10y IBTR for women ≥ 50y of 28→ 11%. 10y IBTR for G1-2, SM- and size ≤ 2 cm of 30→ 12%. RoR 10y BCM ~4% and 10y OM ~8.3%. 30% reduction in any breast event (ipsi or contra) with tamoxifen, no difference in OS.

heading: BCT and LRR in DCIS
heading_path: DCIS and LCIS > DCIS > BCT and LRR in DCIS
full_text: Around 20% of the four trials below had positive surgical margins, mostly median T1c size (compared to ~5 mm on [RTOG 98-04]). B17 had the highest proportion of patients receiving a boost (only 9%), so data for boost in DCIS is not very robust. RoR NSABP B-17 (1985-1990) [Flowchart, Fisher NEJM '93, JCO '98, Semin Onc '01]: R0/1 BCS ± RT. See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section and [Wapnir analysis] of B17 (BCS ± RT) and B24 (BCT ± Tamox) for more. WBRT after BCS cuts IBTR in half. ~50% of recurrences are invasive. Longest follow up of any trial. 813 pts with non-palpable DCIS. No tumor on ink (17% SM+ on path review). 9% boost. MFU 20y 12y IBTR 31→ 15%, 12y OS ~86%. 17y IBTR 35→ 20%. 17y non-invasive IBTR 15.4→ 9%. 17y invasive IBTR 20→11%. There was no improvement in BCM or OS (but only around 3-4% die from DCIS invasive recurrences, therefore not powered to determine a difference in either metric). EORTC 10853 (1986-1996) [Julien Lancet ‘00, Bijker JCO '06, Donker JCO ‘14]: BCS ± RT. WBRT after BCS cuts IBTR in half. ~50% of recurrences are invasive. 1,010 pts. ≤ 5cm. No boost. 71% detected by MMA. 16% SM+ or unknown. Only 5% boost. Risk of recurrence greatest in the first 5y following treatment. On MVA, inc LR with age < 40, palpable DCIS, SM+, cribriform and solid, and tx w BCS only. 10y EFS for age ± 40y of 66→ 81%. 10y EFS for clinical / mammographic detection of 74→ 82%. 10y EFS for G3 / G2 / G1 of 74→ 73→ 86%. 10y EFS for solid-comedo / cribriform / clinging-micropap of 73→ 74→ 91%. 10y EFS for SM ± of 68→ 81%. 10y IBTR 26→ 15%. 10y non-invasive IBTR 14→ 7%. 10y invasive IBTR 13→ 8%. 15y IBTR 31→ 18%. Salvage mastectomy 19→ 13%. UK/ANZ (1990-1998) [Houghton Lancet ‘03, Cuzick Lanc Onc '11]: 2x2 BCS ± tamox x5y ± RT. RT decreases IBTR even when on tamoxifen. CBTR is reduced with tamoxifen. Tamoxifen does not decrease IBTR in the setting of radiotherapy. 1030 pts. 10% < 50y. ER status unknown. Allowed microinvasives, did not require ink. MFU 13y. 5y breast events: 22→ 18→ 8→ 6%. Tamoxifen: 10y IBTR for ± RT of 13→ 2%. No Tamoxifen: 10y IBTR for ± RT of 17→ 3%. 10y CBTR for ± tamoxifen of 4→ 2%. SweDCIS (1987-1999) [Holmberg JCO ‘08, Wärnberg JCO ‘14]: BCS ("sector resection") ± RT. This trial was utilized as the foundation for [DCISionRT]. 1046 pts. 1987-1999. 80% 50 Gy. 20% SM+ or unknown. DCIS < 1/4 of breast. MFU 20y. 20y IBTR 32→ 20%. 20y ARR 12%; 10% for in situ and 2% for invasive. 13y LR 19→ 7%. Hormone therapy in LCIS and DCIS See the [Chemoprevention] section and the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section. Women with LCIS or ADH treated with 5y of tamoxifen have a 50% RRR of invasive breast cancer during years 1-5, this decreases but is still significant by year 10 [NSABP P-1, 2019 USPSTF Recommendation]. [Wapnir analysis] of B17 (BCS ± RT) and B24 (BCT ± Tamox) for DCIS suggests ~33% RRR in CBTR when adding tamoxifen to BCT, while [B-24] demonstrates around 3% ARR in both IBTR and CBTR with five years of tamoxifen in addition to BCT. There are fewer thromboembolic events with anastrozole. RT decreases IBTR even when on tamoxifen, while tamoxifen appears to decrease CBC by ~2% [UK/ANZ]. Anastrozole can decrease invasives and is non-inferior to tamoxifen. Side effect profiles differ [IBIS-II]. For postmenopausal women < 60y, there is improved BCFI with anastrozole over tamoxifen [NSABP B-35].

heading: Hormone therapy (in situ)
heading_path: DCIS and LCIS > Hormone therapy (in situ)
full_text: See the [Chemoprevention] section, the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section and the Summary Box above. NSABP B17 (BCS ± RT) and B24 (BCT ± Tamox) Analysis [Wapnir JNCI '11]: See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. Notable NSABP DCIS trials: B-06, B-17, B-24. RT and tamoxifen decrease invasive IBTR by ~70%. Invasive IBTR is associated with death. Long term mortality risk is low. Tamoxifen is associated with a ~3% decrease in CBC. Localized DCIS patients. Invasive breast cancer was ~54% of all recurrences. B-17 [Flowchart, Summary] (1985-1990): BCS ± RT. WBRT after BCS cuts IBTR in half. Around 50% of recurrences are invasive. 813 pts with non-palpable DCIS. Localized DCIS. MFU 20y. ≤ 50y (33%). MMA detect (80%). Tamox (0%). Median 1.3 cm. SM+ (17%). G3 (48%). ESTRO Recommendations on Dose and Fractionation for EBRT in early breast cancer [Meattini Lanc Onc '21] Whole breast, nodal, and chest wall RT: Moderate hypofractionation is reasonable to offer regardless of age, pathological tumor stage, biology, margin status, tumor bed boost indication, breast size, invasive or pre-invasive disease, oncoplastic breast conserving surgery, and use of systemic therapy. Consensus was also reached for offering moderate hypofractionation for chest wall irradiation without breast reconstruction (96% consensus), reconstruction regardless of its timing and type of breast reconstruction (87% consensus), and for regional nodal RT (83% consensus). Ultrahypofractionated WBRT, 26/5, may be offered as standard of care or within an RCT or prospective registration cohort (87% consensus). However, it must be within an RCT or prospective registration cohort for chest wall or after breast reconstruction. It should not be offered for nodal RT until ongoing trial results are reported. Partial breast irradiation: Luminal-like subtype and small tumor sized 3 cm or smaller (91% consensus), absence of LVSI (87% consensus), non-lobular invasive carcinoma (87% consensus), tumor grade 1-2 (91% consensus), G1-2 DCIS sized 2.5 cm or smaller with SM ≥ 3 mm (78% consensus), age of 50 or older (87% consensus), unicentric or unifocal lesion (unanimous consensus). Uncertainties remained on the following features: surgical margin status, no tumor on ink (65% support), nodal status including ITC (74% support), and no use of primary systemic therapy (74% support). After first voting, a consensus was reached regarding 38.5/10 BID, similar to RAPID, should not be offered (consensus 87%). Conversely, a consensus was not reached on the following schedules: Moderate hypofractionation 40/15 (70% support), 30/5 (60% support) and 26/5 (65% support). Primary systemic therapy and NAC is considered an exclusion criterion for PBI (78% consensus). Long story short, most patients with ≤ 2 SLN may avoid an axillary lymph node dissection. All patients who are cN+ should get ALND unless enrolled in a clinical trial. ASCO Guideline: SLNB for Patients With Early-Stage Breast Cancer Update December 12, 2016 Lack of SLN metastasis should not receive completion ALND. Pts with 1-2 SLN undergoing BCS should not undergo ALND (in most cases). Pts with SLN mets undergoing TM should be offered ALND if PMRT recommendation is uncertain. DCIS undergoing TM should be offered SLNB. Pts with large tumors (e.g. T3-4), IBC, or DCIS undergoing BCS or who are pregnant should not undergo SLNB. Contemporary Axillary Surgical Management for pN+ after NAC: Survey of ASBS [Weiss ASO '24]: Consider clipping biopsied node-positive disease at diagnosis to ensure removal of SLN at time of surgical resection after NAC. This study aimed to understand when and why surgeons consider omitting ALND after NAC. 328 of 2172 ASBS members (15%) completed the survey. Most (61%) offer SLNB to cN1 patients who respond to NAC, and many (44%) sometimes omit ALND in the setting of residual nodal disease. Respondents less often consider omitting ALND with increasing volume of pathologic nodal disease after NAC and are less likely to omit ALND among patients with cN1 disease at presentation than cN0. Respondents cited radiation administration (74%) and belief that ALND would not improve locoregional (48%), distant recurrence or survival (48%) outcomes when axillary radiation is administered. The respondent group comprising male private practice surgeons, practicing ≥ 21y, considering omitting ALND significantly more frequently. ASCO/CCO Guideline: Management of the Axilla in Early-Stage Breast Cancer [Brackstone JCO '21]: TBL QS: Managing the axilla is complicated, and it’s best that surgeons, medical oncologists, and radiation oncologists are all on the same page (or algorithm). See diagram below. For cN0, only use dual dye if low-volume center or radiocolloid non identification. For cN+, may forgo ALND if restaging with negative axilla. Use dual tracer after NAC, or clipping, and ID ≥ 3 nodes. ASCO Guideline Update: SLNB in Early-Stage Breast Cancer [Park JCO '25]: 11 RCTs with 14 publications, 8 meta-analysis and/or systematic reviews, and one prospective cohort study included. Clinicians should not recommend routine SLNB in postmenopausal women and ≥ 50y of age and with negative findings on pre-operative axillary ultrasound for G1-2, small (≤ 2 cm), HR+, HER2- breast cancer who undergo BCS. Ideally unifocal and in patients who are intending to receive endocrine therapy. For patients over 70, the Choose Wisely statement does not require axillary ultrasound for determining omission of SLNB. Clinicians may offer PMRT with RNI and omit ALND in patients with cN0 breast cancer ≤ 5 cm who receive mastectomy and have 1-2 positive SLN. Clinicians may offer SLNB in patients who have cT3-cT4c or multicentric tumors (clinically node negative) or DCIS treated with mastectomy, and in patients who are obese, male, or pregnant, or who have had prior breast or axillary surgery. Clinicians should not recommend ALND for patients with early-stage breast cancer who do not have nodal metastases, and clinically should not recommend ALND for patients with early stage breast cancer who have 1-2 SLN metastases and will receive BCS and WBRT with or without RNI. ALND should be performed (Low, conditional) for inflammatory breast cancer, presence of biopsy proven palpable axillary nodes, and presence of matted axillary lymph node, multiple suspicious level 3 axillary or supraclavicular lymph nodes. The only systematic difference between treatment groups was in RNI, to the IMN chain, SVC fossa, or axilla, or any combinations of these. MFU 14y. TM predictors of recurrence: Size (± T2), nodal status prior to chemo, and pathologic complete response. Total pCR after TM appears to still benefit from radiation [Mamounas ASCO '14].
