RoR TBL QS: To no big surprise, this large series of patients receiving mostly modern neoadjuvant chemo confirms the benefit of PMRT is strongly tied to the extent of residual nodal disease. 1813 patients from 12 institutions. Clinical stage II-III breast cancer treated with NAC and mastectomy. MFU 6y. Only around 1/3 of HER2-positive tumors received trastuzumab either adjuvant or neoadjuvant. RT (mostly 2D, no IMs) recommended for ypN0 with high risk factors, such as < 50y, cT3-4, cN2, or HR-. 5y LRC / DFS / OS of 86→ 68→ 83%. 5y LRC ± PMRT 82→ 88%. 5y OS for ypN2-3 ± PMRT of 56→ 74% (Figure 4). 5y OS for ypN1 ± PMRT of ~88% (Figure 3). Improvement in DFS and LRC. 5y OS for ypN0 ± PMRT of ~94% (Figure 2). Improvement in LRC. MDACC LRR after NAC in T3N0 [Nagar IJROBP '11]: TM ± PMRT. Consider PMRT for all cT3N0 → NAC → TM 162 cT3 cN0 (by US+FNA) pts. Median nodes 15. 1985-2004. 76% with clinical complete or partial response. 8% pCR. 45% were actually pN0. Overall 5y LRR 24→ 4% with the addition of PMRT; ypN+: 14% vs 53%; ypN0: 2% vs 14% MDACC (1974-1998) [Buchholz IJROBP '02]: Retro. NAC and TM  without PMRT. Advanced disease at presentation and positive LNs after chemo predict for clinically significant rates of LRR. pCR does not preclude the need for PMRT if warranted by the pretreatment stage of disease. 150 pts. No HER2 performed. MFU 4y. LRR at 5 / 10y of 27%. LRR for the 18 pts with total pCR was 19%. Pretreatment factors correlated with LRR: Increased T stage and increased combined clinical stage. Pathologic and Tx factors correlated with LRR: Size of residual primary, increased # LNs, no tamoxifen use. Cox logistic regression analysis Clinical stage IIIB+ (HR 4.5), Pathologic involvement of 4+ LN (HR 2.7), no tamoxifen use (HR 3.9). MDACC LRR after NAC (1974-2000) [Huang JCO '04, IJROBP '05]: NAC ± PMRT. Despite higher risk in patients who received PMRT, these patients still had lower locoregional recurrence! Stage III patients with pCR after NAC appear to benefit from PMRT, while this isn't as clear cut for Stage I-II with pCR. 542 patients with PMRT, 134 patients without PMRT. Only ~10% pCR. 95% adjuvant chemo. 34% tamox. RT to CW, SCV, IM. PMRT higher risk: Stage I-II 50→ 17%, Stage III+ 50→ 85%. Around 2/3 have recurrence in the chest wall, while 1/3 have recurrence in the SCV fossa. Only 2% have failure in IMs, 6% axilla, and 8% infraclavicular. 10y actuarial LRR of 22→ 11%. 10y isolated LRR of 20→ 8%. 10y LRR for stage III+ pCR of 33→ 3%. No difference in LRR when adding PMRT for stage I-II with pCR. MVA LRR HRs for No PMRT / ≥ 20% nodes / IIIB+ / no tamox / < PR / ER- of 4.7→ 3.6→ 2.4→ 2.2→ 1.9→ 1.7. No PMRT or ≥ 20% nodal ratio appears to have the largest impact on LRR. MVA LRR HRs for Skin or nipple invlmt / SCV+ / no tamox / ECE / ER- of 2.8→ 2.7→ 2.7→ 2.1→ 2.1. 10y LRR for 0-1 / 2 / 3 factors of 4→ 8→ 28%. Patients presenting with stage I-II disease with pCR and patients with stage II disease with ypN1a did not have significant decreases in LRR with PMRT. 10y OS ~47→ 55% (p=0.06) but most pts who did not receive RT died of other diseases. 10y CSS ~55%. 10y CSS roughly 20→ 40% for any of: Stage IIIB+, cT4, N2+. MVA CSS HRs for IIIB+ / no pCR / no PMRT / N2+ / < PR / < 10 nodes sampled / No tamox / ER- of  2.4→ 2.1→ 2→ 1.7→ 1.6→ 1.5→ 1.4→ 1.4. Fowble [IJROBP '12]: NAC without PMRT for stage II-III disease. Low risk patients (Stage II, >40y, ER+, pCR or 0-3 nodes without LVSI or ECE) may not benefit from PMRT. 4,246 pts. 24 studies. Stage II (T1-2N0-1), > 40y, ER+, pCR or 0-3 nodes without LVSI or ECE have 6y LRF ≤ 10%. Predictors of LR after PMRT and NAC: Stage/nodal status (with ECE, nodal ratio), pCR, No HT, Skin/nipple involvement.

heading: PMRT in DCIS
full_text: Rashtian [IJROBP '08]: LR for margins > 2 mm is rare. 80 pts. 40% SM ≤ 2mm. 60% G3. 55% Comedo. 4y LRR 7.4%. 4y LRR 2-10mm / ≤ 2mm 2→ 16%. If ≤ 2mm and comedo and/or G3, 4y LRR ~25%. Harvard [Childs IJROBP '13]: Retro. Mastectomy without PMRT.Mastectomy for pure DCIS resulted in low rates of local or distant recurrences. 142 pts. 1998-2005. Pure DCIS. Microinvasion excluded. SM+ (15%). SM ≤ 2 mm (16%). MFU 7.5y. One patient had isolated invasive CW recurrence. Crude CW recurrence for SM+ / SM close / all-comers of 4→ 5→ 1.4%. MDACC [Fitzsullivan ASO '13]: Retro. Mastectomy without PMRT.LRR with close surgical margins is low and less than the rate of contralateral breast cancer. Therefore, PMRT is not warranted except for patients with multiple close/positive margins that cannot be surgically excised. 810 pts. 1996-2009. SM < 3 mm (12%). MFU 6y. 10y LRR for SM ≥ 3 / 1.1-2.9 / ≤ 1 mm of 0.7→ 3.6→ 5%. 10y CBC 6.4%. Independent risk factors for close margins: Multicentricity, pathologic lesion size ≥ 1.5 cm, and necrosis. Ontario [Klein Springerplus '15]: Retro. Mastectomy without PMRT. LRR with positive surgical margins was still not significant. 1,546 pts. Pure DCIS. 1994-2003. MFU 10y. CW recurrence in 2.3%. 10y CW recurrence for < 40 / 40-44 / 45-50 / >50y of ~5→ 1→ 3→ 2%. 10y CW recurrence for G1 / G2 / G3 of ~2.5→ 1.4→ 3%. 10y CW recurrence for SM+ / ≤ 2 mm / > 2 mm of ~3→ 1.4→ 1.5%.

heading: Systemic Treatment
full_text: StatPearls: Bisphosphonate Related Jaw Osteonecrosis Last update: 9/19/2019. ASCO Guideline: Adjuvant Bisphosphonates and Other Bone-Modifying Agents in Breast Cancer March 6, 2017 Postmeno pts who are candidates for systemic tx should consider zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q6m or clodronate 1.6 g/d po. Assess risk factors for osteonecrosis of the jaw and renal impairment, may require dental or oral issues to be fixed. Adjuvant denosumab looks promising but are currently insufficient to make recommendation ASCO Guideline: Role of Bone-Modifying Agents in Metastatic Breast Cancer Update October 16, 2017 Bone mets pts should receive denosumab 120 mg SQ q4w, pamidronate 90 IV q3-4w or zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q12w or q3-4w. Analgesic effects of BMAs are modest, but should not be used alone for bone pain. There is no evidence to support BMA over another. EBCTCG Bisphosphonates [Lancet '15]: ± Bisphosphonates x2-5y. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section and [ASCO's Role of bone modifying agents in metastatic breast cancer]. "The 2015 report on 20,000 women in 26 randomized trials of bisphosphonates, showed that 2–5 years of treatment with these drugs, which are usually used to treat osteoporosis, reduces the risk of breast cancer recurring in the bones, and significantly extends survival. However, bisphosphonate treatment appears effective only for post-menopausal women and has little effect in premenopausal women." 19k patients. MFU 5.5y. Recurrence RR 0.94 (CI 0.87-1.01). Distant recurrence RR 0.92 (CI 0.85-0.99), borderline significance. BCM RR 0.91 (0.83-0.99), borderline significance. Reduction in bone recurrence 0.83 (0.73-0.94) more definite. Among premenopausal women, treatment had no apparent effect on any outcome. Among postmenopausal women, recurrence RR 0.86, distant recurrence RR 0.82, bone recurrence 0.72, BCM 0.82. Bone fractures RR 0.85. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram.

heading: Bone Modifying Agents
full_text: See the Summary Box above and Instant.Oncology: [Bone remodeling] ABSCG-18 [Gnant Lancet '15, '19]: Aromatase inhibitor ± denosumab 60 x6m.Denosumab increases DFS?! This appears to only be effective for postmenopausal women. This appears to be proven false in D-CARE. TBL QS: There’s good evidence to add denosumab twice-yearly to aromatase inhibition for early-stage breast cancer to protect against fractures and even maximize DFS. 3,420 postmenopausal early stage ER+ pts: > 60y, BSO, or < 60y w FSH in postmenopausal range. MFU 6y. Rec Calcium 500 mg and at least 400 mg Vit D. 5y DFS 87→ 89%, 8y DFS 78→ 81%. No report of osteonecrosis of the jaw or confirmed atypical fractures. AE in ~80%, serious AE in ~30%. D-CARE [Coleman Lanc Onc '19]: Adjuvant or NAC ± denosumab 120 mg.TBL QS: Denosumab, an inhibitor of RANKL that prevents osteoclast maturation, has [been suggested] to prevent bone mets in women with early-stage breast cancer. The large D-CARE trial has now put it back in its place, squarely outside the realm of oncologic therapeutics, as it conferred no significant improvement in bone mets-free survival. The lack of difference in bone DMFS appears to hold true in the postmenopausal group. 4,509 pts. Stage II-III. 2010-2012. Denosumab 120 mg q3-4w x6mo then q12w up to 5y. Primary endpoint of bone DMFS was not significantly different between groups. Osteonecrosis of the jaw <1 → 5%. Treatment-emergent hypocalcaemia 4→ 7%. SUCCESS A QS (2005-2007) [Friedl JAMA Onc '21]: 2x2. Chemo randomization, then Zoledronate x2y vs. x5y. 2,987 patients from 250 German study centers. Eligible if N+ or high risk N- (i.e., at least 1 of pT2+, G3, HR-, or age ≤ 35y) IDC. Chemo randomization: 5-FU, epirubicin, cyclophosphamide x3c→ docetaxel ± gemcitabine x3c. After chemo, Zoledronate 4 mg IV q3 mo x2y ± 4g q6mo x3y (5y total). There was no difference in DFS, OS, or DM-DFS. AE 27→ 46%, which was particularly true for skeletal-related events bont pain (4→ 8%) and arthralgia (3→ 5%). ASCO Guideline: IHC Testing of Estrogen and Progesterone Receptors in Breast Cancer January 1, 2020.2020 Update: There is limited data on endocrine therapy benefit for cancers with 1-10% of cells staining ER positive. Samples with these results should be reported using a new reporting category, ER Low Positive. ER and PR should be considered positive if at least 1% positive tumor nuclei. No benefit derived in administering endocrine therapy if ER negative. ASCO Guideline: Adjuvant Endocrine Tx for Women with HR+ Breast Cancer November 19, 2018 Node positive pts should receive extended therapy, including an AI, for up to a total of 10 years. Node negative pts should consider extended therapy for up to 10 years. Low risk node negative tumors should not be routinely offered extended therapy. A substantial portion of benefit for extended adjuvant AI tx is derived from prevention of secondary breast cancers. Extended therapy carries ongoing risks and side effects which should be weighed against potential absolute benefit of extended treatment.

heading: Hormonal
full_text: See the Summary Box above. See the Metastatic Breast Cancer section for use of endocrine therapy in HR+ metastatic breast cancer. In brief, sequential hormones are preferred except for in cases of immediately life-threatening disease. Ovarian suppression or ablation should be considered in premenopausal women (be sure to use bone strengthening agents!). In postmenopausal women, AIs are favored with or without CDK 4/6 inhibitors (e.g., palbociclib). Fulvestrant is commonly used in combination with CDK 4/6i. If disease progresses with non-steroidal AIs, then everolimus may be administered with exemestane. TBL QS: Low-fat diets and conjugated equine estrogens can slash the risk of clinically-significant breast cancer and even reduce breast cancer mortality by 20-40% and deserve further study as less morbid and potentially more effective prevention strategies than that of dreaded hormone deprivation [Breast cancer prevention: Time for change Chlebowski JCO JOP '21]. Use endo if ER+ AND tumor > 0.5 cm (consider for tumors ≤ 0.5 cm). Supplementation with 1200 mg calcium and 800 IU Vit D. SERM for premenopausal. Tamoxifen 20 mg po qd x 5-10y. Careful with P-450 inhibitors such as paroxetine (Prozac) and fluoxetine (Paxil), which may generate fewer active tamoxifen metabolites. Consider switching to citalopram or venlafaxine instead. AE: Endometrial cancer (RR 3.28), DVTs, hot flashes, cataracts. Perform Gyn exam q12mo in women with a uterus. Per [NSABP P-1], 67/70 cases stage I, no increased risk for women  ≤ 49y. AI for postmenopausal. Blocks androgen to estrone + estradiol. Nonsteroidal: Letrozole (Femara) 2.5 mg, Anastrozole (Arimidex) 1 mg. Reversible competitors for aromatase. Steroidal: Exemestane (Aromasin): irreversible steroidal inhibitor. AE: Arthralgias, osteoporosis and hot flashes. Perform bone density scan at baseline and periodically. AIs are ineffective in men without concomitant suppression of testicular steroidogenesis. Do not need to have ovarian suppression! Increased bone events/treatment related fracture with 10y vs. 7y of AI (4.7→ 6.3%; SALSA Gnant NEJM '21). QS See [EBCTCG Chemoendocrine data], which demonstrated chemoendocrine therapy decreases annual CSM by 22% in women 55-69 versus chemo alone. For < 45y, chemoendocrine therapy decreases annual CSM by 28% versus chemo alone. Of the younger women, half were known to be premeno or perimeno. This is similar to the decrease in annual CSM with anthracyclines of ~21% for ages 45-69! EBCTCG Tamoxifen data [Lancet ‘11]: 5y Tamoxifen. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. “The 2012 report on 20,000 women in 20 RCTs of about 5y of tamoxifen versus no tamoxifen, showed a highly significant reduction of about a third in BCM not only during years 0-4 and 5-9 after starting treatment but also during years 10-14. Tamoxifen is effective whether or not chemotherapy has been given and, importantly, even in weakly ER positive [low positive] disease.”In postmenopausal women, anastrozole x5y appears to have a [BCM benefit] of 2% at 15y vs. tamoxifen x5y. 20k pts from 20 RCTs in early breast cancer. 5y of tamoxifen with 80% compliance. Recurrence and death rate ratios (RRs) for years 0-4 / 5-9 / 10-14 of 0.53→ 0.68→ 0.97, suggesting no benefit for RR at year 10 and beyond. RRs most pronounced at year 5 (i.e., when patients are on the pill). Even in marginally ER(+) disease, the gain was still substantial. BCM RRR for years 0-4 / 5-9 / 10-14 of 0.71→ 0.66→ 0.68, suggesting continued BCM benefit after year 10. OM was little affected, despite small absolute increases in thromboembolic and uterine cancer mortality (both in women older than 55y of age). EBCTCG 20y risks of breast cancer recurrence after stopping endocrine therapy at 5y [Pan NEJM '17]: See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. When stopping tamoxifen at 5y for T1N0 disease, this is still at least a 10% chance of DM at 20y! Double that for T2N0 disease. “A 2017 report on the 20-year risks of breast cancer recurrence after stopping endocrine therapy after 5 years showed that when endocrine therapy ended, the risk of the cancer reappearing and spreading throughout the body continued at a similar rate over at least the next 15 years. The risk depended mainly on the original cancer’s size, and the number of lymph nodes that were cancerous. But, even for those patients with the best outlook (small tumors with no spread to the lymph nodes), there was a 10% chance of cancer spread 20 years after the initial diagnosis, sufficient for further endocrine therapy to be at least considered” TBL QS: Risks are driven by T and N stage, and risks started rising significantly after endocrine therapy was stopped at 5 years. However, it's hard to say to what extent other therapies such as chemo and nodal irradiation (or lack thereof) influenced outcomes. It will take comparative analysis with maturing results of long-term endocrine therapy [ATLAS] to determine if longer treatment is 1) tolerable and 2) effective in continually reducing the risk of DM over the decades. So for now, the question remains for very early stage breast cancer patients on endocrine therapy... Is Moore really the better option? 88 RCTs with 500,692 pts→ 62,923 pts < 75y, T1-2, ER+, 0-9 LN, 5y endo. 20y DR in T1 for 0 / 1-3 / 4-9 LNs of 13→ 20→ 34%. 20y DR in T2 for 0 / 1-3 / 4-9 LNs of 19→ 26→ 41% . 20y DR for 1-3 / 4-9 LNs of 31→ 52%. Compare these rates of recurrence to 10 year Oncotype Dx data, which is for ER+, node negative disease [Sparano NEJM '19] 9y DM of 5% among women < 50y with RS 11-25 if clinical low risk (no chemo needed). 9y DM of 12% among women < 50y with RS 11-25 if clinical high risk (give chemo!). Clinical low risk: G1 ≤ 3 cm, G2 ≤ 2 cm, G3 ≤ 1 cm (all add up to 4). Clinical high risk: Anything other than clinical LR. Assessment of long-term DMFS associated with Tamoxifen in postmenopausal patients [Yu JAMA Onc '19]: Lum A vs. B. The Swedish STO study is an old adjuvant tamoxifen trial which gave tamoxifen for two years. Around 700 tumor samples were maintained and molecularly sub-typed using PAM50. Among ER+ tumors, the ratio of luminal A to B was roughly 3:1. At 25 years, the long-term patterns of failure and tamoxifen benefit were interesting to see. Luminal A appears to carry a low but persistent risk of distant failure that carries on greater than 15 years after treatment, therefore tamoxifen confers a long-term benefit. Luminal B appears to have a much higher early risk of distant failure that confers a very short-term benefit to tamoxifen treated patients. TBL QS: Long-term patterns of distant failure and benefit from tamoxifen appear considerably different between luminal A and luminal B ER+ breast cancer.

heading: Tamoxifen
full_text: See the Summary Box above.  ER+ breast cancer can recur up to 20 years out. Perhaps it is worth extending to 10 years for select patients. Add ovarian suppression (with bone strengthening agents) if premenopausal and patient at high risk. Give for 5y instead of 1-2y, consider extension of 10y in initially premeno. There appears to be less benefit after 5y. 5y of tamoxifen reduces recurrence up to 10y, but continues to have a BCM benefit at 15y [EBCTCG]. NSABP B-14 and B-20 [Fisher Lancet '04]: ER(+). ALND→ pN0. Placebo vs. Tamoxifen x5y.See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section and [Oncotype Dx], which was based on these two studies. The first characterization of tamoxifen benefits/side effects. There is a continued OS benefit for tamoxifen at 15y. 2,892 pts from B-14(1982-1988) [Flowchart]: MRM/BCT→ Placebo vs. Tamoxifen . MFU 15y. 1,577 pts from B-20 (1988-1993) [Flowchart]: MRM/BCT→ Tamoxifen ± (C)MF Chemo. 15y RFS 65→ 78%. 15y OS 65→ 71%. ATLAS [Davies Lancet '13]: Tamoxifen 20 mg 5y vs. 10y. 10y of tamoxifen reduces absolute recurrence by 3.7% and is associated with an OS benefit. According to [EBCTCG], the risk of DM for ER+ N1 disease when stopping tamox after 5y is at least 20%. 12,894 women with early stage breast cancer. 10y LR, DFS and OS improved by 3%. 1.5-3% absolute risk of endometrial proliferation of uterine cancer over 5-10y. TAM-01 [DeCensi JCO '19]: Placebo vs. Tamoxifen 5 mg x3y.Breast cancer events cut in half, including a 75% RRR for contralateral breast events. TBL QS: Lower doses and shorter durations of tamoxifen are still effective at preventing breast cancer. 500 pts. BIN with HR+ or unknown. Includes DCIS (70%), ADH (20%) LCIS (10%). < 75y. MFU 5.1y. Neoplastic events 28→ 14. Contralateral breast events 12→ 3. 5y NNT 22. There was a slight increase in hot flashes and no increase in the risk of endometrial cancer or embolism. Does tamoxifen decrease IBTR or CBTR? Controversy concerning IBTR, favor no difference with RT in older trials which did not test for ER status. In the setting of known ER positivity, there appears to be a 50% decrease in any breast events for patients with [DCIS]. There is a decrease in CBTR by ~3%. NSABP B-21 [Flowchart, Fisher JCO '02, '07]: WLE→ Tamox x5y vs. 50/25 WBRT vs. WBRT/Tamoxifen x5y.See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. RT improves LC for tumors ≤ 1 cm when given with tamoxifen, although long term follow up demonstrates perhaps no advantage in adding tamoxifen to BCT for small tumors. Caveat: ER positivity was not mandated. 1,009 pts. IDC. ≤ T1b, pN0, SM-. Only 56% are known to be ER+! Boost at discretion (15%). MFU 11y. Tamoxifen 10 mg po BID x5y. 8y IBTR 17→ 9→ 3%. OS ~93%. 14y IBTR 20→ 10→ 10%. Perhaps no advantage to adding tamox to BCT for small tumors. Tamoxifen decreased CBTR by 3.2%. [NSABP B-20] was the trial testing tamoxifen and CMF chemo; similar results. See [NSABP B-24] and [UK/ANZ] for DCIS, which demonstrated less I-IBTR in the setting of RT. EBCTCG [Lancet ‘15]: Tamoxifen vs. AIs x5y in early breast cancer. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. “The 2015 report on 30,000 postmenopausal women in 9 randomized trials comparing aromatase inhibitors (AIs) with tamoxifen, showed that 5y of treatment with an AI produces even better survival than 5y of tamoxifen. Compared to tamoxifen, taking AIs for 5y further reduced the likelihood of the cancer recurring by 30%, and the risk of dying from breast cancer by around 15%. Thus taking an AI for 5y, compared to no endocrine treatment, would reduce the risk of dying from breast cancer by around 40% in the decade after starting treatment.” 32k postmenopausal patients from 9 RCTs. Recurrence RR during years 0-1 / 2-4 / 5+ of 0.64 / 0.80 / NS thereafter. 10y BCM 14→ 12% (RR 0.85). 10y endometrial cancers 1.2→ 0.4%. 10y bone fractures 6→ 8%. EBCTCG [Lanc Onc '22]: Tamoxifen vs. AIs x3-5y in premenopausal women receiving ovarian suppression or ablation. TBL QS: Aromatase inhibitors are more effective than tamoxifen (a selective ER modulator) in postmenopausal women. In pre-menopausal women, though, AIs are ineffective due to compensatory ovarian estrogen production–unless they’re on ovarian suppression. This EBCTCG meta-analysis of >7000 women treated in 4 randomized trials compared AIs and tamoxifen in pre-menopausal women receiving ovarian suppression. At 5 and 10 years, AIs reduced breast cancer recurrence by an absolute 3% compared to tamoxifen. There was also a significant reduction in distant recurrence, although there was no difference in breast cancer mortality (at least at 8 years median follow-up). Among subgroups, those with HER2 negative disease derived greater AI benefit while those with 4+ nodes, surprisingly, derived greater benefit from tamoxifen. 7030 women with ER+ tumors from 4 RCTs (ABCSG XII, SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE) from 1999-2015. MFU 8y. Rate of breast cancer recurrence RR 0.79 (95% CI 0.69-0.90). Main benefit seen in years 0-4 (RR 0.68) with 5y recurrence risk 10→ 7%. There was no further benefit, or loss of benefit, in years 5-9 or beyond year 10. Distant recurrence RR 0.83 (95% CI 0.71-0.97). No significant differences were observed between treatments for BCM, death without recurrence, or all cause mortality. There were more bone fractures with AI than with tamoxifen (5.1→ 6.4%). Non breast cancer deaths (0.8%) and endometrial cancer (0.2%) were rare.

heading: Aromatase inhibitors
full_text: See the EBCTCG Summary Box above. AIs are preferred in postmenopausal women. AI for postmenopausal. Blocks androgen to estrone + estradiol. Nonsteroidal: Letrozole (Femara) 2.5 mg, Anastrozole 1 mg. Reversible competitors for aromatase. Steroidal: Exemestane - irreversible steroidal inhibitor. AE: Arthralgias, osteoporosis and hot flashes. Perform bone density scan at baseline and periodically. AIs are ineffective in men without concomitant suppression of testicular steroidogenesis. Do not need to have ovarian suppression! When compared to SERMs, modest improvements in DFS, NOT OS. May be better for women < 60y. Couple of options with AI: Initial adjuvant for duration unknown. Sequential therapy after 2-3 years. Extended therapy after 5 years of tamoxifen. In each instance, AI with fewer recurrences compared to control arm, which consisted of 5y of tamoxifen therapy. ATAC trial [Cuzick Lanc Onc '10] Adjuvant Tamoxifen vs. AIs x5y in early breast cancer.There appears to be a 3-4% DFS benefit with anastrozole over tamoxifen even at 10y out, but NS difference in deaths. This is similar to the benefit of RNI in MA.20 and EORTC 22922. RoR The [EBCTCG] analysis suggested a 2% BCM benefit at 10 years (15% RRR). 9,366 postmenopausal pts. ~84% ER(+). MFU 10y. Anastrozole 1 mg qday, tamoxifen 20 mg qday. For HR(+), DFS HR 0.86, time to recurrence HR 0.79, time to distant recurrence HR 0.85. For HR(+), absolute differences in time to recurrence increased from 5 / 10y at 2.7→ 4.3%. Recurrence rates remained significantly lower on anastrozole than tamoxifen after treatment completion, although the benefit was smaller after 8y. Fractures during treatment OR of 1.33, but were similar in post-treatment follow up period. Treatment related serious AE during treatment OR 0.57, but were similar in post-treatment follow up period. TEXT-SOFT [Pagani NEJM '14, JCO '19, '22]: Adjuvant tamox vs. exemestane + ovarian suppression in early br ca. Addition of ovarian suppression to tamoxifen alone has FFDM benefit for premenopausal patients. Exemestane + ovarian suppression has a FFDM benefit over tamoxifen + ovarian suppression in premenopausal patients. Premenopausal women with HR+/HER2- and high recurrence risk may experience a 10-15% absolute improvement in 8y. TEXT: Ovarian suppression + 5y tamox vs. exemestane. BSO / ovarian RT ok after 6mo of triptorelin. Chemo ok.SOFT: 5y tamoxifen ± OFS vs. Exemestane ± OFS. Stratified by prior or no prior chemo. MFU 13 years. 4,690 premeno pts. HR+ ≥ 10%. Mostly HER2-. Completion ALND or RT required if SLNB +. MFU 8.5y. Exemestane: irreversible SERMs seem best in premeno with ovarian suppression who had prior chemo. Triptorelin: GnRH agonist, ovarian suppression. Oophorectomy or RT allowed. Bone strengthening agents were not used in this study. RT: Breast + axilla or IM nodes. 5y DFS 87→ 91%, FFBC rate 89→ 93%. FFDM 92→ 94%. Improved DFS with exemestane + ovarian suppression for women on prior chemo. No benefit for women with no prior chemo. Average absolute improvement in 12y DFS with exemestane + OFS vs. tamoxifen + OFS of 4.6% (HR 0.79). Average absolute improvement in 12y DRFI with exemestane + OFS vs. tamoxifen + OFS of 1.8% (HR 0.83). 12y OS ~90%. Among HER2- tumors (86%), the average absolute improvement in 12y OS with exemestane + OFS vs. tamoxifen + OFS of 2.0% (HR 0.85) and 3.3% in those who received chemotherapy. OS benefit was clinically significant in high-risk patients (e.g., women age < 35y and those with > 2 cm or G3 tumors). 8y FFDM 91% (Range: 63-100%). Average absolute improvement in FFDM with exemestane + OFS vs. tamoxifen + OFS of 5.1% (Range: 1-15%). Average absolute improvement in FFDM with exemestane + OFS vs. tamoxifen of 5.2% (up to 10%). Average absolute improvement in FFDM with tamoxifen + OFS vs. tamoxifen of 3.5%. G3+ toxicity 25→ 32%. Ovarian suppression is a toxic treatment: over 1/4 of patients in ovarian suppression arms withdrew due to toxicity. However, bone strengthening agents were not used in this study. AERAS (2007-2012) [Iwase JCO '23]: Phase III. Anastrozole 5y vs. 10y. 1,593 patients who were disease-free after either anastrozole for 5y or tamoxifen x2-3y followed by anastrozole by 2-3y. 5y DFS 86→ 91%. Extended anastrozole reduced incidence of LR and second primary cancers. ASCO Guideline: Use of Endocrine Therapy for Breast Cancer Risk Reduction September 3, 2019. USPSTF Recommendation: Medication Use to Reduce Risk of Breast Cancer [JAMA 2019]SERMs such as tamoxifen and raloxifene have been formally recommended for use as breast cancer prophylaxis in selected populations for years, having consistently proven relative reductions in primary breast cancer surpassing 50%—not to mention the added bonus of lowering fracture risk. But despite what's been on paper since at least 2013, less than 10% of women eligible for such "chemoprevention" in the US have signed up for a daily pill.TBL QS:  The USPSTF now recommends offering primary chemoprevention via SERM or AI to women with a "high-risk" of developing breast cancer and without medical contraindications. For women at increased risk of BrCa ≥ 35y, discuss tamoxifen (20 mg/d x5y) as an option to reduce ER+ BrCa. Postmenopausal women should discuss raloxifene (60 mg/d x5y), exemestane (25mg/d x5y), or anastrozole (1mg/d x5y). High risk of breast cancer is defined as 5y projected risk of breast cancer ≥ 1.66% or women with LCIS. Tamoxifen: Dose: 20 mg/d orally for 5y [NSABP P-1].Discuss as an option to reduce risk of invasive breast cancer, specifically ER+, in premenopausal women who are ≥ 35y with a 5y projected breast cancer risk of ≥ 1.66% or with LCIS. Risk reduction benefit continues for at least 10y. It is not recommended for women with h/o DVT, PE, stroke, TIA, or during prolonged immobilization. It is not recommended in combination with HRT. Follow up should include timely workup of abnormal vaginal bleeding. Discuss risks and benefits in preventative settings. 5 mg a day is also reasonable [TAM-01]. TBL QS: Lower doses and shorter durations of tamoxifen are still effective at preventing breast cancer. Raloxifene: Dose 60 mg/d orally for 5y [NSABP P-2 (STAR)].Same indications as tamoxifen but postmeno, but uncertain if risk reduction benefit continues for at least 10 years. May be used longer than 5y in women with osteoporosis, in whom breast cancer reduction is a secondary benefit. Should not be used for breast cancer risk reduction in premenopausal women. It is not recommended for women with h/o DVT, PE, stroke, TIA, or during prolonged immobilization. Discuss risks and benefits in preventative settings. Exemestane: Dose 25 mg/d for 5y.Same indications as Raloxifene, but also may be used for atypical ductal hyperplasia. Should not be used for breast cancer risk reduction in premenopausal women. Discuss risks and benefits in preventative settings. Anastrozole: Dose 1 mg/d x5y. Women most likely to benefit are with ADH or LCIS. Also, 5y NCI Breast Calculator RAT of ≥ 3% or 10y IBIS/Tyrer Cuzick Risk Calculator of ≥ 5%, or 4x RR for age 40-44, or 2x for age 45-69. Should not be used for breast cancer risk reduction in premenopausal women. Prior to initiating aromatase inhibitors, perform DEXA. Consider concurrent bisphosphonate and RANK-L inhibitors for women with moderate bone mineral density loss. [IBIS II] excluded women with severe osteoporosis (T score < -4 or 3+ vertebral fractures). Other endocrine therapies that do not reduce bone density, such as tamoxifen or raloxifene, are available for this group of women. Patients should be warned of the possibility of joint stiffness, arthralgias, vasomotor symptoms, HTN, dry eyes, and vaginal dryness.

heading: Chemoprevention
full_text: See the Summary Box above and [hormone therapy] in the in situ section for more. Recall: 80% of DCIS is ER+. G1-2 DCIS is more likely to be multifocal/centric, more likely to have gaps, and almost always ER positive. G3 DCIS tends to be continuous and is less likely to be ER positive. RT decreases IBTR even when on tamoxifen, while tamoxifen appears to decrease CBC by ~2% [UK/ANZ]. Anastrozole can decrease invasives and is non-inferior to tamoxifen. Side effect profiles differ [IBIS-II]. There are fewer thromboembolic events with anastrozole. [Wapnir analysis] suggests ~33% RRR in CBTR when adding tamoxifen to BCT, while [B-24] demonstrates around 3% ARR in both IBTR and CBTR with five years of tamoxifen in addition to BCT. NSABP P-1 [JNCI '05]: ± Tamoxifen x5y. See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. There were more ER+ tumors in the placebo group. Unblinded, 33% of the placebo group started taking SERM. Despite significant reduction, only 44% of women with ADH or LCIS receive risk reduction treatment! 13,953 pts. Women ≥ 60y or 35-59 with 5y BrCa risk of ≥ 1.66%, or h/o LCIS or ADH (most < 3 cm). 7y RRR non-invasives 0.63 (37% reduction), or 0.09% ARR. 7y RRR invasives 0.57 (43% reduction), or 0.27% ARR. Tamox reduced risk of invasiveness in all subgroups (i.e. age, h/o LCIS, ADH, predicted risk of BrCa). 5y RRR in development of invasive dz for subset of pure LCIS / ADH ~50→ ~85%. For history of ADH, RR of invasives at 5 / 7y of  0.14→ 0.25. There is less reduction after 5y. RRR of invasives in years 2-5 / 6 / 7 of ~50→ 29→ 14%. Why is there dec RRR after 5y? Answer: Through all years, the rate of invasive disease remained constant (lower) in the tamox group, while in later years the rate of invasives decreased in the placebo group. Less ER+ cancers develop with tamox: Tamoxifen reduced cN0 cancer by 45% and cN+ cancer by 32%, with more ER+ cancers in the placebo group. Tamoxifen reduced ER+ cancers by 62%, but not ER-negative. Subset analysis for BRCA1/2, breast cancer risk reduced by 62% in those with BRCA2. Undesirable effects of tamoxifen: RR of osteoporotic fractures 0.68 (32% reduction), more pronounced in women ≥ 50y. RR of invasive endometrial ca 3.28. Not increased in women ≤ 49. 7y cumulative rate of 5→ 15/1000. 67 of 70 cases were stage I. RR of PE 2.15, RR cataracts 1.21. RR of death, ICM, stroke, DVT [NS]. Trend towards DVT and stroke in > 50y. NSABP P-2 (STAR) [Vogel JAMA '06, Cancer Prev Res '10]: Tamoxifen 20 vs Raloxifene 60 x5y. See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. Raloxifene reduces invasive breast cancer risk by 38% as compared to 50% reduction of invasives with Tamoxifen. Raloxifene reduces non-invasive breast cancer risk by 39% as compared to 50% reduction with Tamoxifen. Raloxifene has fewer cases of invasive uterine cancer, thromboembolic events, and cataracts than tamoxifen. 19,747 postmenopausal women with 5y BrCa risk of ≥ 1.66%. MFU nearly 7y. Invasive breast cancer incidence ~4.3→ 4.4 per 1,000 women (95% CI 0.82-1.28). Worsened with Raloxifene: Invasive breast cancer (RR 1.24; 95% CI 1.05-1.47). Non-invasive breast cancer (RR ~1.22; 0.95-1.59). Improved with Raloxifene: Invasive uterine cancer (RR 0.55). 	Average annual rate of 2→ 1 cases per 1,000 women. Thromboembolic events (RR 0.75). Average annual rate of 3.3→ 2.5 cases per 1,000 women. Cataracts or surgery (RR 0.8). 	Average annual rate of 15→ 12 cases per 1,000 women. No difference for IHD, stroke, or osteoporotic fractures. Meta of Chemoprevention with SERMs [Cuzick Lancet '13]: ± Raloxifene and Tamoxifen. Greatest benefit within the first 5y. Raloxifene appears less effective, especially for DCIS. 9 trials, 84k pts. MFU 5.5y. 10y IBTR 6.3→ 4.2% (RRR 38%). Most pronounced difference in years 0-5 (HR 0.58) than years 5-10 (HR 0.75). 10y ER+ IBTR 4→ 2.1%. 42 women NNT to prevent one breast cancer event in the first 10y. Thromboembolic events OR 1.73. Vertebral fractures OR 0.66. Royal Marsden Hospital study: ± tamox in 30-70yo. HT okay. 20y ⇒ ~BrCa incidence, a/w lower ER+ cancer. Importantly, diff between two arms became significant only in the posttreatment period (ie after 8y of treatment). Italian tamoxifen prevention study (5408) in 35-70yo, s/p TAH, HT okay. 5y Tamox. ~ breast cancer occurrence. Confounder: 13% of pts in trial high risk for breast cancer, HT okay so may not translate to baseline society. IBIS-I (7152): 35-70. ± 5y tamox. RR 32%, TE OR 2.5, endometrial cancer NS.  Excess of deaths from all causes seen in tamoxifen-treated women. 8y ↓ of all types of invasive cancer [RR 0.73]. ER+ 34% lower risk. 16y- HR 0.72 and greater in subsequent years [HR 0.69]. However, more ER- reported at 10y, HR 2.45 [NS]. IBIS-II [High risk, DCIS]: Two separate trials. High risk and DCIS.Anastrozole can decrease invasives and is non-inferior to tamoxifen. Side effect profiles differ. High risk [Cuzick Lancet ‘13, '19]: High risk patients ± Anastrozole 1mg x5y.TBL QS: Anastrozole taken as breast cancer chemoprevention for 5 years significantly reduces long term risk of breast cancer development in post-menopausal women at baseline increased risk. 3864 high risk postmenopausal pts (fam hx, DCIS, LCIS, ADH). MFU 10y. 5y all breast cancers 4→ 2%. 7y all breast cancers 5.6→ 2.8%. 10y all breast cancers 8.5→ 4.4%. During the initial 5y on the study, the risk dropped 67%. After 5y (off the pill), the risk dropped 37%. Roughly 80% were invasives. Mostly (75%) ER(+). NS difference in ER(-) invasive cancers. DCIS [Forbes Lancet ‘16]: BCT for DCIS→ Tamox vs. Anastrozole x5y.There was no difference between use of tamoxifen or anastrozole in the reduction of in situ or invasive events. 2980 fully excised post-menopausal DCIS pts. MFU 7.2y. AI: Fractures, MSK, HLD, strokes (arthralgia and myalgia). Tamox: muscle spasms, gyn cancers/sx, vasomotor sx, DVT. Equivalent outcomes. Anastrozole is non-inferior to tamoxifen. Anastrozole non-inferior to tamoxifen at 7.2y with similar rates of AE. NSABP B-35 [Margolese Lancet '16]: BCT→ Tam vs. Anastrozole x5y. DCIS.For women < 60y, there is a ~3% BCFI benefit with anastrozole over tamoxifen (compared to IBIS-II DCIS above). 3,104 HR+, DCIS postmenopausal pts. Stratified by age (60). 64% completed all 5y. MFU 9y. Tamoxifen 20 mg/day, anastrozole 1 mg/day. 5y breast cancer-free interval (BFCI) ~96%, 10y BFCI 89→ 93%. 10y DFS ~80% For women < 60y: 10y BCFI 91→ 95%, 10y DFS 86→ 90%. For women ≥ 60y: 10y BCFI ~93%, 10y DFS ~80%. 5y contralateral invasive breast cancer of 2.6→ 1.3%. Toxicity: Thrombosis / embolism of 2.7→ 0.8%. More vaginal symptoms on the anastrozole arm.

Magnesium oxide 400-800 mg po qday may decrease frequency and intensity of hot flashes. Venlafaxine also a consideration. Oxybutynin 5 mg po BID. OASIS-4 [Cardoso NEJM '25]: Phase III. Placebo vs. elinzanetant. Sounds like a ridiculously expensive medication when generic alternatives (e.g., Magnesium oxide) are available. 316 patients with moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms associated with endocrine therapy for HER+ breast cancer aged 18-70 years. Primary endpoint change in mean daily frequency of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms from baseline to week 4 and to week 12. Elinzanetant: 120 mg po qday x52w→ 120 mg po qday x40w. At baseline, the mean daily frequency of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms was 11.4 episodes. Week 4 mean change from baseline -3.0→ -6.5 episodes. Week 12 mean chage from baseline -4.2→ -7.8 episodes.

heading: Chemotherapy
full_text: ASCO Guideline: Selection of Optimal Adjuvant Chemo and Targeted Therapy for Early Breast Cancer Oct 20, 2020 See ASCO neoadjuvant therapy guidelines from 2021. RoR See ASCO rapid recommendation update: Neoadjuvant Pembro is now recommended for early stage TNBC as of 2022. RoR Pts w HER2- BrCa without pCR after standard anthracycline- and taxane-based NAC should consider Xeloda x6-8c. Clinicians may add 1y of adjuvant pertuzumab to trastuzumab-based combo chemo in HR, early stage HER2+. Clinicians may use extended adjuvant tx w neratinib to follow trastuzumab in early stage, HER2+ BrCa. Neratinib causes substantial diarrhea, and diarrhea ppx must be used. Consider adjuvant capecitabine for HER2- w residual dz after NAC (5y OS improved ~5%; 10% for TNBC). RoR Consider adjuvant TDM-1 for HER2+ w residual dz after NAC (3y DFS improved by 10%). RoR ASCO Guideline: Role of Pt and Dz Factors in Adjuvant Systemic Tx for Early-Stage, Operable IBC June 17, 2019All recommendations refer to patients who present with HR+, HER2-, axillary node negative early breast cancer. See ASCO neoadjuvant therapy guidelines from 2021. RoR For patients > 50y with Oncotype DX < 26, and for patients ≤ 50y with Oncotype DX scores < 16, there is little to no benefit from chemotherapy. Clinicians may offer endocrine therapy alone. For patients ≤ 50y with Oncotype DX score 16-25, clinicians may offer chemoendocrine therapy. New evidence suggests patients ≤ 50y with Oncotype Dx 11-25 should consider chemotherapy if [clinical high risk]. Patients with Oncotype DX >30 should be considered candidates for chemoendocrine therapy. Based on Expert Panel consensus, oncologists may offer chemoendocrine therapy for Oncotype DX 26-30. Mammaprint for HR+, HER2-, node negative BrCa at high clinical risk to help determine whether or not to withhold adjuvant systemic chemo due to the ability to ID a good-prognosis population where chemo may not benefit. Women in low clinical risk did not benefit from chemo regardless of genomic Mammaprint risk group. Mammaprint for HR+, HER2-, N1 BrCa at high clinical risk to inform decisions on withholding chemotherapy. Benefit from chemo cannot be excluded, particularly for 2+ lymph nodes. Do not use Mammaprint to guide decisions on adjuvant systemic treatment for HR+, HER2-, N+ at low clinical risk, nor any patient with HER2+ or TNBC due to lack of definitive data in these populations. Consider adjuvant chemotherapy for: pN+: Requires 1+ LN with macro metastatic deposit > 2 mm. ER-, HER2+, and high risk node negative w size > 5 mm. pN-: if  tumor > 5 mm, G3, TNBC, LVSI, Oncotype DX 10y risk of distant relapse > 15%, or HER2+. Tumors < 5 mm, pN- and no other high risk features may not benefit from adjuvant chemo. ASCO Guideline: Chemo-and Targeted Tx for HER2- (or unknown) Advanced Breast Cancer September 2, 2014 Except in cases of immediately life-threatening dz, hormone therapy, alone or in combo, should be used for initial tx. Single agents preferred to combination chemo, and longer planned duration improves outcomes. Discuss toxicity. The role of bevacizumab remains controversial. EBCTCG Chemoendocrine therapy [Lancet '05, '12]: Anthracyclines > non-anthracyclines. Add a taxane to it. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. "The 2005 Lancet report on systemic therapies showed the substantial effects on 15y survival of the chemo regimens (eg, about 6 mos of anthracycline-based chemo) and endocrine regimens (eg, 5 years of tamoxifen) that were being tested in the 1980s." "The 2011-12 Lancet reports updated evidence from 2005, bringing together data from 100,000 women in 123 randomized trials of chemotherapy, showing that chemotherapy can reduce breast cancer mortality not only in ER-negative but also in ER-positive disease, and showing benefits of taxane-based over standard anthracycline chemotherapy." Adjuvant CTX and tamoxifen decrease odds of recurrence and death for all age groups.Issue: Didn't consider HER2 status. Retro analysis suggests the best benefit in HER2+. Addition of taxane to fixed anthracycline regimen reduced BCM (RR 0.86). CMF and standard 4AC are equivalent, but >240 mg A (e.g. CAF, AC) reduced BCM compared to CMF (RR 0.78). Trials versus no chemo suggested greater mortality reductions with FAC than standard 4AC or CMF. Anthracyclines decrease annual CSM by ~21% for ages 45-69y, insufficient evidence for women >70y. Chemoendocrine therapy decreases annual CSM by 22% in women 55-69 versus chemo alone. For < 45y, chemoendocrine therapy decreases annual CSM by 28% versus chemo alone. Of the younger women, half were known to be premeno or perimeno. This is similar to the decrease in annual CSM with anthracyclines of ~21% for ages 45-69! Old data from the Lancet '05 article: Tamoxifen decreases annual CSM by 31%, largely irrespective of chemo or other factors. Chemo with 10-15% 15y OS and DSS benefit for premeno and a 5% OS and DSS benefit for postmeno pts. Largely independent up age (up to age 70), taxane/anthracycline regimens reduce CSM by ~33%. EBCTCG Chemotherapy dose intensification [Lancet ‘19]: q3w vs. q2w chemotherapy. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. “The 2019 report on 37,000 women in 26 trials of  chemotherapy dose intensification showed that increasing dose intensity (e.g. by 2-weekly rather than 3-weekly administration) reduced the risk of breast cancer recurrence and death.” Most women were aged younger than 70y and had node positive disease. 10y risk of recurrence of 28→ 24% (RR 0.83). 10y CSM 21→ 19% (RR 0.87). 10y OM 25→ 22% (RR 0.87). EBCTCG Meta [McGale Lancet Onc '18]: NAC vs. Adjuvant chemo. See the [Overview of EBCTCG Studies] section. “The 2018 report on 4500 women in 10 trials of neoadjuvant chemotherapy versus adjuvant chemotherapy showed that there was no significant difference between neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy for distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality or death from any cause. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy allowed more women to have breast-conserving therapy than adjuvant chemotherapy. However, the risk of cancer recurring in the breast or adjacent lymph glands (local recurrence) was somewhat higher in the neoadjuvant than the adjuvant chemotherapy group. This increased risk of local recurrence was greater in trials which omitted surgery in the event of a good response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.” Stage-matched yp has higher LRR. 4,756 pts from 10 RCTs. Compared to the same chemo before and after. 1983-2002. MFU 9y. Chemo: Mostly anthracycline based (81%). BCT 65→ 49%. Increased BCT in the NAC arm likely contributes to increased LR. NAC does NOT improve OS, but can convert from TM to BCS in 20-30% of pts. 15y LR 21→ 16%. 15y DM ~38%. 15y BCM ~34%. 15y OM ~41%. NAC with 30% CR, 40% PR. More than 2/3 respond to NAC. Docetaxel is lipophilic, and appears inferior in overweight women with breast cancer QS [Desmedt JCO '20]. General Principles Use taxanes for node positive patients. Dose dense (q2w cs. q3w) with increased efficacy. Chemo above the age of 70 is unclear as this age group was excluded from early clinical trials. Chemo generally recommended for T1c or pN+: TN or HER2/neu: Consider adjuvant chemo for T1c, consider for T1b. ER+ and Her2/neu- and T1bN0: Consider 21-gene assay to determine the role of adjuvant chemo. Can try to avoid chemo in T2 disease. Adjuvant Typically post-op for LN+, ER-, HER2+. Consider for young age or high oncotype. DFS benefits are more pronounced in younger, LN+, ER-. Neoadjuvant ~OS as adjuvant (NSABP B18) but may allow less extensive surgery. Consider adjuvant capecitabine for TNBC. Consider adjuvant TDM-1 for HER2+ w residual dz after NAC. Trastuzumab w OS for HER2+ in addition to chemo. Add pertuzumab with pCR up to 50%! Don't give concurrently with Adriamycin but can give with RT. Upfront-Outback [Recht NEJM '96, Bellon JCO '05]: BCS + ALND→ Sequential CRT (RT first vs. Chemo first). Although the initial paper demonstrates FFDM benefit when chemo is given first, this washes out at long term. No difference in chemo first versus RT first, though the standard is still to give chemo before RT (except capecitabine). 244 pts. Stage I/II at risk for DM. Chemo: 4c cyclophosphamide 500 D1, doxo 45 d3, MTX 200 d1/15, 5-FU 500 d1, prednisone 40 d1-5. WBRT 45 Gy + 16-18 Gy boost. 5y FFDM 64→ 75%. 10y FFDM ~65%. 10y OM ~30%. Among women with close margins (n=47), crude LR 4→ 32%. CALGB 9344 [Sartor JCO ‘05, JCO '03, '07]: Node positive disease. Adjuvant 4AC→ ± 4T (Paclitaxel). Paclitaxel improves DFS and OS, but does not benefit patients with HER2-, ER+ cancers. Modern chemotherapy can reduce the risk of locoregional recurrence. 3,121 pts. LN+ disease. Tamoxifen in 94% ER+. AC and T each q3w x4c. MFU ~6y. Adriamycin 60/75/90, cyclophosphamide 600, paclitaxel 175 q3w x4c. 5y DFS ~66% regardless of adriamycin dose escalation. 5y DFS for ± paclitaxel 65→ 70%, 5y OS for ± paclitaxel 77→ 80%. 5y LRR for ± paclitaxel of 13→ 6%. HER2 subset: Addition of paclitaxel to HER2+ HR for recurrence 0.59! NSABP B-28 [Mamounas JNCI '05]: Node positive disease. Adjuvant AC x4→ ± 4T (Paclitaxel).There is more of a benefit with addition to taxanes to adriamycin for HR(-) patients. See the [Oncotype] analysis. 3060 pts. 1995-1998. Half BCT and half TM (no PMRT). Tamoxifen if ≥ 50y or < 50y and HR+. MFU 5y. 5y DFS 72→ 76%. 5y OS 85%. ECOG E1199 [Sparano NEJM '08, '15]: Adjuvant 4AC→ 4T vs. 12T (Paclitaxel/Doxorubicin). Benefit for all pts with weekly taxol, including ER+ / HER2- cancers 4,954 pts. Stage II/III. Adriamycin 60, cyclophosphamide 600 q3w x4c. Q3w arm: Paclitaxel 175 or docetaxel 100 q3w x4c. Q1w arm: Paclitaxel 80 or docetaxel 35 Q1w x 12c. Weekly taxol DFS (HR 1.27), OS (HR 1.32). OS benefits are lost in the long term. Long term: weekly taxol DFS (HR 0.84) with ~OS (HR 0.87, p=0.09). Weekly taxol for TN tumors improved DFS and OS (each HR 0.69, SS). Long term: q3w docetaxel DFS (HR0.79), with ~OS (HR 0.86, p=0.054). Common chemotherapy regimens Adriamycin lifetime total 450. AC gives 240 mg/m2. CAF (50s) gives 300 mg/m2. AC: Adriamycin 60 + cyclophosphamide 600 q2/3w x4c (ddAC regimen [q2w] with filgrastim support). CALGB 9741: ddAC q2w→ paclitaxel q3w inc DFS, ddAC may have inc efficacy in high risk patients. Adria 60 mg, as CALGB 9344 II-IIIA N+ tested A 60/75/90. CMF and standard AC x4c are equivalent, while FAC [appears superior] of the three. Solution: Give ddAC, and at least 240 mg of doxorubicin for OS advantage, as anthracyclines decrease annual CSM ~21% for ages 45-69y, insufficient evidence for >70y. AC→ T: As above + Paclitaxel 175 q3w x4c or 80-100 q1w x12c. Paclitaxel = taxol; docetaxel = taxotere. [ECOG E1199]: ACq3w x4→ paclitaxel/docetaxel q3wk ≅ qwk., qwk may be better in TNBC. ddAC q2w x4c→ paclitaxel q1w x12c is a common NAC regimen. AC→ TH: As above, but Trastuzumab 4 mg/kg loading→ 2 mg/kg q1w concurrently with paclitaxel, then trastuzumab monotherapy (6 mg/kg q3w) x1y. Cardiac monitoring at baseline and 3, 6, 9 mo. TCH ± Pertuzumab. TCHP (carboplatin) is the most common contemporary NAC for HER2+ breast cancer [KRISTINE]. Taxotere 75, Carbo AUC 6, H 8→ 6, Pertuzumab 840→ 420 q3w up to 18c (6c given neoadjuvantly). TC: Taxotere 75, cyclophosphamide 600. TCH: Taxotere 75, carboplatin AUC 6 q3w x6c + Trastuzumab as above. TAC: q3w x6c. CMF: cyclophosphamide, MTX, 5-FU. For > 65y, AC or CMF may be superior. CAF: 5-FU, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide. Non-taxane chemo, most common for preggers. There appears to be no increased risk of major congenital malformations if chemo given > 12w [van Gerwen JAMA Netw Open '21]. QS CAF is the most widely studied regimen for pregnant women, but AC (q3w) is also commonly used today in pregnant women. Not ddAC (q2w) as G-CSF support in pregnant women has not been well studied. Do not give anti-HER2 therapy during pregnancy due to oligohydramnios. CEF: 5-FU, epirubicin, cyclophosphamide. FEC is a grueling regimen and does not improve DFS vs. AC (B-36) for node negative disease. FEC may be good for node positive disease. Preferred regimens: AC→ T; TC. Paclitaxel increases DFS and OS, questionable additional benefit in ER+ disease. Risk of recurrence: Oncotype Dx and Mammaprint Estimating risk of relapse or death / benefit of systemic tx: www.adjuvantonline.com, www.predict.nhs.net (includes HER2). ASCO Guideline: Use of Biomarkers to Guide Decisions on Adjuvant Systemic Tx for Early-Stage IBC May 31, 2019 See [Mammaprint] section for the version of this guideline pertaining to Mammaprint. Oncotype DX for ER+, HER2-, node negative BrCa to help guide decisions for adjuvant systemic chemo. Oncotype DX should not be used for ER+,  HER2- node positive BrCa. Oncotype DX should not be used for HER2+ or TNBC. For patients > 50y with Oncotype DX < 26, and for patients ≤ 50y with Oncotype DX scores < 16, there is little to no benefit from chemotherapy. Clinicians may offer endocrine therapy alone. New evidence suggests patients ≤ 50y with Oncotype Dx 11-25 should consider chemotherapy if [clinical high risk]. For patients ≤ 50y with Oncotype DX score 16-25, clinicians may offer chemoendocrine therapy. Patients with Oncotype DX >30 should be considered candidates for chemoendocrine therapy. Based on Expert Panel consensus, oncologists may offer chemoendocrine therapy for Oncotype DX 26-30. Oncotype Dx in a Nutshell Only obtained for early stage ER+ node negative patients in order to determine LRR and DM and need for chemo. Oncotype LR (< 11): 9y risk of any recurrence < 5%. Treatment: Endocrine therapy alone. Oncotype IR (11-25): Endocrine therapy ± chemotherapy was investigated by [TAILORx]. Treatment for women > 50y: Chemotherapy not required. Treatment for women <  50y: Chemotherapy if [clinical high risk] as 9y risk of recurrence is > 10%.Clinical low risk: G1 ≤ 3 cm, G2 ≤ 2 cm, G3 ≤ 1 cm (all add up to 4). Clinical high risk: All others. Oncotype HR (>25): Endo + Chemo. All who receive chemotherapy still have a 9y risk of recurrence of 15%. Compared to N1 disease, which has a risk of recurrence of around 20-30% [Pan NEJM '17]. Recall: N1 disease is not tested by Oncotype, as they all receive chemotherapy anyway. Molecular Drivers of Oncotype Dx, PAM50, endopredict and BCI [Buus JCO '20]: "In contrast to the other tests, Oncotype Dx was most often driven by estrogen-related genes as opposed to proliferation genes. So, for many tumors, Oncotype RS appears to predict the benefit of endocrine therapy more so than the benefit of chemotherapy." TBL QS: Understanding the biology of prognostic molecular tests for breast cancer is key to interpreting their results. TransATAC sample collection. 785 pts with ER positive, HER2 negative tumors treated without chemo. Clinicopathologic features included in some tests were excluded from comparisons. Estrogen, proliferation, invasion, and HER2 module scores were used to characterize the respective molecular features. There were moderate to strong correlations among the four molecular scores except Oncotype Dx RS. RS had a strong negative correlation with its estrogen module and moderate positive correlation with its proliferation module. RS's proliferation module explained 73% of ROR's variance, while the estrogen module explained only 0.6%. Most of EP and BCI's variation was accounted for by the proliferation module and much less by the estrogen module.

heading: Oncotype Dx (21 gene assay)
full_text: See the Oncotype Dx in a Nutshell Summary Box above. Measures distant recurrence at 10 years. See details on IDEA in the [Future Directions for Omission] section. See details on [ADAPT] which successfully omit chemotherapy in patients with RS12-25 and Ki-67 < 10% after 3 weeks of neoadjuvant endocrine therapy. See [TAILOR-RT/ MA.39]. BCS/TM ± PMRT for Mammaprint low risk node + breast cancer. Molecular Predictive and Prognostic Markers in Locoregional Management [Mamounas, Mitchell and Woodward JCO '20]. Oncotype Dx (21 gene assay): For early stage ER+ node negative patients. Performed to tell us who needs systemic chemo based on data from LRR and DM. Data is from B-14 and B-20, which utilized BCT or TM alone without PMRT. BTxCHOICE [Jayasekera JCO '21]: An industry-independent decision tool that integrates clinicopathologic features, comorbidities, and genomic information for women with node-negative, invasive, HR+, HER2- early stage breast cancer.TBL QS: BTxCHOICE is a web-based decision tool to help inform patients and clinicians about the benefits of chemoendocrine therapy versus endocrine therapy alone for early stage, ER+ breast cancer. B-20 analysis [Flowchart, Paik JCO '06]. 651 pts with pathology blocks available. Tamoxifen ± Chemo.The high risk group (≥ 31) barely has a double-digit rate of DM at 10 years when receiving tamox and chemo. MRM/BCT→ Tamoxifen vs. (C)MF Chemo [Flowchart]. LR (< 18): 10y FFDM ~96%. Endocrine alone is adequate for low risk. IR (18-30): 10y FFDM ~90%. Chemotherapy for select groups. HR (≥ 31): 10y FFDM 60→ 88%. Chemotherapy for all. B-14 and B-20 analysis [Mamounas JCO '10]: ER(+). ALND→ pN0. Placebo vs. Tamoxifen ± Chemo.See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section and [Oncotype Dx], which was based on these two studies. See Fisher's 2004 [breakdown] on the design of B-14 and B-20 and the benefit of tamoxifen. Both of these studies utilized TM without adjuvant RT. This study suggests that the 10y LRR is ≤ 5% for LR or IR patients who underwent mastectomy and received tamoxifen, therefore PMRT may not be necessary for Oncotype ≤ 30. 895 patients with path blocks available. LR (< 18): Compared to 10y LRR of 6% for Low Risk Mammaprint. RoR 10y LRR of 11→ 4→ 2% No benefit in chemotherapy. Give Tamoxifen alone. 10y LRR with tamox for BCT / TM of 7→ 2%. Do LR Oncotype need PMRT if tamox is given? IR (18-30): 10y LRR of 20→ 7→ 3%. Chemotherapy may benefit select groups. 10y LRR with tamox for BCT / TM of 11→ 5%. heading: Mammaprint (70 gene assay)
full_text: See the Summary Box above. 70 gene assay: Low risk or high risk. Molecular Predictive and Prognostic Markers in Locoregional Management [Mamounas, Mitchell and Woodward JCO '20]. Drukker [Breast Ca Tr '14]: Low vs. High risk Mammaprint.The 70-gene signature's strongest prognostic power is seen in the first 5y after diagnosis. 293 patients < 53y with T1-2N0-1 breast cancer. 1984-1995. 50% N1. MFU 18.5y. DMFS is predicted for low vs. high risk Mammaprint, applying to node negative and node-positive pts. 10y LRR 6→ 13%. Compared to 10y LRR of 4% for Oncotype RS < 18. There is a 1.5% detriment for withholding chemo. 5y DMFS 96→ 95%, 8y DMFS 92→ 89.4%. There is a 2.6% detriment for withholding chemo. For genomic HR and clinical LR, equivalent 5y OS w/o DM. heading: Neoadjuvant Therapy
full_text: See the [Chemotherapy] section. ARRO: [Radiation indications in the setting of NAC]. RoR See ASCO rapid recommendation update: Neoadjuvant Pembro is now recommended for early stage TNBC as of 2022. RoR There is insufficient evidence to support use of markers or genomic profiles. Consider histology (e.g., inflammatory), grade, stage, HR, HER2. Clinically node positive TNBC and/or at least T1c should be offered an anthracycline- and taxane-containing regimen. cT1a-cT1b cN0 TNBC should not routinely be offered NAT. Carboplatin may be offered to TNBC to increase pCR. There is insufficient evidence to add ICI to standard chemotherapy. Patients with HR+/HER2- disease may receive NAT in any patient where the decision for chemotherapy can be made without surgical pathology data. Postmenopausal patients with HR+, HER2- disease may use hormone therapy to downstage disease. Clinically node positive or high-risk node negative HER2 positive disease should be offered NAT. cT1a-cT1b cN0 HER2 positive disease should not routinely be offered NAT.

heading: Perform SLNB before NAC
heading_path: Neoadjuvant Therapy > Perform SLNB before NAC
full_text: Traditional FN 4-8%; now FN rates ~2.5%. After NAC, FNR 6-12% using 2 dyes. With one dye 18%, and I-125 seed localization 4%. Primary cause of variation: biopsy proven node not routinely identified as SLN in 25% of patients. SLNB is reliable prior to NAC, but not afterwards. FNR after NAC is in the single digits for 3+ SLNs [SENTINA]. SLNB after NAC leads to 13% FNR when utilizing two dyes. FN SLNs were N2 15% of the time on ALND [Z1071]. "The much more accessible lower axillary sampling technique appears more reliable than sentinel node sampling (without a clip) at ruling out axillary nodal disease following neoadjuvant chemo for breast cancer." QS [Parmar JCO Glob Onc '20].

heading: Nonoperative management
full_text: MDACC (2017-2021) [Kuerer Lanc Onc '22]: Phase II. NAC→ If no tumor on bx, definitive RT. TBL QS: In this small trial of a highly select group of patients with a pCR to neoadjuvant systemic therapy, adjuvant radiation alone and omission of surgery results in a low risk of short-term recurrence. 58 patients consented, but 50 participated. Aged ≥ 40y with TNBC or HER2+. Unicentric cT1-2N0-1M0. Residual breast lesion < 2 cm on imaging after NAC. Patients had one biopsy (minimum of 12 cores) obtained by image guided vacuum assisted core biopsy. If no invasive or in situ disease was identified, breast surgery was omitted and patients underwent standard WBI (40/15 or 50/25 plus a 14/7 boost). MFU 26 mo. pCR was identified in 62%. No IBTR was identified in all 31 patients.

heading: Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy
full_text: In general, use an anthracycline regimen and taxane, but may substitute docetaxel for doxorubicin if contraindication. Risk of LR is determined by both pretreatment stage and residual dz after chemo. NAC does NOT improve OS, but can convert from TM to BCS in 20-30% of pts [EBCTCG]. Consider adjuvant capecitabine for HER2- w residual dz after NAC (5y OS improved ~5%; 10% for TNBC) [CREATE-X]. Consider adjuvant TDM-1 for HER2+ w residual dz after NAC (3y DFS improved by 10%) [KATHERINE]. Consider NAC for cN2a (fixed axillary LN), major skin involvement (T4b-4d), ± chest wall invasion. Don’t offer NAC if unable to ID the extent of invasive disease clearly or if not palpable / clinically accessible. May use if pregnant and unable to undergo surgery. Use non-taxane, CAF most commonly. Previously, pCR for all-comers was ~30%. Recall: Around 1/3 of pts with cCR have residual dz. Proven in AC/T, Epirubicin/paclitaxel, CMF. ddAC q2w x4c→ paclitaxel q1w x12c is a common NAC regimen. Response: Basal > Her2/neu > luminal A/B. Diminished response noted in ER+, low-grade or ILC. pCR associated with improvements in DFS [HR 0.48] and OS [HR 0.48]. pCR up to 60% for HER2+ treated with trastuzumab/pertuzumab [TRYPHAENA]. TC-HP (Carboplatin) is the most common contemporary NAC for HER2+ breast cancer [KRISTINE]. pCR up to 60% if TN. Carboplatin increases pCR in TN disease [BrighTNess]. pCR according to breast cancer subtype [Swisher ASO '16]: HR-/Her2+ most likely to achieve pCR; pCR most prognostic for 5y LRRFS in TNBC. Notably a regimen that improves PCR does not reliably improve OS. See the [Predictors of LR after NAC] section for more. Great strides have been made in TNBC and TPBC - as of 2020, pCR is up to 60% in both subsets. Ensure addition of carboplatin to NAC regimens for TNBC [BrighTNess] and HER2 positive [KRISTINE] disease for maximum response. pCR is a strong predictor of outcomes in TNBC [Liedtke JCO '08]. 751 pts. 2005-2012. All BCT after NAC. All HER2+ received trastuzumab. MFU nearly 5y. pCR 5y LRRFS HR+ Her2- (n=369) 16.5% 97.2% HR+ Her2+ (n=105) 45.7% 96.1% HR-  Her2+ (n=58) 72.4%. 94.4% TNBC (n=219) 42.0% 93.4% p<0.001 p=0.44 5y LRR-free survival ~95%. 5y LRR-free survival for HR-/HER2+ ± pCR of 87→ 97% (p=0.11). 5y LRR-free survival for TNBC ± pCR of 90→ 99% (p=0.007) On MVA, TNBC, clinical stage III disease and failure to experience pCR were associated with LRR. pCR according to breast cancer subtype [Samiei JAMA Surg '21]: Lum A vs. Lum B vs. TNBC vs. HR-/HER2+. QS pCR 13→ 35→ 48→ 59%. pCR appears increased for Lum B pts with sperm-associated antigen 5 (SPAG5) QS [Abdel-Fatah JAMA Netw Open '20]. Residual cancer burden (RCB) after NAC (1994-2019) [Yau Lanc Onc '21]: TBL QS: Residual cancer burden (RCB) provides important prognostic information for patients with breast cancer who don’t achieve a pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. See I-SPY2 data for residual cancer burden. RoR Participant level data from 5,161 patients treated with NAC. Median 49y. HR+/HER2- (38%). HER2+ (28%; HR+ 60%, HR- 40%). TNBC (34%). RCB-0 (33%). RCB-1 (13%). RCB-2 (39%). RCB-3 (16%). MFU 56 mo. RCB was prognostic within each breast cancer subtype, with higher RCB score significantly associated with worse EFS. The univariable HR associated with one unit increase in RCB ranged from 1.55 (95% CI 1.41-1.71) for HR+, HER2- patients to 2.16 (95% CI 1.79-2.61) for HR-, HER2+ patients. RCB remained prognostic for EFS in MVA models adjusted for age, grade, T category, and nodal status at baseline. The aHR ranged from 1.52 (95% CI 1.36-1.69) in the HR+, HER2- group to 2.09 (1.73-2.53) for HR-, HER2+ patients.

heading: Neoadjuvant vs. Adjuvant chemo
heading_path: Neoadjuvant Therapy > Neoadjuvant vs. Adjuvant chemo
full_text: There is no difference in DMFS and BCM for neoadjuvant versus adjuvant chemotherapy [EBCTCG]. There appears to be more LRR with NAC, which is most pronounced in trials that omitted surgery in the event of good response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. However, per NCCN 2022: "These trials [EBCTCG] delivered chemo that are no longer standard, did not include targeted therapies, did not use modern imaging techniques, and/or used non-standard locoregional management." NAC does NOT improve OS, but can convert from TM to BCS in 20-30% of pts. Stage matched yp to p (without NAC) has higher LRR in the former. NSABP B-18 [Flowchart, Fisher JCO '97, Wolmark JNCI '01, Rastogi JCO '08]: AC x4 adjuvant vs. neoadjuvant. See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. Neoadjuvant chemo has equivalent DFS/OS and may convert to BCS. Response predicts survival. There is controversy on how to assess axillary response to NAC [SENTINA, Z1071]. 1,523 pts. Operable cT1-3N0-1, palpable and non-fixed. Majority ≤ T2, cN0. Adriamycin 60, cyclophosphamide 600 q3w x4c WBRT only for BCS, no RT if MRM. 66% in each arm thought to be BCS candidates. BCS 60→ 67% and pN+ 57→ 41%. ORR 79%. Total pCR 13%. Nodal pCR 57→ 41%. Decrease in nodal positivity led to SLNB studies after NAC. Equivalent 9y OS. Around 27% conversion rate to BCS. 9y OS for no response / PR / CR of 65→ 67→ 78%. Trend towards DFS (HR 0.85, p = 0.09) and OS (HR 0.81, p = 0.06) advantage for women < 50y. NSABP B-27 [Flowchart, Bear JCO '03, Rastogi ‘08]: 3 arm: Neo AC→ ± T Neo/Adj (Docetaxel) + Tamox 20mg x5y. See the [Overview of NSABP Studies] section for more. pCR doubled with docetaxel! Yet, BCT rates remained the same (~63%). The addition of T to AC does not impact DFS or OS. This questions the utility of pCR’s ability to predict more valuable clinical outcomes. 2,411 pts. Operable, palpable cT1-3N0-1. NAC AC ± T pre or post surgery (3 arms). Adriamycin 60, cyclophosphamide 600 q3w x4c, docetaxel 100 q3w x4c. WBRT only for BCS, no RT if MRM. Response 85→ 91%. pCR 14→ 26% (cCR 40→ 64%). G4 toxicity 10→ 23%. BCT ~62%. 5y DFS ~70%. ~OS. EORTC 10902 [Hage JCO '01]: 4FEC neo vs. adjuvant. 698 pts. T1c-4bN0-1. Rate of BCS 22→ 35%. ~10y LRR, PFS, OS. MDACC (1974-1998) [Buchholz IJROBP '02]: Retro. NAC vs. Adjuvant chemo. Stage-matched yp has a higher LRR. Recall: NAC were at a higher clinical stage initially. 150 NAC pts vs. 1,031 pts who underwent TM and adjuvant chemo without RT. No HER2 performed. 5y LRR 27→ 15% for all comers, including yp matched to p staging. LRR among ypT1-2y pN1 patients of initial T1-2 / T3-4 of 4→ 46%.

heading: Neoadjuvant Endocrine Therapy
full_text: The Landmark Series: Neoadjuvant Endocrine Therapy (NET) for Breast Ca [Weiss, King and Mittendorf ASO '20]. Clinical response to NAC for HER2+ or TNBC is generally robust, while response for HR+ is less impressive. NET appears to have similar ORR (~66%) and pCR (~5%) as NAC [Semiglazov Cancer '07]. Pts with high Allred scores (Percent/intensity of ER staining on IHC) may have higher response [Harvey JCO '99]. Letrozole is superior to tamoxifen as NET for postmenopausal ER+ women [P024 Eiermann Ann Onc '01]. Anastrozole may increase eligibility for BCS more commonly than tamoxifen [IMPACT Smith JCO '05], and also appears to suppress IHC staining for Ki-67 at two weeks as compared to tamoxifen [Dowsett Clin Ca Res '05]. However, ORR was similar across groups (~37% for tamoxifen vs. anastrozole vs. both). Anastrozole has a similar ORR as tamoxifen (~37%), but axillary downstaging favored anastrozole [PROACT Cataliotti Cancer '06]. Preoperative endocrine prognostic index (PEPI) score: Developed from P024 and validated in samples from IMPACT. Evaluates pT, pN, post-treatment Ki-67, and ER status and was prognostic for RFS with PEPI 0 (T1-2N0, Ki67 < 2.7% and maintained ER expression as Allred 3-8 after treatment) having an excellent RFS [Ellis JNCI '08]. ACOSOG Z1031 [Hunt ASO '23] enrolled postmenopausal ER+ patients with Allred 6-8, cT2-4N0-3, palpable tumors at least 2 cm in size and randomized to 16-18w of exemestane, letrozole or anastrozole. PAM50, Ki-67 and post-treatment PEPI scores were determined. Clinical response ~67%, with letrozole and anastrozole trending better. pCR 1%. Around half of patients deemed mastectomy only underwent BCS. Mean percent change in Ki67 was ~80%. PEPI 0 in ~16%, although luminal A patients were twice as likely to have PEPI score of 0 [Ellis JCO '11]. Cohort B looked at biopsy after 2-4 weeks, and patients with Ki-67 > 10% (20%) were switched to NAC. Only 6% of this group had pCR. Among patients who continued NET and calculated PEPI score, 4% (n=4/119) with PEPI 0 recurred, while 14% (n=49/341) of PEPI > 0 recurred [Ellis JCO '17]. ALTERNATE is studying the Ki67 triage approach and ability of modified PEPI score (which excludes ER status) to predict RFS. If Ki-67 > 10% at week 4 or 12, then NAC [Suman Chin Clin Onc '16].
