Stratified by surgery (BCS/MRM), ER status (+/-), HER2 (+/-), adjuvant chemo (Y/N), presence or absenceabscence of pCR in breast (Y/N). Age ≤ 39y (15%), 40-49 (25%), 50-59 (33%). TN (23%). HER2+/HR- (25%), HER2+/HR+ (32%). pCR breast (78%). TM (42%). BCS (58%). SLNB (55%). ALND (44%). MFU 60 mo. Example constraints: MHD ≤ 4 Gy, Ipsi lung V20 < 30%, Contra breast V3 ≤ 5%. Only allows CW boost if SM ≤ 2 mm. CW CTV: Skin ant to post aspects of ribs (exclude heart and lung). Includes clinically detected post op changes, scar, estimates of extent of previous breast (exclude sternum). Exclude axilla deep to pec major. CW PTV: CW CTV + 7mm, exclude heart, do not cross midline. CW PTV eval: CW PTV skin-3mm, posterior surface of ribs (excluding lung and heart). IMN CTV: IMN vessels in the first 3 intercostal spaces. (RTOG sup aspect of 1 rib to sup aspect of 4th rib). IMN PTV: IMN CTV + 5mm sup, inf, medially, laterally. No expansion post or ant. Do not extend into the sternum medially. SCLV CTV: Inf extent of cricoid to inf extent of clav head. Medially exclude thyroid, trach, esoph.  Lateral edge of SCM superiorly and clavicle inferiorly. SCLV PTV: SCLV CTV + 5mm, exclude thyroid, trach, esoph, lung. Ax CTV: If prior ax dissection, then just include undissected ax levels 1-3 (usually part of 2-3).  If only SLNBx then include ax levels 1-3 per RTOG Consensus. Ax PTV: Ax CTV + 5mm, exclude lung. 5y BC-RFI ~92→ 93% (HR 0.88, 95CI 0.60-1.28). 5y LR-RFI ~99% (HR 0.57, 95CI 0.21-1.54). 5y DM-RFI (HR1.00, 95CI 0.67-1.51). 5y OS ~94% (HR 1.12, 95CI 0.75-1.68). Preplanned analysis: There were no differences in BC-RFI among stratification (type of surgery, HR status, HER2 status, pCR in breast, or use of adjuvant chemo). Exploratory analysis: Suggestion of BC-RFI improved with no RNI better in TNBC (HR 2.3, 95CI 1.00-5.25). No difference in ALND or SLNB alone. G3 AE ~0.1→ 0.5%.

heading: Recurrent Breast Cancer
full_text: See the [Metastatic Breast Cancer] section. Multi-D Management of Recurrent Breast Cancer [Buchholz, Ali and Hunt JCO '20]. See the [Radiation PBI] and [General Reirradiation] section. Time between true recurrence and new primary is different: 33 mo and 55 mo, respectively [Needs source]. Long term control of locally recurrent disease in 45-70% of patients. DEGRO Guidelines for RT of locoregional breast cancer recurrences [Harms STO '16]: Isolated IBTR < 2-3 cm, age ≥ 50y, long interval between primary treatment and recurrence. CALOR (2003-2010) [Aebi Lancet '15, Wapnir JCO '18]: iLRR surgically excised ± Chemotherapy.Chemotherapy improves DFS for ER(-) locally recurrent breast cancer. 162 pts. Completely excised iLRR. 58 ER-, 104 ER+. HER2 therapy optional. MFU 9y. RT mandated for microscopically involved margins. 5y OS 76→ 88%. 5y DFS 57→ 69%. 10y DFS for ER(-) tumors of 34→ 70%. 10y OS ~53→ 73%. 10y DFS for ER(+) tumors of ~59→ 50% (p=0.13). 10y OS ~66→ 76%. Final analysis demonstrated benefit in ER(-) but no benefit for ER(+). See [RTOG 10-14] in the re-irradiation PBI section. 45/30 BID is a common re-irradiation scheme. Mayo (1999-2019) [Fattahi ARO '22]: Reirradiation to the breast. TBLQS: Reirradiation for resected recurrent breast cancer is tolerable and can achieve excellent local control. 72 patients underwent re-RT. MFU 22 mo. Median prior RT dose 60 Gy (IQR 50-60.4 Gy), re-RT dose 45 Gy (IQR 40-50 Gy), cumulative dose 103.5 Gy-2 (IQR 95-110 Gy-2). MTT re-RT 73 mo (IQR 29-129 mo). Gross residual at time of re-RT in 47% (n=34). Curative (61%) and palliative (39%). Photons ± electrons (72%) and protons (28%). G3 toxicity in 13% (10% acute, 3% late skin necrosis). MTT re-RT was significantly associated with development of G3 toxicity. Among patients treated with curative intent without gross disease, 2y LRRFS 75%. 2y OS 66%. 2y DMFS was 59% among all curative intent patients. Switzerland [Datta IJROBP '16]: Hyperthermia (HT) meta-analysis. Size of tumors not well described in most publications. Some tumors were breast, and not all were superficial. One study demonstrated increased CR with size ≤ 6 cc. Hyperthermia given by microwaves or RFA to 8-2450 MHz. 2210 pts. 31 articles with 8 RCTs and 26 single arm reports. Median 7 hyperthermia sessions biw. Average temperature 42.5C, mean duration 54 min, median interval to treatment 55 mo, mean RT dose 38.2 Gy. Hyperthermia is usually given after RT. CR for RT ± hyperthermia of 38→ 60%. CR of 67% in patients previously irradiated. Acute G3/4 toxicity 14% with RT/HT. Late G3/4 toxicity 5% with RT/HT. Multi-institutional review of repeat irradiation of the chest wall and breast (1993-2005) [Wahl IJROBP '08]: 81 pts. Median pRT 60 Gy, median re-RT 48 Gy. Median total RT dose 106 Gy. MFU 1y. Second RT course BID (20%), RT/HT (50%), concurrent chemo (50%). Late G3-4 in 5% (n=4). Overall complete response rate 57%. No repeat RT parameters were associated with improved CR. CR for RT ± HT of ~39→ 67% (p=0.08). 1y local DFS for ± gross disease of 53→ 100%. Ohio State [Bazan ASTRO '18]: Retro. IMRT/VMAT 45/30 (n=12). 28 pts. 18 iLRR, 10 LRR + DM. Median pRT 50.4 Gy. Half RNI. 11% IMN RT. 11 pts rec'd concurrent chemo. Curative intent to 22/28 patients, including 3 with high cervical nodes and 1 with mediastinal disease. 2014-2017. MFU 1y. MTT re-irradiation 5 years. Median re-RT dose was 45 Gy in 2 Gy fractions, 50% received a boost to median total re-RT dose of 60 Gy. G3+ esophagitis in 1 pt, 45/30 BID with 15/10 BID boost to mediastinal disease. G3+ wound dehiscence in 1 pt 3 mo after re-RT. 1y FFDM 50%. Reirradiation for locally recurrent breast cancer [Nader Marta Breast '17]: Mastectomy is standard of care for local control in patients with IBTR, although BCS followed by PBI can be offered in a subset of patients: IBTR ≤ 3 cm and ≤ 3 LN without ECE (90% ≤ 2 cm, all cN0), Local excision or lumpectomy alone is associated with high recurrence rates of 20-40%. Local excision for CW relapse is associated with high recurrence rates of ≥ 50%. Completion mastectomy is associated with local control rates ≥ 50%. [RTOG 10-14] demonstrated BCS with repeat 45/30 has 5y IBTR of only 5%. Brachytherapy has plenty of evidence. Re-RT dose of 30 Gy or 45-50 Gy with suggestion of 50 Gy having better local control though all regimens had ≥ 75% local control. Only 10% experienced G3 toxicity. G2-3 toxicity for cumulative breast dose ± 100 Gy of 4→ 33%. G2-3 toxicity for brachytherapy dose ± 45 Gy of 14→ 36%. Reirradiation and hyperthermia appear promising. Mayo Reirradiation for Locoregional Recurrent Breast Cancer (1999-2019) [Fattahi ARO '21]: Retro. Disease control and survival are promising among curative intent pts without gross disease. 72 pts. MFU 22 mo. Gross residual in 47% (n=34). Curative (61%). Palliative (39%). Vast majority re-RT qday. Median prior RT 60 Gy, re-RT 45 Gy (IQR 40-50 Gy), cumulative dose 103.54 Gy2 (IQR 95-109 Gy2). MTT Re-RT 6y (IQR 29-129 mo). G3 AE in 13% (10% acute skin toxicity, 3% late skin necrosis). Time between RT and re-RT fields were significantly associated with G3 toxicity at any point. Proton therapy conferred a dosimetric advantage without difference in toxicity. 2y LRFS 75%. 2y OS 66%. 2y LRFS among curative intent patients without gross disease 93%.

heading: Metastatic Breast Cancer
full_text: ASCO Rapid Recommendation Update: Chemo and Targeted therapy for HER2- metastatic breast cancer that is either endocrine-pretreated or hormone receptor negative [Moy JCO '22] [DESTINY-Breast 04] defined Low expression of HER2 defined as a score of 1+ on IHC or 2+ with negative FISH. Patients with HER2 IHC 1+ or 2+ and ISH-negative metastatic breast cancer who have received at least one prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, and if receptor-positive are refractory to endocrine therapy, should be offered treatment with trastuzumab deruxtecan. ASCO Guideline: Systemic Tx for Pts w Advanced HER2+ Breast Cancer June 25, 2018 RoR HER2 therapy for all advanced breast cancer, except those with CHF or significantly compromised LVEF. Trastuzumab, pertuzumab and taxane are first line, while trastuzumab emtansine second line. Third line should offer other HER2 combinations or trastuzumab emtansine and may offer pertuzumab (if not previously given). Optimal duration of chemotherapy is 4-6 months or until maximum response, depending on toxicity and FFP. HER2 may continue until time of progression or unacceptable toxicities. Triple positive BrCa may receive standard first line therapy, or endocrine ± HER2 for selected pts. ASCO Guideline: Recommendations on Dz Mgmt for Pts w Advanced HER2+ BrCa and Brain Mets May 31, 2022 RoR Clinicians should have a low threshold for MRI of the brain due to high incidence of [brain mets] for HER2+. TNBC appears to have [identical rates] of brain metastasis as HER2(+) HR(-). ASCO Guideline: Endocrine Therapy for HR+ Metastatic Breast Cancer May 23, 2016 Sequential hormones preferred. Except in cases of immediately life-threatening dz, hormone therapy, alone or in combo, should be used for initial tx. Consider ovarian suppression or ablation in premenopausal women. Postmenopausal women favor AIs over endocrine therapy, with or without CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib. As 2nd line tx, fulvestrant should be administered at 500 mg w loading schedule, may be given with palbociclib. Mammalian targets of rapamycin inhibitor everolimus may be administered with exemestane whose dz progresses while receiving non-steroidal AIs. Among TPBC, HER2 along with AI can be effective for those who are not chemo candidates. ASCO Guideline: Use of Biomarkers to Guide Decisions on Systemic Tx for Metastatic Breast Cancer July 20, 2015 Accessible mets should be biopsied and HR/HER2 assessment offered, but evidence is lacking if switching tx on the basis of change in receptor status affects clinical outcomes. There is a discordance between primary and metastatic tumor receptor status, and the latter favored to direct care. Markers such as CEA, CA 15-3 and CA 27-29 may be used as adjunctive assessments, but never alone. No role for tumor re-biopsy or use of CTC markers as there is an absence of studies looking into clinical utility. ASCO Guideline: Role of Bone-Modifying Agents in Metastatic Breast Cancer Update October 16, 2017 See the [EBCTCG Bisphosphonates] report. Bone mets pts should receive denosumab 120 mg SQ q4w, pamidronate 90 IV q3-4w or zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q12w or q3-4w. Analgesic effects of BMAs are modest, but should not be used alone for bone pain. There is no evidence to support BMA over another. See the [Recurrent Breast Cancer] section and Instant.Oncology: [Metastatic Breast Cancer Chemo based on subtype]. Chemo in Metastatic disease Failure to achieve tumor response to 3 sequential chemo regimens or ECOG 3 is indication for supportive care only. Eribulin: For pts who have received 2 previous CTX regimens for tx of mets (anthracycline + taxane). When compared to capecitabine, best with HER2- or TNBC. Ixabepilone: epothilone B analogue. Okay as a last resort. Causes neuropathy and neutropenia. Combinations: Bevacizumab may ↑ PFS, appearing to be greatest in combination with paclitaxel. Resistance to endocrine therapy with HR+ disease is frequent. One mechanism of resistance to endocrine therapy is activation of rapamycin (mTOR) signal pathway. Tamoxifen + everolimus increases median time to progression. Even if ER/PR-, still try endocrine therapy, esp when localized to bone or soft tissue tissue only or with asymptomatic visceral disease. HRQoL was worse at 18 mo in the LRT, but no difference was observed at time points 6 or 30 mo. Israel (2006-2016) [Jacobson Sci Rep '21]: Retro. Palliative RT for symptomatic advanced breast cancer 53 patients with metastatic breast cancer with skin invasion or ulceration/mass forming who received palliative RT to the breast with a minimum follow up of 2 months after RT. MTT radiation from diagnosis of 23 months (range 0-72 months). Prior breast RT in 17% (n=9). Mean breast tumor size 6.3 cm (min-max 2-35 cm). Tumors larger than 9 cm in 17% (n=9). MFU 15 mo (min-max 2-94 mo). RT: Mostly photons. 1 cm bolus utilized. Nine patients received single fraction RT (8/1), while fractionated regimens included 45/15, 39/13, and 50/25. Of the nine patients who received single fraction RT, 4 required reirradiation and received another fraction of 8 Gy in 1 fraction, median time to re-RT of 2 months (min max 0.5-9 months). Of the 44 patients who received multi-fraction RT, 18% (n=8) required reirradiation at a median 13.5 months (min-max 1-36 months). New Delhi [K.P. ASTRO '20]: 40/5 q1w vs. 24/3 q1w. 24/3 q1w is safe and feasible with lesser side effects without compromise in response compared to 40/5 q1w for advanced/fungating breast lesions. 37 pts with large fungating tumors (9 inoperable, 28 metastatic). MFU 10 mo. Median size of the breast lesion of 240cc (25-2160cc), median largest dimension 7 cm (3.3-15cm). 17 pts had skin lesions: 10 extensive Peau d'orange, 8 ulceration, and 6 satellite lesions. 13 patients succumbed to death before 6 mo of follow up. "Progression" ~15%. G2 dermatitis of ~42→ 31% (p=0.07). G3 dermatitis of ~8→ 0% (p=0.07). G4 dermatitis of ~4→ 0% (p=0.07). Fair cosmesis ~21→ 0%. Poor cosmesis ~4→ 0% (p=0.06). Stony Brook [Zabrocka IJROBP '23]: Retro. 40/5 qod. 21 non-surgical candidates (10 metastatic, 11 stage IA-IIIC) who received 23 SBRT to primary breast cancer. Median pre-SBRT lesion size 3.1 cm (0.5-14.5) and 32.4 cc (12-522). MFU 15 mo. Initial post-treatment imaging performed at median 4 mo post SBRT demonstrated median decreased index lesion size of 21% and SUV reduction of 65%. Second follow up scans at median 8 mo post-SBRT showed 62% median reduction of lesion size and SUV reduction of 88%. 6 mo LC 100%. 3y LC 93%. Local progression occurred in 1 case 9.6 mo after SBRT, following an initial response. Regional progression in 17% (n=4) at a median 19 mo post-SBRT. DM in 35% (n=6) at median 3 mo. 1y OS 70%. 3y OS 64%. Acute G1 / G2 / G3 toxicity of 48→ 4→ 9%. G4 toxicity 0%. FALCON [Robertson Lancet '16]: Anastrozole vs. fulvestrant. Fulvestrant is at least as effective as anastrozole in patients who progressed on tamoxifen. 524 pts. 2012-2014. Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer. MPFS 14→ 17 mo. Arthralgia 10→ 17%, hot flashes ~10%. Discontinuation due to AE in ~5%. FACT [Bergh JCO '12] and SoFEA [Johnston Lanc Onc '13] demonstrated anastrozole ± fulvestrant were no different, while S0226 [Mehta NEJM '19] demonstrated marginal prolongation of overall survival when fulvestrant was added to anastrozole. Statins attenuate outgrowth of breast cancer metastases [Beckwitt BJC ‘18]: Hypothesis generating, but statins appear to block metastatic tumor outgrowth in a 3D ex vivo system and should be considered for use as long-term adjuvant drugs to delay clinical emergence and decrease mortality in breast (and potentially lung) cancer patients.

full_text: EA2108 and RWD: A Cautionary Tale in Stage IV Breast Cancer [Boughey ASO '22]. Treatment of primary studies (n=5): Deferred surgery: Tata Memorial (mostly initially unresectable) and E2108 required at least stable disease on induction chemotherapy before randomization. No benefit in PFS or OS with deferred surgical resection. However, PRIM-BC suggests LR-PFS benefit with long term follow up. Upfront surgery: ABSCG-28 and MF 07-01. No benefit in PFS or OS with ABSCG-28 (closed early due to poor accrual). There was an OS benefit in MF 07-01, especially for patients with solitary bone metastases, ER+, HER2+, or < 55y. Tata Memorial (2005-2013) [Badwe Lancet '15]: Observation vs. delayed LRT to primary and axillary lymph nodes. 🐦Local treatment of primary tumors in initially unresectable metastatic breast cancer patients who received induction chemo (96%) did not improve overall survival. Low use of taxane and HER2-directed therapies. 350 pts. Metastatic breast cancer. Low volume (0-3 metastases) in 25%. SM+ not reported. Chemo prior to randomization if unresectable (96%) who were randomized if PR after 6-8c. Initially polymetastatic with >50% tumor volume decrease after induction chemotherapy. Involvement of no more than two visceral organs. MFU 2y. In the LRT arm, 72% mastectomy and 23% BCS + ALN dissection. RT per institutional guidelines. No HER2 directed therapy. MRM: 45/20 if initial T3, T4 or N+. BCT: WBI 45-50Gy + 15 Gy boost. 69% CW/breast and SCV fossa, 11% CW alone, 5% no RT, 16% unknown RT. MS ~20 mo. 2y OS ~43→ 42%. Distant PFS 20→ 11 mo. LR PFS 18.2→ NR. Low volume (≤ 3 metastases) OS HR 1.16 (0.69-1.95) Only 10% (n=18/177) had palliative treatment to the primary tumor for symptoms or progression in the control arm. Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram. E2108 (2011-2015) [Khan ASCO ‘20, JCO '22]: Systemic treatment ± delayed locoregional therapy (Surgery ± RT).🐦 [Plenary Session 2.55]: This is the last nail in the coffin for aggressive local therapy in metastatic breast cancer. EA2108 and RWD: A Cautionary Tale in Stage IV Breast Cancer [Boughey ASO '22]. Locoregional therapy does not improve OS or QoL for patients with de novo MBC [Dulaney and Dover PROshot '22]. Caveat: Treatment of the primary in metastatic cancer has a suggested OS benefit for Prostate cancer with low-volume disease. RoR Importantly, E2108 does not tease out the volume of disease. The Betting Line QS: Surgery and/or radiation after response to initial chemotherapy will improve overall survival for women with de novo metastatic breast cancer and resectable primary disease—but this may be driven by certain receptor subtypes. TBL QS: We steered you wrong if you bet that locoregional therapy for women with stage IV breast cancer improves survival, but it could very well be due to lack of patient selection. TBL QS: Once again, metastatic breast cancer—particularly the “indolent” variety—appears prone to subclinical metastatic disease with trajectories uninfluenced by local therapy to visible mets. 256 pts. De novo stage IV breast cancer without progression on chemo x4-8 mo (66%). Resectable primary. T1-3N0-1 (51%).  HR+ (59%). TNBC (11%). HER2+ (30%). Oligometastatic (≤ 3 sites of lesions in a single organ site; 16%). SM+ (8%). MFU 5y. 3y OS ~68%. MS ~54 mo. 3y LRR (or LR progression) 40→ 16%. MS for oligometastatic disease (16%; ≤ 3 lesions in a single organ) HR 1.18 (95% CI 0.38-3.67). Solitary bone metastases not reported (see MF07-01 below). There was no benefit in OS in the oligometastatic subgroup (12% of patients). Among the 20 patients with TNBC (8%), survival was worse (HR 3.33) in the early local therapy arm. In the systemic therapy arm, 21% of patients eventually received either surgery or radiation during the course of the trial. JCOG 1017 / PRIM-BC [Shien BJC '25]: Phase III. Systemic treatment ± delayed locoregional therapy (Surgery ± RT) 570 patients randomized, 410 enrolled between 2011 and 2018 with de novo stage IV breast cancer without progression on systemic therapy according to HR and HER2 status for three months without disease progression and one or more measurable metastatic lesions diagnosed by CT or MRI at diagnosis and again after randomization. No brain metastases allowed. SM+ (13%, n=22/173), including 14 TM and 8 PM, with no re-excision or PORT to the chest wall. ER+ (72%). HER2+ (30%). TNBC (9%). Single organ metastatic site (60%). Liver metastases (22%). Bone-only metastases (~30%). MFU 60 mo. Surgery: Within 42 days after second registration. Prophylactic ALND and/or resection of adjacent organs are not allowed. Surgery was not performed in 14% due to patient preference (n=29/202). Failed to initiate planned systemic therapy after surgery in 3% (n=6/173). HR+ (regardless of HER2 status): tamoxifen 20 mg/body+goserelin 3.6 mg/body q4w if premenopausal, or letrozole 2.5 mg/body x4w if postmenopausal. HER2+: paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 d1,8,15 + trastuzumab 2mg/kg (d1,8,15,22) q4w or docetaxel 75 mg/m2 (d1) + trastuzumab 6 mg/kg (d1) + pertuzumab 420 mg/body (d1) q3w. HER2-: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 (d1, 8, 15) q4w. MS ~69→ 75 m (HR 0.86, 90CI 0.69-1.07). PTR was associated with improved OS on preplanned analysis in premenopausal patients (unstratified HR 0.54, 95CI 0.33-0.87) and those with single organ metastases (unstratified HR 0.71, 95CI 0.50-1.01). Premenopausal MS 65→ 93 mo (unstratified HR 0.54, 95CI 0.33-0.87). Single organ metastases MS ~77→ 95 mo (unstratified HR 0.71, 95CI 0.50-1.01). Positive surgical margins in 13% MS for SM+ / SM- of 61→ 95 mo (HR 1.97, 95CI 1.16-3.35). 3 months after randomization, no progression at metastatic sites 82→ 67%. LRFS 20→ 63 mo (HR 0.42, 95CI 0.33-0.53). PFS (HR 0.68, 95CI 0.56-0.84). Palliative treatment to the primary tumor for symptoms or progression in the control arm in 20% (n=40/205). G2+ postoperative complications 6%. G3+ postoperative complicaitons 1%. MF07-01 [Soran ASO '18, JACS '21]: Systemic treatment ± upfront locoregional therapy (Surgery ± RT).🐦 Perhaps an OS benefit in patients with solitary bone metastases per unplanned post-hoc analysis, but this trial moved the goalposts from the original 3y OS endpoint. Of note, every patient underwent an R0 resection (unlike the 20% reported on ABSCG-28 and 8% on E2108. Tata memorial did not report rates of positive margins). 274 patients with de novo metastatic breast cancer. In local therapy arm: BCS (26%), Mastectomy (74%), positive LN (89%), SM+ (0%). A third of patients had interventions to metastases. This trial was not balanced (e.g., solitary bone 24→ 34%, T4 27→ 17%, TNBC 17→ 7%, HR+ 72→ 86%). MFU 54.5 mo. MS 35→ 46 mo. 10y OS 5→ 19%. OS HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.59-0.86). Note: this trial did not meet its primary endpoint of 3y OS. Goalposts were moved to long-term differences past originally planned 3y OS, though differences in OS were significant at 5 years. 🐦 ER+ OS HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.46-0.91). HER2+ OS HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.45-0.91). Age < 55y OS HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.38-0.86). Solitary bone-only metastases OS HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.36-0.86). Solitary pulmonary/liver metastases OS HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.37-1.29). Palliative treatment to the primary tumor for symptoms or progression in the control arm in 9% (n=12/131). ABSCG-28 (2011-2015) [Fitzal Ann Surg '19]: Systemic treatment ± upfront locoregional therapy (Surgery ± RT).🐦 No OS benefit with upfront treatment of the primary tumor. No subgroup/low metastatic reporting. 20% positive margins. 90 of 254 planned patients with de novo metastatic breast cancer, stopped early due to poor recruitment. In local therapy arm: BCS (33%), Mastectomy (67%), positive LN (81%), SM+ (21%). Lum A (50%). Lum B (13%). TNBC (9%). HER2 (22%). A third of patients had interventions to metastases. MFU 37.5 mo. Patients in surgery arm had more cT3 (7→ 22%) and more cN2 (4→ 16%). MS 55→ 35 mo. Survival was worse in the surgery arm. OS HR 1.45 (95% CI 0.75-2.79)*. *Please note, HRs were flipped as surgery was control arm. Time to distant progression 29→ 14 months.

full_text: MSKCC (2008-2018) [Wijetunga Cancer Med '21]: Retro. TBL QS: Large retrospective data consistently draws more of a chronic, not rapidly fatal, disease picture for metastatic breast cancer, particularly when all sites are amenable to ablative radiation. 82 women receiving ablative RT to all extracranial mets. MFU 50 mo. MS 82 mo. 4y LC 82%. 8 out of 10 women experiencing further progression progressed at fewer than five sites. Italy (2015-2021) [Franceschini RTO '24]: Non-randomized Phase II. SBRT to oligometastatic medically inoperable liver/lung lesions. Very high rates of local control with no recorded G3+ toxicities, although optimal selection of patients is needed to improve survival and reduce rates of DM. 64 patients with 90 medically inoperable lung and liver oligometastases from breast cancer. Up to 4 liver/lung lesions allowed, maximum diameter < 5 cm. Extra-hepatic and extra-thoracic disease was allowed so long as stable or responding to systemic therapy. Luminal A (28%), Luminal B (28%), HER2 enriched (22%), TNBC (22%). Synchronous metastases (23%). Polymetastatic at onset of disease (92%). Induced oligometastases (67%). Repeat OMD (10%). Disease outside SBRT target(s) (36%). LC at 1 / 2y of 95→ 91%. Median LC was not reached. MS 17 mo. OS at 1 / 2 / 3y of 88→ 61→ 52%. MDMFS 8 mo. DMFS at 1 / 2 / 3y of 38→ 21→ 16%. On UVA, local response to SBRT was associated with OS, DMFS, and STFS. No G3+ toxicity recorded. Toronto (2011-2017) [Tan RTO '21]: Retro. TBL QS: Large retrospective data consistently draws more of a chronic, not rapidly fatal, disease picture for metastatic breast cancer, particularly when all sites are amenable to ablative radiation. 120 women receiving ablative radiation for all extracranial mets (not just oligo). MFU 15 mo. 2y LC 87%. 1y OS for ablative RT to new oligomets / oligoprogression / dominant disease only of 91→ 79→ 64%. The [CURB] study was a study of palliative standard of care ± SBRT to all progressive sites. This study included metastatic breast and metastatic NSCLC who received ≥ 1 line of systemic therapy with oligoprogressive lesions amenable to SBRT.  There was no difference in PFS oligoprogressive SBRT within the breast cancer cohort on this study. There was no upper limit of non-progressive lesions. Most patients had 2-5 oligoprogressive lesions on this study, and lower doses were utilized (e.g., half got 27-30/3). However, most progression (90%) in patients with breast cancer was at non-irradiated sites. MFU was only 12 months, perhaps differences will emerge with longer follow up. The [RADIANT] study was a study of metastatic GU, GI, and breast cancer patients who received systemic therapy for ≥ 3 months with radiographic oligoprogressive disease in ≤ 5 sites. The primary endpoint was change in systemic therapy. Most patients (80%) had 1 oligoprogressive lesion. Nearly half of the breast cancer cohort of patients had not changed systemic therapy by one year. NRG BR002 [Chmura ASCO '22, Protocol]: Phase II/III. Standard of care and tx of symptomatic mets vs. LCT. See NCTN Trial Portfolios by Disease Site: [Breast], [Future Directions] and [Constraints and Toxicity] section. TBL QS: Once again, metastatic breast cancer—particularly the “indolent” variety—appears prone to subclinical metastatic disease with trajectories uninfluenced by local therapy to visible mets. It is plausible that this trial closed too early to determine differences in outcomes for HR+ disease. See [MF 07-01], although a study of primary tumor resection, the curves separated after 3 years. 129 patients with metastatic breast cancer and ≤ 4 extracranial mets after ≤ 12 months of systemic therapy without progression. Phase III goal was for 360 patients, or phase IIr + 232 patients (closed early). Metachronous (80%). Solitary mets (60%). HR+/HER2- (79%). Amended in 2016 to pathologically confirmed metastatic breast cancer to ≤ 2 sites and < 12 mo of standard first line systemic therapy with controlled primary disease. For the phase IIR portion to proceed to phase III, target sample size of 128 pts for 92% power and 1-sided significance level = 0.15 to determine when adding MDT shows a signal for improved PFS (HR 0.55; mPFS 10.5→ 19 mo). Stratified by metastases (1 vs. >1), HR status (HR+ vs. HR-), HER2 status (Y/N), and chemotherapy for breast cancer (Y/N). MFU 30 mo. Nonosseous sites: 30/1 (28-30.3): Only single liver and peripheral lung. 45/3 (42.5-45.5): Preferred for peripheral lung, liver, and abdominal pelvic mets. 50/5 (48-50.5): Preferred for central lung, mediastinal/cervical lymph nodes. Osseous sites: 20/1 (14-20.2): Spinal mets. 30/3 (27-30.3): Non-spinal mets. 35/5 (30-35.4): Thoracic/Cervical spine. mPFS 23→ 20 mo. 2y PFS ~46%. 3y PFS ~33→ 38% (HR 0.92, 70% CI 0.71-1.17, p=0.36). 3y OS ~70%. First failures outside index area ~40%. LRP 29→ 7%. At MFU 30 mo, there was no signal for improved PFS or OS between arms. No subgroup showed benefit to MDT including those with single vs. multiple metastases or circulating tumor cell counts (0 vs ≥ 1). As such, the trial will not proceed to the phase III component. Grade 3 toxicity 5→ 10%. AVATAR (2020-2022) [David ASTRO '23]: Phase II. 20/1 or 24/2 to sites of oligoprogression. 🐦 32 patients with ER positive, HER2 negative oligoprogressive (1-5 sites) breast cancer who received first or second line systemic therapy in the metastatic setting with a CDK 4/6+AI for ≥ 6 months. 1 site (41%). 2 sites (31%). 3 sites (22%). Bone oligoprogression (71%). Nodal oligoprogression (18%). Goal to see if SBRT can delay a change in combination CDK4/6 +AI by 6 months in > 25% of patients. MFU 16 mo. At subsequent progression, further SABR was permitted to delay a change in systemic therapy. Nearly half of patients remained event free for 6 months. Median mPFS 10 mo with 46% remaining unchanged on systemic therapy for 12 mo. Median PFS was 5 mo with 33% (n=10/30) of progressions suitable for a second course of SBRT for oligoprogression to further delay systemic therapy change. EXTEND breast [Reddy IJROBP '24]: Phase II. SoC Systemic Therapy ± MDT. There was no benefit in PFS when MDT was added to SoC systemic therapy. However, this trial was limited by a heterogeneous and small sample size with overperformance of both treatment arms. 43 patients with oligometastatic (≤ 5 metastases amenable to MDT) breast cancer and ≤ 4 prior lines of systemic therapy. Nearly half had 1 or 2 lesions. De novo oligometastatic (40%, n=17; 11 out of 12 had the primary tumor treated with surgery and radiotherapy), but this included genuine OMD and inducible OMD. Three patients in the SoC therapy only arm were treated with radiation therapy directed to the primary site and regional nodal basins. HR+ (75%). TNBC (20%). Bone-only disease (37%). Designed to have 80% power to detect improvement in MPFS from 4 mo to 8.5 months in the combined-therapy arm by using a one-sided log rank test with type I error of 0.10. Stratified by number of lesions (1-2 vs. 3-5), number of prior lines of systemic therapy (0-1 vs. > 1), and hormone receptor status (TNBC vs. not TNBC). MFU 25 mo. MDT: delivered to 40 lesions, 37 lesions received RT (32 were SBRT) and 3 received MWA or RFA. SBRT (n=32): 16-18/1 (n=10), 20/1 (n=1), 27-30/3 (n=14), 50/4 (n=7). Dose escalated hypofractionated RT (n=3): 70/10 or 52.5/15. Conventional RT (n=2): 61.6/28 or 62/31. MWA or RFA (n=3). Treatment of Primary Tumor on MDT arm (n=10): Segmental mastectomy ± ALND (n=4), MRM/TM and axillary sampling (n=4), No surgery, RT alone 27/3 (n=1), ALND only (n=1). All patients who underwent surgery also received postoperative radiotherapy ranging from 50.4/28 to 66/33. Half of patients underwent primary tumor surgery on the MDT arm, whereas while primary tumor surgery was allowed on the SoC arm, the three patients who underwent primary tumor treatment on the SoC arm underwent radiotherapy directed to the primary site and regional lymphatics without surgery. Overall baseline clinical and stratification factors were well balanced, but patients in the MDT arm were older (median age 48→ 61.5y) and trend towards more primary disease present (29→ 50%). Notably, surgery and/or RT were permitted on the no MDT arm for patients with de novo metastatic presentation. Among the 40 evaluable patients, there were 5 deaths (3 in the MDT arm, 2 in the no MDT arm). MPFS ~25→ 16 mo (HR 0.91, 95CI 0.34-2.48). Local control rate for treated lesions in the MDT arm was 100%, and all progression events occurred at new distant anatomic sites. In the SoC arm, half of progression events occurred at index lesions, while the other half occurred at new anatomic sites. Time to new metastatic lesion ~16 mo→ NR. 2y estimate of time to subsequent line of systemic therapy of ~18→ 33% (p=0.80). Two G3 toxicities were observed in the MDT arm, one in the no MDT arm. SBRT for breast cancer oligomets [Viani RTO '21]: ± Oligometastatic directed therapy. TBL QS: Select patients who are eligible for metastasis-directed therapy for oligometastatic breast cancer have excellent local control and very low toxicity with SBRT, but we need randomized data to determine whether this changes disease trajectory. 10 studies with 467 patients and 653 treated metastases for studies treating patients with ≤ 5 metastases using ≥ 5 Gy per fraction with ≤ 10 fractions. RT: Very heterogeneous with schemes ranging from 20/1 to 75/3 to 50/10. BED10 ranged from 60-262 Gy, with median BED10 of 75 Gy. LC at 1 / 2y of 97→ 90%. OS at 1 / 2y of 93→ 81%. G2 toxicity 4%. G3 toxicity 0.7%. In the meta-regression analysis, only prospective design and bone-only metastases were significantly associated with better OS. 2y OS for HER2+ / HR+HER2- / TNBC was 100→ 86→ 32%. For local control, HR status was significantly associated on meta-regression analysis. Choroidal mets Optho exam, MRI brain and spine, consider bx and LP. EBRT 40/20, 45-50.4/25-28. HBB at canthus to protect lens/gland - posterior border is posterior globe. Plaque if <18x18 mm at base and < 1 cm deep: Rx 45 Gy to apex over 96h with I-125.

heading: Brain Metastases
heading_path: Metastatic Breast Cancer > Treatment of Metastases > Brain Metastases
full_text: Incidence of brain mets is highest in TNBC and HER2(+) disease [Darlix BJC '19]. Trastuzumab/Capecitabine + Tucatinib (HER2) appears to have 1y PFS of 25% for patients with brain mets who have progressed on the big HER2-three (Herceptin, Perjeta, Kadcyla) [HER2CLIMB]. CNS ORR for Capecitabine + Neratinib (HER2/erbB) appears to be around 50% if lapatinib-naive [TBCRC 022], while ~30% if ≥ 2 prior HER2/neu therapies [NALA trial]. For ER(+) disease, abemaciclib (CDK 4/6) appears to have an intracranial clinical benefit of around 25% [Anders JCO '19]. For TNBC, intracranial response for immunotherapy remains unknown [IMpassion130]. Palbociclib in progressive brain metastases [NCT02896335]. Abemaciclib in participants with breast cancer, NSCLC or melanoma [NCT02308020]. Molecular Subtypes and Brain Metastases [Darlix BJC ‘19]: Retro. HER2(-)HR(+) / TP / TN / HER2(+)HR(-). Highest incidence of BM for HER2(+), HR(-) or TNBC. HR(-) patients have the highest incidence of brain metastasis. HER2(+) patients have a median survival above one year in the setting of brain metastases. 16,701 pts with metastatic breast cancer. 2008-2014. MFU nearly 4y. CNS metastasis developed in 25%. Only 7% were metastatic to the brain at the time of diagnosis. Incidence in brain metastasis for HER2(-) / HER2(+) of 11→ 22%. Incidence in brain metastasis for HR(+) / HR(-) of 9→ 33%. Incidence in brain metastasis for TNBC 33%. De novo BM at the time of metastatic diagnosis of 4→ 9→ 13→ 17%. 1y BM after a metastatic diagnosis of 8→ 17→ 30→ 32%. 2y BM after a metastatic diagnosis of 14→ 29→ 45→ 49%. 4y BM after a metastatic diagnosis of 37→ 53→ 71→ 73%. Rates do not appear to decrease over time. MS 7→ 19→ 4 → 13 mo. Treatment of BM: Systemic treatment (60%), WBRT (45%), BSC only (15%), SRS (10%), Resection (2%). RTOG 1119 (2012-2019) [Kim ASTRO '20]: Phase II. WBRT (37.5/15) or SRS ± concurrent Lapatinib. The addition of lapatinib to WBRT/SRS did not improve 12w CR, but did trend towards improved 4w ORR. Commentary: This study allowed prior lapatinib, the effect of which may wean over time. Also, CNS response is potentially amplified with capecitabine, which is typically contraindicated with radiotherapy. 143 HER2+ breast cancer pts with ≥ 1 measurable unirradiated parenchymal brain mets (de novo or progressive after prior SRS or resection of 1-3 BM). 6 pts on each arm received SRS, the rest received WBRT. G3 AE 8→ 29%. G4 AE 0→ 6%. 12w CR ~6→ 0% (p=0.77). 4w ORR 42→ 56% (p=0.06).

heading_path: Metastatic Breast Cancer > Treatment of Metastases > Brain Metastases
full_text: HER2CLIMB [Murthy NEJM '19, Lin JCO '20, JAMA Onc '22]: Previously rec'd HP and T-DM1→ Trast/Capecitabine ± Tucatinib. [Plenary Session 2.56]: One hundred percent of patients had all three lines of prior therapy. Around 60% of patients had active (new or progressing) brain mets at the time of diagnosis, which were likely candidates for radiotherapy, including around 25% overall with known, untreated brain mets. We know trastuzumab or capecitabine will be unlikely to penetrate the BBB, while tucatinib is a small molecule. Did these patients visit with a thorough radiation oncologist prior to enrollment? No wonder the 1 year PFS in patients with brain mets was 0% in the control arm - many of these patients likely should have been irradiated. TBL QS: The addition of tucatinib to capecitabine and trastuzumab improves PFS and OS among patients who progress on the big HER2-three (i.e., Herceptin, Perjeta, and Kadcyla), including those with brain metastases. 612 HER2(+) metastatic pts. Brain metastasis in 50% (n=291). Excluded LMD. MFU 30 mo. Tucatinib is a highly selective oral HER2 TKI. Included patients with asymptomatic or previously treated brain metastasis. 1y PFS 12→ 33%. MPFS 6→ 8 mo. Brain mets cohort (n=291) [Lin JCO '20, JAMA Onc '22]: 60% with active (new/progressing) brain mets at enrollment. TBL QS: Tucatinib when combined with trastuzumab and capecitabine has significant intracranial activity for women with HER2+ brain met after prior HER2-targeted therapy. 1y PFS 0→ 24%. 1y CNS-PFS 0→ 40%. MCNS-PFS 4→ 10 mo. MIC-DOR 3→ 9 mo. MS 13→ 22 mo. In the subset of women with active brain mets, MS 12→ 21 mo. 1y OS 27→ 45%. MS 17→ 22 mo. One of the many interesting side effects of tucatinib is that it increases serum creatinine without affecting GFR. Something to ponder when ordering your surveillance imaging. NALA [Saura JCO '19, '20]: Capecitabine + (Lapatinib vs. Neratinib). The CNS ORR for lapatinib or neratinib + capecitabine in the setting of heavily pretreated HER2 therapy appears to be around 30%, while < 10% for either next-gen EGFR/HER2neu inhibitor alone. [Plenary Session 2.40]: Co-primary endpoint of p < 0.1 for PFS and < 0.4 for OS. Only 35% received HP→ T-DM1, which is the optimal regimen prior to enrollment. Therefore, most patients had weaker HER2 directed therapy before enrollment. The difference only separates after the median, and HRQoL is definitely not improved due to diarrhea. TBL QS: Neratinib is superior to lapatinib when paired with capecitabine for women with metastatic HER2+ breast cancer. 621 patients. Stage IV HER2+ metastatic breast cancer who had rec'd ≥ 2 prior HER2 directed therapies. Includes stable, asymptomatic CNS disease (16%). 6 mo PFS 29→ 47%. 12 mo PFS 15→ 38%. MPFS ~5.5→ 5.6 mo (p=0.059). 6 mo OS ~73→ 90%. 12 mo OS ~67→ 88%. MS ~19→ 21 mo (p=0.2). ORR in patients with measurable disease at screening of ~27→ 33%. Interventions for CNS disease 29→ 23%. Grade 3 diarrhea of 13→ 24%. TBCRC 022 [Freedman JCO '19]: Phase II. Capecitabine + Neratinib for brain metastasis. 49 Her2(+) pts, lapatinib naive (n=37) or lapatinib pre-treated (n=12). BM ≥ 1 cm with CNS progression after any prior CNS-directed therapy (WBRT, SRS, surgery, CNS-directed systemic therapy, or any combo). Neratinib 250 mg po qday, capecitabine 750 mg po BID 14/7. Primary endpoint: CNS ORR, requiring reduction of 50% or more of sum of largest CNS lesion volumes without progression of nontarget lesions, new lesions, escalating steroids progressive neuro symptoms, or non-CNS progression. CNS ORR nearly 50% for lapatinib-naive cohort, or 33% for lapatinib pretreated. MPFS 5.5 mo in lapatinib-naive cohort, 3 mo in lapatinib pretreated. MS ~14 mo. G3 diarrhea 29%. PATRICIA [Lin JCO '21]: Phase II. Pertuzumab + high-dose Trastuzumab (6 mg/kg weekly) until PD or toxicity. TBL QS: Despite a relatively low intracranial response rate (11%), most patients with CNS progression after prior radiation maintain stable intracranial disease for 6 months with pertuzumab and high dose trastuzumab. 39 patients with HER2+ brain mets and CNS progression despite prior RT. CNS ORR 11% (95% CI 3-25%) with 4 PR. Median DOR 4.6 mo. PERMEATE (2019-2020) [Yan Lanc Onc '22]: Phase II. Pyrotinib + Capecitabine. This is the first prospective study showing the activity and safety of pyrotinib plus capecitabine in patients with HER2+ breast cancer and brain metastases, especially in the RT-naive population. TBL QS: The CNS response rate for pyrotinib plus capecitabine is 74.6% for patients with radiation-naive brain metastases and 42.1% for progressing brain metastases after radiation. RT-naive HER2+ brain mets (cohort A; n=59, 74%) or progressive disease after radiotherapy (cohort B; n=19, 24%). Around 90% had prior exposure to trastuzumab. MFU 16 mo. Pyrotinib 400 mg qd. Capecitabine 1000mg/m2 BID x14d, 7d off q3w until PD or unacceptable toxicity. Intracranial ORR 75% in cohort A and 42% in cohort B. MDOR 12.5 mo in cohort A and 7.7 mo in cohort B. G3+ treatment-emergent AE of diarrhea in 22%. DEBBRAH [Perez-Garcia Neuro Onc '22]: Phase II. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). TBL QS: In this small study, T-DXd showed intracranial activity in patients with HER2+ breast cancer. 21 HER2+ patients with brain metastases (also includes HER2-low cohort, not reported here). Non-progressing BM after local therapy (n=8), asymptomatic untreated BMs (n=4), or progressing BMs after local therapy (n=9). 16w PFS in non-progressing BM after local therapy 88%. Intracranial ORR 50% in untreated BMs and 44% in progressing BMs after local therapy. Shanghai (2020-2022) [Yang JAMA Onc' 24]: Phase II. Pyrotinib, Capecitabine and brain RT. 40 ERBB2-positive metastatic breast cancer with brain metastases treated with WBRT (28%, n=11) or FSRT (73%, 32/4 in 20 patients, 24/3 in 6 patients, and 40/5 in 3 patients). MFU 17 mo. RT: Whole brain or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy. For patients with 1-4 metastases, fractionated SRS to a total dose of 24-40 Gy in 3-5 fractions (8 Gy/Fx) was delivered. For patients with 5-10 metastases, WBRT or FSRT was delivered. For > 10 mets, WBRT was delivered. Chemo: Pyrotinib (400 mg po qday) and capecitabine (1000 mg/m2, BID, on d1-14 of each 21 day cycle) was allowed to be initiated from the first day of RT to the 7th day after completion of radiotherapy, and continued until disease progression or unacceptable side effects. 1y CNS-PFS 75%. MCNS PFS 18 mo. 1y PFS 67%. MPFS 18 mo. CNR ORR 85% (n=34/40). Most common G3-4 AE diarrhea (8%). Asymptomatic radiation necrosis in 4 of 67 lesions (6%) treated with stereotactic fractionated radiotherapy. Most patients maintained neurocognitive function as evaluated by MMSE at different points. Metastatic ER+, HER2- breast cancer: CDK 4/6 and PI3K inhibitors in a nutshell A multitude of trials demonstrated ~10 mo PFS benefit with CDK 4/6 inhibitors for metastatic HR+ HER2- disease. The most recent trials [MONALEESA-3, 7] demonstrated an OS advantage for post or pre/peri-menopausal women with HR+ HER2- disease! As many as 40% of women with ER+, HER2- breast cancer harbor PIK3CA activating mutations. However, we should note that PIK3CA-mutations are a common mechanism of CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance - meaning these drugs could have important complementary roles. No data exists on combining the two agents together. For now, CDK 4/6 is the first line, while PI3K is the second line. TBL QS: Patients with advanced ER(+), HER2(-) breast cancer harboring PIK3CA-mutations have improved progression-free survival with the addition of a PI3K-inhibitor to endocrine therapy. HR+, HER2- metastatic postmenopausal breast cancer [Giuliano Lanc Onc '19]: Endocrine vs. chemotherapy.CDK 4/6 with hormone therapy appears to have the best PFS when compared to any chemo with or without targeted therapy. No chemotherapy regimen with or without targeted therapy is significantly better than the above regimen. HR+, HER2- metastatic breast cancer in women > 75y [Howie JCO '19]: PFS HR for CDK4/6 with AI of 0.49 in women age 75 or older. MPFS 14→ 31 mo. G3/4 AE for ± 75y of 73→ 89%. Patients > 75y experienced higher rates of toxicity, dose modifications, and a decrease from baseline QoL measures.

heading: CDK4/6 inhibitors
full_text: Instant.Oncology: [Metastatic Breast Cancer Chemo based on subtype]. Typically utilized in ER+, HER2- metastatic breast cancer. CDK 4/6 inhibitors: Palbociclib, Ribociclib, and Abemaciclib. [PALOMA-2, PALOMA-3, MONALEESA-2 QS [long term], MONARCH-3, Review of CDK4/6 inhibitors]. All of the above trials demonstrated a uniform 10 mo PFS benefit. Palbociclib + letrozole doubles PFS in ER+, HER2- disease compared to letrozole alone. Palbociclib may be used with letrozole or fulvestrant [PARSIFAL Llombart-Cussac ASCO ‘20] Neutropenia and leukopenia side effects. "Pending more data, concomitant delivery of RT and CDK 4/6i appears safe, particularly when limiting radiation dose to bone marrow" QS [Ratosa Clin Br Ca '20] Credit: Dr Lei Wang. Click image above or follow @instant.oncology on Instagram. PALOMA-3 [Cristofanilli Lanc Onc '16, Turner NEJM '18]: Fulvestrant ± palbociclib. See the Plenary Session commentary on MONALEESA 7 below. A higher percentage of patients received subsequent therapy on this trial than MONALEESA 7.TBL QS: The huge PFS advantage seen with CDK4/6 inhibition eventually translates to a proportional OS benefit, particularly among post-menopausal women and those with previous endocrine sensitivity. 521 mostly post-menopausal pts. Median age ~56. HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer with progression or relapse during previous endo treatment. MS ~28→ 35 mo (HR 0.81, p=0.09). HR fell short of "significant" as both survival times were relatively long. This difference became significant when removing patients previously insensitive to previous endocrine treatment (n=111) and especially pre-menopausal women (n=108). MONALEESA-3 [Slamon NEJM '19]: Fulvestrant ± ribociclib. TBL QS: Just like in MONALEESA-7, ribo again proves to significantly improve OS among women with metastatic ER(+), HER2(-) breast cancer...and that’s no easy feat. 736 pts. Postmenopausal women with HR(+), HER2(-) advanced breast cancer. MFU 3.5y. 3.5y OS 46→ 58%. MPFS 19→ 34 mo. G3/4 events primarily neutropenia (57%) and leukopenia (16%). MONALEESA-7 [Im NEJM '19]: Endocrine therapy ± ribociclib.[Plenary Session 1.67]: The very first CDK 4/6 inhibitor to demonstrate an OS benefit? This trial is contrasted with the lack in PALOMA-3 (above), which had more post-menopausal patients. Among patients who discontinued therapy, around 70% in MONALEESA 7 and 80% in PALOMA 3 received subsequent antineoplastic therapy, while around 15% in MONALEESA 7 and 35% in PALOMA 3 received prior antineoplastic therapy. The one trial which has a benefit (i.e., MONALEESA 7) has a lower use of prior and subsequent therapy. Perhaps women did not receive enough subsequent antineoplastic therapy after progression. Figure 2 demonstrates the only geographic region to benefit was Asia, with OS HR 0.4! All other regions NS. Is the use of subsequent therapy different in the Asian subset (i.e., is there less subsequent antineoplastic therapy)? TBL QS: In pre- or peri-menopausal women with advanced ER(+) HER2(-) breast cancer, the addition of ribociclib to initial endocrine therapy improves overall survival. 672 pre or peri-menopausal patients. Median age ~44. 70% received subsequent antineoplastic therapy. MFU 3y. Deaths 32→ 25%. MS 41→ NR. 42 mo OS 46→ 72% (HR 0.71). This is misleading, as there are only 7 events pulling the control line down (Fig 1A) MONARCH-2 [Sledge JAMA Onc '19]: Fulvestrant ± abemaciclib. TBL QS: CDK4/6 inhibition improves OS for women with advanced ER(+), HER2(-) breast cancer. 669 pts. HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer. MS 37→ 47 mo. Time to chemotherapy 22→ 50 mo. More pronounced effects in patients with visceral disease and primary resistance to primary endocrine tx. monarcHER [Tolaney Lanc Onc '20]: Phase II. Chemo + Trastuzumab vs. Trastuzumab + Abemaciclib ± fulvestrant. TBL QS: The combination of abemaciclib, fulvestrant, and trastuzumab may be a promising non-chemo treatment option in women with progressive TPBC after multiple lines of therapy. 237 patients. Unresectable, LA, recurrent, or metastatic who rec'd prior HER2. 2016-2018. MFU 19 mo. MPFS 6→ 6→ 8 mo. The addition of fulvestrant improved outcomes when given with abemaciclib.

heading: ESR1 mutations/Progression on CDK4/6
heading_path: Metastatic Breast Cancer > ESR1 mutations/Progression on CDK4/6
full_text: ESR1 encodes the gene for the most common ER isoform. Up to 40% of patients who progress on an aromatase inhibitor have mutations in ESR1 that can be detected by ctDNA. While resistant to AI therapy, these mutated ERs may still be sensitive to fulvestrant. EMERALD [Bidard JCO '22]: Phase III. SOC endocrine monotherapy vs. Elacestrant. TBL QS: Women with advanced hormone receptor positive (HR+) breast cancer who progress on endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibition, and chemo often exhibit endocrine resistance. Elacestrant is an oral, selective estrogen receptor degrader. In the randomized phase 3 EMERALD trial, patients with advanced, progressive HR+ breast cancer were randomized to continued endocrine monotherapy or elacestrant. Nearly half of patients (48%) had ESR1 mutations, which result in estrogen-independent ER-activation. Elacestrant reduced the risk of progression or death by 30% overall and 45% among those with ESR1 mutation. 477 breast cancer patients with pretreated ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer who had one-two lines of endocrine therapy, prior treatment with CDK4/6, and ≤ 1 chemotherapy. ESR1 mutation detected in 48% of patients. PFS was prolonged in all patients (HR 0.70) and in patients with ESR1mt (HR 0.55). Treatment related G3-4 AE leading to treatment discontinuation in 3→ 7%. Nausea of any grade 19→ 35%. PADA-1 [Bidard Lanc Onc '22]: Phase III. AI/Palbociclib vs. Fulvestrant/Palbociclib. TBL QS: In patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer receiving an AI and palbociclib, switching from the AI to fulvestrant upon a rising bESR1mut prolongs progression-free survival. 1017 women with advanced HR+ breast cancer were monitored for rising ESR1 mutations in the blood while on first line AI and palbociclib. Of these, 18% (n=172) had rising bESR1mt without clinical progression and were randomized to continue AI/Plabo or to switch to fulvestrant/palbo. Overall, 27% had a rising bESR1mt, but some were excluded due to synchronous disease progression. MPFS 6→ 12 mo. EMBER-3 [Jhaveri NEJM '24]: Phase III. Endocrine therapy vs. Imlunestrant ± Abemaciclib. Imlunestrant is a next-generation brain pentetrant oral selective ER degrader that delivers continuous ER inhibition, even in cancers with ESR1mt (ERα). 874 patients with ER positive, HER2 negative advanced breast cancer that recurred or progressed during or after AI therapy, administered alone or with a cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitor. Among 256 patients with ESR1mt MPFS for ± imlunestrant was 3.8→ 5.5 mo. Restricted mean survival time at 19 months for ± imlunestrant of 5→ 8 mo. Overall population MPFS for ± imlunestrant ~5.5 mo. Among 426 patients, MPFS for imlunestrant ± abemaciclib of 5.5→ 9.4 mo. G3+ for imlunestrant / standard therapy / imlunestrant+abemaciclib of ~17→ 21→ 49%.

heading: PI3K inhibitors
full_text: Instant.Oncology: [Metastatic Breast Cancer Chemo based on subtype]. More than 70% of breast cancer is ER+, and as many as 40% of women with ER+ HER2- breast cancer harbor [PIK3CA] α isoform activating mutations. SOLAR-1 [André NEJM '19, ESMO '20]: Fulvestrant ± PI3K inhibitor (Alpelisib).As recently pointed out by Vinay Prasad, a fair number of cancer drugs make it to market without facing what would be considered “the standard.” In this particular scenario, most advanced ER/PR+, HER2- patients nowadays get first-line endocrine therapy + CDK4/6-inhibition. So, how would alpelisib compare to the -ciclib’s? We’re not sure. However, we should note that PIK3CA-mutations are a common mechanism of CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance - meaning these drugs could have important complementary roles. TBL QS: Patients with advanced ER(+), HER2(-) breast cancer harboring PIK3CA-mutations have improved progression-free survival with the addition of a PI3K-inhibitor to endocrine therapy. 572 patients. Advanced ER+, HER2-. Stratified based on the presence of PIK3CA activating mutations. MFU 20 mo PIK3CAmt group (n=341): ORR 13→ 27%, MPFS 6→ 11 mo. MS ~31→ 39 mo (p=0.15). Appears to be most beneficial in patients with lung or liver disease. Alpelisib with hyperglycemia (G3+ in 2/3), rash, and diarrhea. BYLieve [Rugo ASCO ‘20]: Phase II. Fulvestrant + PI3K inhibitor (Alpelisib). 127 patients progressing on CDKi + AI. All had PI3K mutations. MFU 1y. 6 mo PFS 50%. Most frequent AEs include diarrhea (60%), hyperglycemia (58%), nausea, fatigue, decreased appetite, and rash. PAKT trial [Schmid JCO '19]: Phase II. Paclitaxel ± Capivasertib (AKT inhibitor). The PI3K/AKT signaling pathway is frequently activated in TNBC. Patients with activation of PI3K or AKT and/or deletions of PTEN have a more pronounced response. 140 pts. Untreated metastatic TNBC. MPFS 4→ 6 mo (p=0.06). MS 13→ 19 mo. In patients with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations (n=28), MPFS 4→ 9 mo. G3+ most common AE of diarrhea (1→ 13%). PARP inhibition in metastatic breast cancer BRCA mutations As a gross oversimplification, PARP repairs minor but frequent DNA damageQS. PARPi requires [BRCA mutation] or homologous recombination deficiency for synergistic effect. Without faulty DS-DNA repair such as in the setting of BRCA mutation, then PARPi is not effective in and of itself. Recall: 20% of TNBC have BRCA mutations. See Hall and Giaccia, p496, Figure 27.4 for more on PARPi and the concept of synthetic lethality. The [BrighTNess] trial showed that carboplatin and not veliparib (a PARPi) doubled pCR rate for triple negative breast cancer, defying the hypothesis it would respond well to both agents. However, this trial should be repeated requiring BRCA-mutations for enrollment. Investigation of PARPi in the metastatic setting learned from this by only enrolling patients with known BRCA mutations. Of note, the BrighTNess trial failed to demonstrate efficacy of PARPi in the TNBC population as a whole (it did not require BRCA mutation for enrollment, and only 15% of the population was BRCA mutants). Both the OlympiAD and EMBRACA trials demonstrated a DOUBLING in ORR with PARPi for metastatic TNBC. Both of these trials required BRCA mutations on enrollment.

heading: PARP inhibitors
full_text: See the summary box above. Instant.Oncology: [Metastatic Breast Cancer Chemo based on subtype] and [synthetic lethality]. OlympiAD [Robson NEJM '17]: Standard chemotherapy vs. Olaparib (PARPi)TBL QS: To grossly oversimplify (you're welcome), PARP repairs minor but frequent DNA damage. And if PARP doesn't fix things, the big guns (homologous recombination) typically pick up the slack. But, if homologous recombination also doesn't work (as in this case of a BRCA mutation), all those tiny little problems become big problems. Looks like BRCAmt+ breast cancer's got 99 problems...and PARP inhibition just became a big one. 302 metastatic pts. BRCA mutants with TNBC. Standard chemo: Single agent chemo such as capecitabine, eribulin, vinorelbine q3w. MPFS 4→ 7 mo (HR 0.58) ORR 29→ 60%. G3+ toxicity 50→ 37%. Toxicity leading to treatment discontinuation 8→ 5%. EMBRACA [Litton NEJM '18]: Phase III. Chemo of choice vs. Talazoparib (PARPi) + systemic agent.Big caveat: no platinum agent included. So, while PARP inhibition is definitely active in this population, we’ll probably be seeing it next in combination, sequence, or compared to a platinum. [Plenary Session 1.03]: Median survival is less than two years in both arms. These drugs cost a fortune! Are they worth it? TBL QS: Talazoparib plus non-platinum chemo is effective in patients with advanced BRCAmt breast cancer. Refractory or metastatic breast cancer and germline BRCA mutation. Stratified by HR(+) or HR (-). Combination: One of four systemic agents - capecitabine, gemcitabine, eribulin, vinorelbine. Only 18% crossed over to the control arm, so crossover cannot explain the lack of the OS benefit. ORR 27→ 62%. MPFS 6→ 9 mo (HR 0.54). full_text: Safety and Tolerability of Metastasis-Directed Radiation Therapy in the Era of Evolving Systemic, Immune, and Targeted Therapies [Guimond ARO '22]: As a precaution, until further data are available, for CDK4/6i (palbociclib - t1/2 29 hours, ribociclib or abemaciclib - t1/2 30-55 hours), consideration of suspending treatment 3 days before and after RT should be given. There was unanimous consensus that radiotherapy parameters and toxicity is mandatory when reporting safety data in both early and advanced settings, there are few or no high-quality clinical data concerning combination of RT and new systemic treatments for breast cancer, and potential risks, benefits and uncertainties regarding combination of RT and new systemic therapy should be fully discussed with the patient. heading: Cardiac Toxicity
full_text: Modern mean heart dose constraints Conventional fractionation: Mean heart dose < 4-5 Gy per RTOG 10-05. Hypofractionation: Mean heart dose < 3.2-4 Gy per RTOG 10-05. For non-smokers, the absolute risks of lung cancer and heart disease from modern radiation therapy were < 1%. But for long-term continuing smokers they were close to 5%, which may outweigh the benefit. Stopping smoking at the time of radiotherapy may avoid much of this risk." Compare this to data for hodgkin lymphoma survivors, which also demonstrated a 7.4% excess relative risk for each 1 Gy increase to mean heart dose. However, for the patients in the 40 year age range, this number was only 4% excess relative risk 2168 women who underwent RT between 1958-2001. 963 with major coronary events, 1205 controls. Major coronary events: MI, coronary revascularization, death from ICM. Majority of patients were treated prior to the 3D era. Mean dose to the whole heart 4.9 Gy. Rate of major coronary events increased by 7.4% for each 1 Gy increase to MHD, no apparent threshold. Risk started within the first 5y and continued into the third decade after RT. Differences were noted in shortness of breath, willingness to recommend treatment, and to choose treatment again, although this was an unblinded study. One could argue that IMRT photons should be option on control arm given IMN coverage mandated. 1,239 patients with non-metastatic breast cancer undergoing comprehensive nodal irradiation. Primary endpoint major CV events with sufficient power to detect clinically meaningful differences in HRQOL defined by effect size >0.33 in mixed-effects models assuming a correlation of ≥ 0.40. Median age 50y (mind-max 21-92). MRM (70%). 0-2 CV risk factors (81%). Left or bilateral cancer (62%). On the control arm, IMRT was delivered in 66% of patients! (n=384/582). Stratified by Age (± 65), CV risk (0-2 vs. ≥ 2 RF), surgery (BCS/MRM), laterality. No clinically meaningful differences in PROMIS fatigue total score, satisfaction with breast cosmetic outcomes, BREAST-Q total score, and FACT-B trial outcome index score. PRO-CTCAE severity shortness of breath for 0 vs. 1-4 favored protons (OR=0.74, 95CI 0.59-0.93), but there was no difference when categorized as 0-2 vs. 3-4. More than 10% of patients reported moderate, severe or very severe SOB. Ipsi lung V20 < 50% is quite lenient considering traditional metrics are V20 < 35-40%. It is not known how many patients received Ipsi lung V20 in the range of 35-50%. Other PRO-CTCAEs were similar between arms. FACIT in favor of protons included willingness to recommend treatment (OR=0.13, 95CI 0.8-0.22) and choose treatment again (OR 0.11, 95CI 0.07-0.18).

heading: Metastatic
full_text: Up-front capecitabine + neratinib for HER2+ disease appears to be the most reasonable option if planning to defer local therapy for brain mets with intracranial ORR ~50%  if lapatinib-naive [TBCRC 022], while ~30% if ≥ 2 prior HER2/neu therapies [NALA trial]. Finally, MPFS is only around 6 mo (similar to BRAF/MEKi for melanoma). For TNBC, intracranial response for immunotherapy remains unknown [IMpassion130]. See the [Omission of RT for breast brain mets] section for more. EAI142 [NCT02398773]: Phase II. 18F Fluoroestradiol PET as a predictive measure for endocrine therapy. HR+/HER2-. See [NRG-BR002]: Phase II/III. Standard of care and tx of symptomatic mets vs. LCT. See the [Constraints and Toxicity] section. De novo breast cancer, ≤ 4 lesions. May receive up to 12 mo of first line systemic tx without progression. Nonosseous sites: 30/1 (28-30.3): Only single liver and peripheral lung. 45/3 (42.5-45.5): Preferred for peripheral lung, liver, and abdominal pelvic mets. 50/5 (48-50.5): Preferred for central lung, mediastinal/cervical lymph nodes. Osseous sites: 20/1 (14-20.2): Spinal mets. 30/3 (27-30.3): Non-spinal mets. 35/5 (30-35.4): Thoracic/Cervical spine. EA1183 (FEATURE) [NCT04316117]: Utilizing PET/CT to measure response as binary predictor of PFS. HR+. Bone dominant or bone-only disease. NRG-BR004 [NCT03199885]: Phase III. THP ± Atezolizumab. Note: Omission of RT for asymptomatic HER2+ brain metastasis is [experimental]. 150 patients have been screened as of January 2021 (14% accrual; n=86/600). HER2+. First line. Asymptomatic brain mets (< 3 cm, up to 4 mets, steroids allowed, non-brain stem or OC/ON location, no LMD) may be enrolled. SRS or WBRT allowed 1 mo prior to randomization. Weekly paclitaxel 2 of 3 weeks. Docetaxel is now allowed. HP q3w until progression ± Atez q3w x2y or until progression. To assist with enrollment, allowed to administer loading doses of HP and first 3 weeks of chemo while awaiting confirmation of HER2+ status and determination of PD-L1 prior to randomization. OLIGOMA [Krug CTRO '21, NCT04495309]: Systemic therapy ± OligoSBRT. Patients with up to five mets are eligible, including patients with up to 3 brain mets (only in case of extracranial disease). Allows for locoregional recurrence as target lesion (compared to controlled primary in BR002). Control arm allows for palliative RT to symptomatic mets so long as at least 1 lesion remains untreated. Co-primary endpoints of PFS and QoL. See Table 2 for differences between OLIGOMA and BR002. SUBMIT [NCT01392586]: Systemic therapy ± (Upfront surgery ± PORT) Untreated patients of any T stage with resectable T4 status with distant metastases who were randomized to resection of the primary tumor followed by chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone. Terminated due to low accrual rate. Primary endpoint: Median survival. Goal 516 participants, but only enrolled 10 patients. PRIM-BC/JCOG 1017 [UMIN000005586]: Systemic therapy ± (Deferred Surgery ± PORT). Untreated patients with histologically confirmed breast cancer with one or more measurable metastatic lesions diagnosed by radiological examination. No brain metastasis allowed. Patients who completed primary systemic therapy according to ER and HER2 status for three cycles without disease progression are randomized to continue the same systemic therapy as additional therapy for as long as possible, or complete resection of the primary lesions. Prophylactic axillary lymph node dissection and/or resection of adjacent organs are not allowed. As long as the tumor is completely resected, it does not matter whether the surgical procedure is partial mastectomy or total mastectomy. Patients in the primary tumor resection arm will then receive the same systemic therapy as additional therapy for as long as possible. Primary endpoint: OS. Goal: 410 participants. Palbociclib in progressive brain metastases [NCT02896335]. Abemaciclib in participants with breast cancer, NSCLC or melanoma [NCT02308020].
